They praise (जरन्ते, 3rd-person plural) you (त्वाम्, accusative) with hymns (उक्थेभिः) — the तृतीया of means, the same "with/by" you met in नरैः and धिया. Two epithets describe them: सुतसोमाः ("Soma-pressed," a बहुव्रीहि) and अहर्विदः ("day-knowers"). All grammar you hold.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: वायो॒ तव॑ प्रपृंच॒ती धेना॑ जिगाति दा॒शुषे॑। उ॒रू॒ची सोम॑पीतये॥
readings.translation: O Vāyu, your nourishing stream goes to the worshipper, broad, for the Soma-drinking.
readings.teaches: a feminine subject (धेना "stream") + षष्ठी of possession (तव "your") + दाशुषे dative + a purpose-dative (सोमपीतये)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits प्र-पृञ्चती; प्र + पृच् "fill, mingle"

notes.en: present participle (feminine, शतृ + ई) qualifying धेना
recipient — to whom the stream goes

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → दाशुषे (the dative you met in hymn 1)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सोम-पीतये; सोम + पीति "drinking"

notes.en: purpose — "for the sake of" (the dative of purpose)

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → सोमपीतये (इ-stem dative, like स्वस्तये)

readings.vyakhya: तव धेना दाशुषे जिगाति। दाशुषे सोमपीतये च चतुर्थ्यौ — सम्प्रदाने तादर्थ्ये च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A feminine subject leads: धेना ("stream," an आ-stem feminine like विद्या), with two feminine adjectives agreeing — प्रपृञ्चती ("nourishing") and उरूची ("broad"). It is तव ("yours," genitive) and it जिगाति ("goes") दाशुषे ("to the worshipper," dative). The last word shows a second flavour of the dative: सोमपीतये — *for the purpose of* Soma-drinking. One case (चतुर्थी), two senses: "to whom" (दाशुषे) and "for what" (सोमपीतये).

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: इंद्र॑वायू इ॒मे सु॒ता उप॒ प्रयो॑भि॒रा ग॑तं। इंद॑वो वामु॒शंति॒ हि॥
readings.translation: O Indra and Vāyu, these pressed (Somas) are here — come with delights; the drops long for you both.
readings.teaches: the DUAL debuts — a dual deity (इन्द्रवायू), a dual imperative (आ गतम् "come, you two"), and वाम् "you two" (1.4.22)

notes.en: a dual द्वन्द्व compound — इन्द्र + वायु, two deities as one pair

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → the DUAL number (two → द्विवचन) → इन्द्रवायू

notes.en: demonstrative (इदम्), nom. plural agreeing with सुताः
subject — the offerings (past participle of सु "press", used as noun)

words.gloss: with delights, with offerings of joy

notes.text: padapāṭha splits प्रयः-भिः; प्रयस् "delight, dainty" (अस्-stem)

notes.en: imperative — but DUAL: "come, you two" (मध्यम द्विवचन)

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → dual ending → गतम् (addressed to the two gods)

notes.en: subject (second clause) — the bright drops (उ-stem nom. plural)
object — whom the drops long for

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → वाम् ("you two", the dual enclitic of युष्मद्)

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्रवायू इति द्वन्द्वः द्विवचने; आ गतम् इति द्विवचनलोट्; वाम् इति द्विवचनम्। द्वौ देवौ, द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The DUAL arrives — Sanskrit's third number, for exactly two. The pair इन्द्रवायू is a द्वन्द्व compound ("Indra and Vāyu") in the dual (द्विवचन, 1.4.22), and everything addressed to them is dual too: आ गतम् "come, *you two*" (a dual imperative), and वाम् "you two" (the dual of युष्मद्). Between, सुताः ("the pressed Somas") and इन्दवः ("the drops") are plural subjects. Singular, plural, and now dual — the वचन triad is complete, here in real Vedic.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: वाय॒विंद्र॑श्च चेतथः सु॒तानां॑ वाजिनीवसू। तावा या॑त॒मुप॑ द्र॒वत्॥
readings.translation: O Vāyu and Indra, you two take note of the pressed (Somas), O rich in plenty — come, you both, swiftly.
readings.teaches: a DUAL finite verb (चेतथः "you two perceive") + a dual epithet (वाजिनीवसू) + तौ "you two" — the dual reinforced

notes.en: vocative (here नॉम-form joined to वायो by च — "Vāyu and Indra")
genitive plural — that of which they take note

words.gloss: O you two rich in plenty

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वाजिनी-वसु; वाजिनी "abundance" + वसु "wealth"

notes.en: vocative DUAL epithet — addressing the pair
pronoun — the DUAL of तद् ("those two / you two")
imperative DUAL — "come, you two" (as आ गतम् in rd020)

readings.vyakhya: वायुः इन्द्रश्च — द्वौ; चेतथः यातम् इति द्विवचने तिङन्ते। सर्वं द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The dual you just met now drives the VERB. वायो and इन्द्रः, joined by च, are two — so चेतथः ("you two perceive") is a dual finite verb, तौ ("you two") is the dual pronoun, यातम् ("come, you two") the dual imperative, and वाजिनीवसू a dual vocative epithet. Everything addressed to the pair is dual. They take note सुतानाम् — "of the pressed Somas," a partitive genitive (षष्ठी). The whole verse is a drill in द्विवचन.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: वाय॒विंद्र॑श्च सुन्व॒त आ या॑त॒मुप॑ निष्कृ॒तं। म॒क्ष्वि१॒॑त्था धि॒या न॑रा॥
readings.translation: O Vāyu and Indra, come to the presser's prepared (offering), swiftly, even so, through thought, O strong ones.
readings.teaches: a goal-of-motion (निष्कृतं, what they come UP-to) + a genitive of the presser (सुन्वतः) + dual vocative नरा

notes.text: a present participle of सु "press", used as a noun

notes.en: genitive — "of the presser" (whose offering they approach)

words.gloss: the prepared place / the readied offering

notes.text: padapāṭha splits निः-कृत; निस् + कृत "made ready"

notes.en: goal of motion — "up to the readied (offering)"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → निष्कृतम् (the goal of गति takes द्वितीया)

notes.en: means — "by thought" (the धिया you met in rd014)

words.gloss: O you two men / strong ones

notes.text: नरा = नरौ — the dual of नर, your very first noun, now in the vocative dual

readings.vyakhya: सुन्वतः निष्कृतम् उप आ यातम् — गत्यर्थे द्वितीया। नरा इति द्विवचनसम्बोधनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The pair is called again — यातम्, "come, you two" — but now with a goal: उप … निष्कृतम्, "up to the prepared offering," where the goal of motion takes the accusative (द्वितीया, just as a destination does). सुन्वतः ("of the presser") is a genitive: whose offering it is. धिया ("by thought") is the instrumental of means you already hold. And the address नरा is नरौ — the DUAL of नर, the very first noun you ever declined, now standing in the vocative dual.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: मि॒त्रं हु॑वे पू॒तद॑क्षं॒ वरु॑णं च रि॒शाद॑सं। धियं॑ घृ॒ताचीं॒ साधं॑ता॥
readings.translation: I call Mitra of pure discernment and Varuṇa the foe-destroyer, who make perfect the lucid thought.
readings.teaches: a new deity-pair (Mitra & Varuṇa) as accusative objects + 1sg हुवे "I call" + a dual participle साधन्ता

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पूत-दक्ष; पूत "purified" + दक्ष "skill, discernment"

notes.en: possessive compound qualifying मित्रम् — "(he) whose दक्ष is pure"
object of साधन्ता — "(who perfect) the thought"

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) in the DUAL — "the two perfecting"

notes.en: apposed to मित्रम् + वरुणम् (the pair) — accusative dual

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → dual → साधन्ता (the two of them)

readings.vyakhya: मित्रं वरुणं च हुवे — द्वितीयायाम्। साधन्ता इति द्विवचनं कृदन्तम्, तयोः विशेषणम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new divine pair enters — Mitra and Varuṇa. Here they are OBJECTS: मित्रम् … वरुणम् च, accusatives, "I call (हुवे, 1st-person singular) Mitra and Varuṇa," each with its epithet (पूतदक्षम् "pure-skilled," रिशादसम् "foe-destroying"). They jointly perfect धियं घृताचीम् ("the luminous thought," accusative) — and साधन्ता, "the two who perfect," is a participle in the DUAL, agreeing with the pair. The dual now appears even on a participle.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.translation: By the Truth, O Mitra-Varuṇa, increasers of Truth, touchers of Truth — you two have won a vast will.
readings.teaches: a dual द्वन्द्व vocative (मित्रावरुणौ) + तृतीया-of-means (ऋतेन) + a PERFECT dual verb (आशाथे)

words.gloss: by the Truth, through cosmic order

notes.en: dual द्वन्द्व compound — Mitra + Varuṇa as one pair

words.gloss: O you two who increase the Truth

notes.text: padapāṭha splits ऋत-वृध्; ऋत "Truth" + वृध् "increasing"

words.gloss: you two who touch the Truth

notes.text: padapāṭha splits ऋत-स्पृश्; ऋत + स्पृश् "touching"

words.gloss: you two have attained, have won

notes.en: perfect — "have won" (the लिट् you met in चकार)

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → DUAL perfect → आशाथे ("you two have")

readings.vyakhya: ऋतेन इति करणम्; मित्रावरुणौ ऋतावृधौ ऋतस्पृशा — द्विवचनसम्बोधनानि; बृहन्तं क्रतुम् आशाथे — लिटि द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Now Mitra-Varuṇa are ADDRESSED, as a single dual द्वन्द्व: मित्रावरुणौ (vocative dual), with two dual epithets, ऋतावृधौ ("Truth-increasers") and ऋतस्पृशा ("Truth-touchers"). The line opens with ऋतेन — "by the Truth," the instrumental of means. And the verb is new: आशाथे, "you two have attained" — a PERFECT (लिट्, the tense of चकार) in the DUAL. Tense, number, and compound all converge on the pair.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; final verse of the Vāyu/Mitra-Varuṇa hymn. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: क॒वी नो॑ मि॒त्रावरु॑णा तुविजा॒ता उ॑रु॒क्षया॑। दक्षं॑ दधाते अ॒पसं॑॥
readings.translation: Two seers, Mitra and Varuṇa, of mighty birth, wide-dwelling — they hold for us a working skill.
readings.teaches: dual NOMINATIVE epithets (कवी, तुविजाता, उरुक्षया) + a present DUAL verb दधाते + the dative नः

notes.text: कवी = the DUAL of कवि — "two seers"

notes.en: dual द्वन्द्व — here NOMINATIVE (the agents), vs vocative in rd024

notes.text: padapāṭha splits तुवि-जात; तुवि "much, mighty" + जात "born"
padapāṭha splits उरु-क्षय; उरु "wide" + क्षय "dwelling"

words.gloss: the two hold, the two establish

notes.en: "hold, place" (the दा/धा you met in ददाति)

readings.vyakhya: कवी मित्रावरुणा तुविजाता उरुक्षया — द्विवचनप्रथमायाम्; नः दक्षम् अपसं दधाते — द्विवचनतिङन्तम्। हिमवत् सूक्तं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with the pair as SUBJECTS, all in the nominative dual: कवी ("two seers"), मित्रावरुणा (now agents, not addressed), तुविजाता ("mightily born"), उरुक्षया ("wide-dwelling"). They दधाते — "the two hold" — a present DUAL verb of √धा, the same root as ददाति "gives." For us (नः, dative) they hold दक्षम् अपसम् ("a working skill," accusative). You have now read the whole second hymn, and through it drilled the entire dual — noun, pronoun, adjective, participle, and verb across three tenses.

readings.sentence: अश्वि॑ना॒ यज्व॑री॒रिषो॒ द्रव॑त्पाणी॒ शुभ॑स्पती। पुरु॑भुजा चन॒स्यतं॑॥
readings.translation: O Aśvins, swift-handed lords of bliss, take pleasure in the worshipper's offerings, you of many bounties.
readings.teaches: a NEW dual pair (the Aśvins) in the vocative + an accusative-plural object इषः + the present dual imperative चनस्यतम् ("take pleasure, you two")

notes.text: अश्विना = the dual of अश्विन् — the two horsemen-gods, addressed as a pair

notes.en: object — what they are to enjoy

notes.text: padapāṭha splits द्रवत्-पाणी; द्रवत् "rushing" + पाणि "hand"
शुभः (gen.) + पती (dual of पति) — "lords of welfare/bliss"

words.gloss: O you of many enjoyments, much-bestowing

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पुरु-भुजा; पुरु "much" + भुज "enjoying, bestowing"

notes.en: "take delight in" (denominative) — here addressed to the pair
2nd person — DUAL imperative ("you two, take pleasure")

readings.vyakhya: अश्विना — सम्बोधने द्विवचनम्; यज्वरीः इषः — द्वितीयाबहुवचनं कर्मणि; द्रवत्पाणी शुभस्पती पुरुभुजा — सम्बोधनद्विवचनविशेषणानि; चनस्यतम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new dual pair: the अश्विन्s, the twin horsemen, addressed throughout in the dual vocative — अश्विना, द्रवत्पाणी ("swift-handed"), शुभस्पती ("lords of bliss"), पुरुभुजा ("of many bounties"). They are asked to चनस्यतम् — "take pleasure, you two" — a DUAL imperative (लोट्), the same dual-of-command you met as आ गतम् in rd020. What they enjoy is यज्वरीः इषः, "the worshipper's offerings," an accusative PLURAL object (कर्मन्). The dual you drilled across RV 1.2 now carries to a fresh pair.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; second ṛc of the Aśvins triplet. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: अश्वि॑ना॒ पुरु॑दंससा॒ नरा॒ शवी॑रया धि॒या। धिष्ण्या॒ वन॑तं॒ गिरः॑॥
readings.translation: O Aśvins of many deeds, O heroes, with your forceful thought, attentive ones, win our songs of praise.
readings.teaches: the instrumental धिया ("by thought," the करण met in rd014) + an accusative-plural object गिरः + नरा (= नरौ, the very first noun ever declined, now in a hymn)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पुरु-दंससा; पुरु "much" + दंसस् "deed, wondrous act"
नरा = नरौ, the DUAL of नर — the very first noun you declined, now vocative in the hymn

notes.en: instrument — "by means of thought" (the धिया you met in rd014)
object — what they are to win

readings.vyakhya: अश्विना नरा धिष्ण्या — सम्बोधनद्विवचनम्; शवीरया धिया — तृतीयैकवचनं करणे; गिरः — द्वितीयाबहुवचनं कर्मणि; वनतम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The Aśvins again, addressed as नरा — which is नरौ, the dual of नर, the first noun this whole reader ever declined, now standing in a Vedic hymn. They are to वनतम् ("win, you two," dual imperative) the गिरः, "songs of praise" (accusative plural object). The means is शवीरया धिया, "with forceful thought" — an INSTRUMENTAL (करण, तृतीया), the same धी "thought" you met as धिया in rd014. One verse braids three threads you already hold: the dual address, the accusative object, and the instrument of means.

source.ref: RV 1.3.3 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — closes the Aśvins triplet
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; third and last ṛc to the Aśvins. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: दस्रा॑ यु॒वाक॑वः सु॒ता नास॑त्या वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः। आ या॑तं रुद्रवर्तनी॥
readings.translation: O wondrous Nāsatyas, the pressed soma-draughts are yours, the sacred grass is strewn — come, O you whose path is Rudra's.
readings.teaches: a string of dual-nominative predicate words (युवाकवः, सुता, वृक्तबर्हिषः) + the familiar आ यातम् ("come, you two," dual imperative met in rd020)

notes.en: vocative dual — the Aśvins as "wondrous ones"

notes.text: युवाकु "directed toward you two" — derived from युवाम् (you two)

notes.en: predicate adjective of the soma — "yearning for you"

notes.text: सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press" — the pressed soma

notes.en: vocative dual — a name of the Aśvins

words.gloss: for whom the sacred grass is strewn

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वृक्त-बर्हिस्; वृक्त "twisted, strewn" + बर्हिस् "sacred grass"

notes.en: "go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — the same आ यातम् of rd020

words.gloss: O you whose path is Rudra's

notes.text: padapāṭha splits रुद्र-वर्तनी; रुद्र + वर्तनि "track, path"

readings.vyakhya: दस्रा नासत्या रुद्रवर्तनी — सम्बोधनद्विवचनम्; युवाकवः सुताः वृक्तबर्हिषः — प्रथमायां प्रत्ययनामानि; आ यातम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्। अश्विसूक्तं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The triplet to the Aśvins closes with a NOMINATIVE string describing the offering: युवाकवः सुताः वृक्तबर्हिषः — "the pressed (soma), yearning for you, with sacred grass strewn." These are predicates: the rite is ready. The pair, addressed as दस्रा ("wondrous"), नासत्या ("truthful"), रुद्रवर्तनी ("of Rudra's path"), are bidden आ यातम् — "come, you two" — the very dual imperative you first met as आ गतम् in rd020. The Aśvin hymn is complete.

source.ref: RV 1.3.4 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — opens the Indra triplet
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; fourth ṛc of RV 1.3, the hymn turns to Indra. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि चित्रभानो सु॒ता इ॒मे त्वा॒यवः॑। अण्वी॑भि॒स्तना॑ पू॒तासः॑॥
readings.translation: Come, O Indra of bright splendour — these pressed (soma-draughts) are longing for you, purified through the fine (filter), in continuous flow.
readings.teaches: the SINGULAR turn — after the dual Aśvins, Indra is addressed one-on-one: vocative इन्द्र + the 2nd-person SINGULAR imperative आ याहि ("come!") vs the dual आ यातम् of rd028

notes.en: vocative SINGULAR — one god now addressed, not a pair
singular (contrast the dual अश्विना of rd026)
"go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — same root as the dual आ यातम्
2nd person — SINGULAR imperative ("you, come"), vs dual यातम्

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चित्र-भानो; चित्र "bright" + भानु "radiance"
सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press"
त्वायु "yearning toward you" — built on त्वा (you, acc.)

notes.en: predicate adjective of सुताः — "(the draughts) longing for you"

notes.text: पूत = क्त-participle of पू "purify"; -आसः = Vedic nom. pl.

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र चित्रभानो — सम्बोधने एकवचनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम् (द्विवचनयातमः प्रतियोगि); सुताः इमे त्वायवः पूतासः — प्रथमाबहुवचने कर्तृविशेषणानि; अण्वीभिः तना — तृतीया करणे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn turns from the pair to a single god, and the grammar turns with it: इन्द्र is a SINGULAR vocative, and he is bidden आ याहि — "come!" — a 2nd-person SINGULAR imperative, exactly the dual आ यातम् of rd028 with one fewer. Hold the two side by side: यातम् = "come, you two," याहि = "come, you one." The soma is described in a nominative string (सुताः … त्वायवः … पूतासः, "pressed … longing for you … purified"), strained अण्वीभिः, "through the fine filter" (instrumental of means). The dual you drilled all through RV 1.2 now has its singular foil.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; fifth ṛc of RV 1.3. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि धि॒येषि॒तो विप्र॑जूतः सु॒ताव॑तः। उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि वा॒घतः॑॥
readings.translation: Come, O Indra, urged on by the thought, hastened by the seers — up to the prayers of the soma-pressing worshipper.
readings.teaches: the same singular आ याहि again + the preverb उप governing an accusative goal (ब्रह्माणि "the prayers") + the instrumental of agent (धिया "by the thought")

notes.en: instrument — "urged BY the thought" (the धी met in rd027)

notes.text: इषित = क्त-participle of इष् "impel" — "(you,) urged on"
padapāṭha splits विप्र-जूतः; विप्र "inspired seer" + जूत "sped, urged"

words.gloss: of the soma-presser, of him who has pressed (soma)

notes.text: सुतावत् = सुत "pressed soma" + मतुप् (वत्) "possessing"

notes.en: preverb — "toward," directing the motion to ब्रह्माणि
goal of motion — "(come) up to the prayers"

words.gloss: of the worshipper, of the reciter

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; धिया — तृतीया करणे; इषितः विप्रजूतः — क्तान्तविशेषणे; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया कर्मणि गत्यर्थे; सुतावतः वाघतः — षष्ठी सम्बन्धे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same call — आ याहि, "come" — but now Indra is moved BY something and moves TO something. He is धिया इषितः, "urged on by the thought" (instrumental of means, the धी you met as धिया in rd027), and विप्रजूतः, "hastened by the seers." Where to? उप ब्रह्माणि वाघतः — "up to the prayers of the worshipper," where उप is a preverb steering the verb of motion onto an accusative goal (ब्रह्माणि), and वाघतः is a genitive ("of the worshipper"). Means in the instrumental, goal in the accusative, possession in the genitive — three cases you hold, in one line of the Veda.

source.ref: RV 1.3.6 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — closes the Indra triplet
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; sixth ṛc of RV 1.3, last to Indra. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि॒ तूतु॑जान॒ उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि हरिवः। सु॒ते द॑धिष्व न॒श्चनः॑॥
readings.translation: Come, O Indra, hastening, up to the prayers, O lord of the bay steeds; at the pressing take delight in us.
readings.teaches: a LOCATIVE of occasion (सुते "at the pressing," when the soma is pressed) + a middle imperative दधिष्व ("take, for yourself") + the dative नः

notes.en: 2nd person — singular imperative (third time in the triplet)

notes.text: तूतुजान = perfect middle participle of तुज् "speed" — "(you,) hastening"

notes.en: preverb directing motion to ब्रह्माणि (as in rd030)
goal of motion — "(come) up to the prayers"

words.gloss: O lord of the bay steeds

notes.text: हरिवत् = हरि "bay horse" + मतुप् (वत्) "possessing"; here vocative हरिवः

words.gloss: at the pressing, when (the soma) is pressed

notes.text: सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press," here LOCATIVE — "at the pressed (soma)"

notes.en: "hold, place, take" — the same √धा of दधाते (rd025), here MIDDLE imperative
2nd person — singular MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative "take for yourself"
for us / in us — the enclitic नः
object — "take delight" (the चन- of चनस्यतम्, rd026, now as a noun)

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र हरिवः — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया गत्यर्थे; सुते — सप्तमी अधिकरणे; दधिष्व — लोटि आत्मनेपदम्; नः चनः — आत्मने ग्रहणम्। इन्द्रसूक्तत्रयं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The third and last call to Indra adds one new case: सुते, a LOCATIVE — "at the pressing," the occasion when the soma is pressed (अधिकरण, सप्तमी, by 2.3.36). The verb दधिष्व is √धा again — the root of दधाते "the two hold" in rd025 — but here a MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative, "take FOR YOURSELF," carrying delight (चनः, the noun of the very चनस्यतम् "take pleasure" that opened the hymn in rd026). The triplet to Indra is complete: three times "come," each adding a case — instrument, goal, and now occasion.

chapters.title: कृदन्त — primary derivation: participles, infinitive, gerund, action-nouns

readings.translation: The man (who has) gone to the village.
readings.teaches: क्त — the past participle (निष्ठा); a root made into an adjective

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → ग्रामम् (→ ग्रामं before ग)

notes.en: a कृत्-formed word — a participle built from a root

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त (and क्तवतु) after a root for past sense → गम् + त → गतः

readings.vyakhya: भूते निष्ठा — क्तप्रत्ययः। गम् + क्त → गतः। धातुः विशेषणं जातम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The first कृदन्त: the past participle. The निष्ठा affixes — क्त and क्तवतु (3.2.102) — attach to a root to give a past adjective. गम् + क्त → गतः "gone." It then declines like any अ-stem and agrees with its noun: ग्रामं गतः नरः "the man gone to the village." A root has become an adjective — this is what कृत् affixes do, and the whole chapter is their varieties.

readings.translation: The rice was made by the man.
readings.teaches: क्त as a PASSIVE past participle — agent in तृतीया (the कर्मणि construction)

notes.en: agent — but in the passive, expressed by तृतीया

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → the agent of a passive takes तृतीया → नरेण (with णत्व, 8.4.1)

notes.en: the object — but the grammatical subject of the passive participle
agrees with ओदनः (the patient), not the agent

readings.vyakhya: क्तप्रत्ययः कर्मणि — कर्ता तृतीयायाम्, कर्म प्रथमायाम्। नरेण ओदनः कृतः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The क्त participle is usually PASSIVE: it agrees with the patient, and the agent stands in the instrumental (2.3.18) — exactly the कर्मणि (passive) construction. नरेण ओदनः कृतः = "by the man the rice (was) made." This is the everyday Sanskrit past: not a finite verb but a participle + agent-in-तृतीया. (Note रामेण-style णत्व in नरेण.)

readings.translation: The man, (while) going, sees.
readings.teaches: शतृ — the present active participle (replaces लट्)

notes.en: the शतृ affix — present active participle, replacing लट्

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ → शतृ/शानच् replace लट् for a participle → गच्छत् → गच्छन्
तौ सत् → these two are termed सत् (the "present-participle" साधन)
उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थाने → the त-stem inserts नुम् before strong endings → गच्छन्

readings.vyakhya: लटः स्थाने शतृ — वर्तमाने कर्तरि। गच्छत् → गच्छन् नुमा। "गच्छन् पश्यति" = गच्छन् सन् पश्यति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The present participle: शतृ (active) replaces the present लट् (3.2.124) when the form is a participle agreeing with the agent — गम् → गच्छत्, which surfaces as गच्छन् (नुम्-insertion before strong endings, 7.1.70). "गच्छन् नरः पश्यति" = "the man, going, sees" = "while he goes, he sees." It is a त्-stem consonant participle, declining राजन्-style (strong/weak). The middle counterpart is शानच् (यजमानः "sacrificing").

readings.translation: The man wishes to go to the village.
readings.teaches: तुमुन् — the infinitive ("to do"), for a purposed action

notes.en: the तुमुन् affix — "to ___", an indeclinable verbal goal

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् → तुमुन् for the purposed action → गम् + तुम् → गन्तुम्

readings.vyakhya: क्रियार्थायां क्रियायां तुमुन् — गन्तुम्। अव्ययम्, इच्छाद्यपेक्षम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The infinitive is तुमुन् (3.3.10): "to go" = गन्तुम्, "to do" = कर्तुम्, "to see" = द्रष्टुम्. It names the action one *aims at* — so it pairs with verbs of wishing, being able, beginning: गन्तुम् इच्छति "wishes to go," गन्तुं शक्नोति "can go." Unlike क्त and शतृ, तुमुन् is indeclinable (an अव्यय) — it never changes form.

readings.translation: Having gone to the village, the man eats rice.
readings.teaches: क्त्वा — the gerund: the EARLIER of two acts by one agent

notes.en: the क्त्वा affix — the prior action, same agent

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले → क्त्वा after the verb of the EARLIER act, one shared agent → गत्वा
क्त्वातोसुन्कसुनः → a क्त्वा-form is an अव्यय (indeclinable)

readings.vyakhya: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा — गत्वा खादति = गत्वा पश्चात् खादति। एकः कर्ता, द्वे क्रिये।
readings.vyakhya_en: The gerund (क्त्वा, the "absolutive") chains two acts of ONE agent, marking the EARLIER (3.4.21): गत्वा … खादति = "having gone … (he) eats." First go, then eat — one man, two actions, the क्त्वा-form taking the first. It is indeclinable (1.1.40). When a prefix is present it becomes ल्यप् instead (आगत्य "having come"), but the meaning — "having ___, then ___" — is the same. This is how Sanskrit strings narrative: a row of gerunds ending in one finite verb.

readings.translation: Going is better. / The going is preferable.
readings.teaches: ल्युट् — the action-noun ("the ___ing"), a कृत् abstract

words.gloss: the going, the act of going

notes.en: the ल्युट् affix (→ अन) — names the action

notes.role: ल्युट् च → ल्युट् after a root for the action's name → गम् + अन → गमनम्

readings.vyakhya: भावे ल्युट् — गमनम्। क्रियायाः नाम नपुंसकम्। घञापि भावः (यथा "यागः")।
readings.vyakhya_en: Beyond participles, कृत् affixes also build action-NOUNS — "the going," "the doing." ल्युट् (→ अन, 3.3.115) gives गमनम् "going," दर्शनम् "seeing," a neuter अ-stem that declines like फल. The affix घञ् does the same with a different shape and grade (यज् → यागः "sacrifice," 3.3.18 भावे). So one root yields a whole family: गतः (gone), गच्छन् (going), गन्तुम् (to go), गत्वा (having gone), गमनम् (the going) — the कृदन्त system entire.

chapters.title: तद्धित — secondary nominal derivation (selected, learner-facing only)

readings.translation: The descendant of Daśaratha is "Dāśarathi" (= Rāma).
readings.teaches: अपत्य — the patronymic; इञ् after an अ-stem, with आदिवृद्धि

notes.en: genitive — the विग्रह "of ___" that the affix replaces

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → दशरथस्य (the analysis; the तद्धित condenses it)

notes.en: the SENSE the affix carries — "descendant of"
a secondary derivative — noun made from a noun

notes.role: तस्यापत्यम् → in the sense "descendant of ___", a तद्धित affix
अत इञ् → after an अ-stem the affix is इञ् → दशरथ + इ → दाशरथि (आदिवृद्धि अ→आ)

readings.vyakhya: तस्य अपत्यम् इति अर्थे इञ्; आदेर्वृद्धिः। दशरथ → दाशरथिः।
readings.vyakhya_en: A तद्धित attaches to a *finished* word and makes a new one. The patronymic: "descendant of X" (4.1.92) becomes a single word by adding इञ् after an अ-stem (4.1.95), with vṛddhi of the first vowel — दशरथ → दाशरथिः "son of Daśaratha." The genitive phrase दशरथस्य अपत्यम् collapses into one derived noun. (Other bases take अण् → गार्ग्यः, यञ् → for गोत्र lines.)

readings.translation: One born/found in Mathurā is "Māthura."
readings.teaches: तत्र भवः — "born in / belonging to a place", with आदिवृद्धि

notes.en: locus — the सप्तमी base of the derivation

notes.role: तत्र भवः → "being in (that place)" → an affix after the locative base → माथुरः (आदिवृद्धि)

readings.vyakhya: तत्र भवः इति अर्थे अण्; मथुरा → माथुरः। देशकालादेः भवार्थः।
readings.vyakhya_en: "Born in / found in / belonging to a place" — तत्र भवः (4.3.53) — turns a locative phrase into one adjective: मथुरायां भवः → माथुरः "of Mathurā," with vṛddhi (मथुरा → माथुर). The same family gives "relating to X" (तस्येदम्, 4.3.120) and "good for X" (तस्मै हितम्, 5.1.5). These locative/genitive/dative taddhitas are how Sanskrit forms its everyday relational adjectives.

readings.translation: He who has wealth is "wealthy" (dhanavān).
readings.teaches: मतुप् — the possessive "having ___"

notes.en: "be" — the विग्रह "X is his / in him"

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् → मतुप् "it is his / in him" → धन + मतुप् → धनवत् → धनवान्
उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थाने → the मतुप् (वत्) stem inserts नुम् before strong endings → धनवान्

readings.vyakhya: तत् अस्य अस्ति इति मतुप् — मत्वर्थः। धन + मतुप् → धनवान् (बुद्धिमान् वत्)।
readings.vyakhya_en: The possessive: "having X / in whom X is" — मतुप् (5.2.94). धन + मतुप् → धनवान् "wealthy," बुद्धि + मतुप् → बुद्धिमान् "wise" (the affix shows as -वत्/-मत्, declining राजन्-style with नुम्). You met गुणवान् and वीरवत्तमं in real text; this is the rule behind them — the workhorse that turns any noun into "the one who has it."

readings.translation: This one is cleverer than that.
readings.teaches: तरप् — the comparative ("more ___ than")

notes.role: पञ्चमी विभक्ते → the term compared-from takes पञ्चमी → ततः
द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ → तरप् (तर)/ईयसुन् for comparison of two → पटु + तर → पटुतरः

readings.vyakhya: द्वयोः विभजने तरप्; पञ्चमी विभक्ते। पटु → पटुतरः, अन्यस्मात्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Comparing TWO: तरप् → -तर (5.3.57), "more X (than the other)" — पटु → पटुतरः "cleverer." The thing surpassed stands in the ablative (पञ्चमी, 2.3.42): ततः पटुतरः "cleverer than that." The matching ईयस् (-ीयस्) is the irregular comparative (श्रेयस्, the श्रेयः you met). For surpassing ALL — the superlative — it is तमप्/इष्ठन् (5.3.55): पटुतमः "cleverest" (you saw रत्नधातमम्, वीरवत्तमम्).

readings.translation: The state of being heavy/a-teacher is "gurutva" (heaviness / gravity).
readings.teaches: त्व/तल् — the abstract noun ("-ness, the state of")

words.gloss: of the heavy one / of the teacher

notes.en: genitive — the base whose "-ness" is named

words.gloss: heaviness, gravity; the state of being a guru

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ → त्व (and तल् → ता) for "the state of ___" → गुरु + त्व → गुरुत्वम्

readings.vyakhya: तस्य भावः इति त्व-तलौ। गुरुत्वम् (नपुंसकम्), गुरुता (स्त्री)। भाववाचकम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The abstract: "the state of being X" — त्व and तल् (5.1.119). गुरु → गुरुत्वम् "heaviness/gurutva" (neuter, with -त्व) or गुरुता "guru-hood" (feminine, with -ता). देव → देवत्वम्/देवता. This is Sanskrit's "-ness / -hood": take any noun or adjective, add त्व or ता, and you have named its quality as a thing. Patronymic, place-adjective, possessive, comparative, abstract — the तद्धित system's productive core.

readings.translation: Among all the clever, this one is the cleverest.
readings.teaches: तमप् — the superlative ("most ___ of all"); निर्धारण in सप्तमी

notes.role: यतश्च निर्धारणम् → the group one is singled out from → सप्तमी (or षष्ठी) → सर्वेषु

notes.en: the class — locative plural, parallel to सर्वेषु

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ → तमप् (तम)/इष्ठन् for surpassing all → पटु + तम → पटुतमः

readings.vyakhya: अतिशायने तमप्; निर्धारणे सप्तमी। सर्वेषु पटुषु पटुतमः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The superlative completes the pair: तमप् → -तम (5.3.55), "most X of all" — पटु → पटुतमः "the cleverest." The group one is singled out FROM takes निर्धारण-सप्तमी (2.3.41): सर्वेषु पटुषु "among all the clever." So तर/तम are the degree-affixes — पटुतरः "cleverer (of two)," पटुतमः "cleverest (of all)" — closing the productive तद्धित set the reader needs.

chapters.title: कथा — graded retellings of extant stories (bāla-Kṛṣṇa, Pañcatantra…)

source.curated: our simple Sanskrit telling the well-known episode; NOT the verbatim text

readings.sentence: गोकुले कृष्णः नाम बालः वसति। यशोदा तस्य माता। सः गोपानां गृहेषु क्रीडति। सर्वे गोपाः तं बालं पश्यन्ति, सर्वाः गोप्यः च तं कामयन्ते।
readings.translation: In Gokula lives a boy named Kṛṣṇa. Yaśodā is his mother. He plays in the houses of the cowherds. All the cowherds see the boy, and all the cowherd-women love him.
readings.teaches: first STORY reading — connected prose reusing known grammar (loc., gen.pl, सः/तम्, present pl.); introduces the cast

notes.en: locus — where the story is set

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → सप्तमी for the locus → गोकुले

notes.en: agent — our hero (an a-stem masc., declined like देव)
"by name" — in apposition (कृष्णः नाम बालः = a boy named Kṛṣṇa)
locative plural (neuter a-stem → एषु, as देवेषु)
agent (ī-stem fem. nom. plural, as नद्यः)

readings.vyakhya: कथायाः आरम्भः। गोकुलम् अधिकरणम्, कृष्णः कर्ता, यशोदा माता। ज्ञातमेव व्याकरणम् — केवलं कथा नूतना।
readings.vyakhya_en: Your first connected story — and almost every form is grammar you already hold: a locative setting (गोकुले), genitive plurals (गोपानाम्), the सः/तस्य/तं pronoun, present verbs singular and plural. Nothing new to learn — that is the point. Meet the cast: कृष्णः the boy, यशोदा his mother, the गोपाः (cowherds) and गोप्यः (gopīs). They return in every episode, so their forms grow familiar. From here the sentences lengthen.

source.curated: our graded prose telling the famous butter-theft; not the verbatim text

readings.sentence: यशोदा गृहे नवनीतम् रक्षति। किन्तु कृष्णः नवनीतम् इच्छति। सः शनैः गृहम् प्रविशति, उच्चैः च नवनीतम् चोरयति। ततः सः मित्रेभ्यः तत् नवनीतम् यच्छति, स्वयम् च खादति। यशोदा तं पश्यति, क्रुध्यति च।
readings.translation: Yaśodā keeps butter in the house. But Kṛṣṇa wants the butter. He quietly enters the house and steals the butter from up high. Then he gives that butter to his friends and eats it himself. Yaśodā sees him and grows angry.
readings.teaches: a real SCENE — adversative किन्तु/ततः, adverbs (शनैः, उच्चैः, स्वयम्), सम्प्रदान (मित्रेभ्यः), clauses joined

notes.en: object — the prize of the whole episode (neuter a-stem)
adverb — "aloft" (the butter hung high; Kṛṣṇa reaches it)
recipients — to whom he gives the butter

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → मित्रेभ्यः (dat. pl., as देवेभ्यः)

readings.vyakhya: दृश्यं विस्तृतम् — किन्तु, ततः, च इति योजकैः वाक्यानि सम्बद्धानि। नवनीतम् कर्म, मित्रेभ्यः सम्प्रदानम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Now a whole scene, not a single fact. Sentences link by connectives — किन्तु ("but," turning Yaśodā's guarding into Kṛṣṇa's wanting), ततः ("then"), च ("and") — so the action flows. The new pieces are small and natural: adverbs (शनैः "quietly," उच्चैः "high up," स्वयम् "himself") and a chain of present verbs (इच्छति, प्रविशति, चोरयति, यच्छति, खादति). The case-roles are all known — नवनीतम् the object, मित्रेभ्यः the dative of recipient. You are reading a story now.

source.curated: our graded prose telling the दामोदर binding; not the verbatim text

readings.sentence: क्रुद्धा यशोदा रज्ज्वा कृष्णम् बध्नाति। किन्तु रज्जुः सर्वदा ह्रस्वा भवति। सा पुनः पुनः यतते, तथापि बालम् बन्धितुम् न शक्नोति। अन्ते कृष्णः स्वयम् एव मातुः प्रेम्णा बद्धः। तेन सः दामोदरः इति प्रसिद्धः।
readings.translation: Angry Yaśodā binds Kṛṣṇa with a rope. But the rope is always too short. She tries again and again, yet cannot bind the boy. In the end Kṛṣṇa is bound only by his mother's love, of his own accord. By this he became famous as "Dāmodara" (bound-at-the-belly).
readings.teaches: longest yet — past participles (क्रुद्धा, बद्धः), an infinitive (बन्धितुम्) with शक्, तृतीया of means (रज्ज्वा, प्रेम्णा), closing name-etymology

notes.en: past participle (क्त) of क्रुध्, feminine, agreeing with यशोदा
instrument — that with which she binds
means — that by which he is bound (न-stem प्रेमन् instr.)
past participle (क्त) of बन्ध् — the predicate "is bound"

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त → बद्ध; passive past participle as predicate

notes.en: possessive compound — दाम (rope) + उदर (belly) → "(he) at whose belly is the rope"

readings.vyakhya: कथा दीर्घतरा। क्रुद्धा बद्धः इति निष्ठे, बन्धितुम् इति तुमुन्, रज्ज्वा प्रेम्णा इति करणे। अन्ते नामनिर्वचनम् — दाम उदरे यस्य सः दामोदरः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The longest reading yet, weaving together what you met as isolated cells: past participles as adjective and predicate (क्रुद्धा "angry," बद्धः "bound"), an infinitive with "can" (बन्धितुम् न शक्नोति "cannot bind"), and the instrumental of means twice (रज्ज्वा "with a rope," प्रेम्णा "by love"). It closes the way Sanskrit tales love to — a name-etymology: दाम (rope) + उदर (belly) makes the बहुव्रीहि दामोदर, "the one with a rope at his belly." The grammar is familiar; the story now carries it.

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

readings.sentence: पूतना राक्षसी गोकुलं आगत्य शिशुरूपेण तिष्ठति। सा कृष्णं स्तनयित्वा विषेण हन्तुम् इच्छति। किन्तु कृष्णेन सः स्तनः पीतः, विषं च पीतम्। एवम् पूतना कृष्णेन हता।
readings.translation: The demoness Pūtanā comes to Gokula and stands there in the form of a child (i.e. a woman). She wishes to kill Kṛṣṇa by nursing him with poison. But by Kṛṣṇa the breast was suckled, and the poison too was drunk. Thus Pūtanā was slain by Kṛṣṇa.
readings.teaches: passive construction (कर्मणि क्त — पीतः, हता, with instrumental of agent); gerund आगत्य (prior action); accusative object (कृष्णम्, विषम्)

notes.en: goal of motion — where she comes to
gerund (क्त्वा after prefix → ल्यप्) — prior action of same agent

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → ल्यप् (prefix + root → आगत्य)

words.gloss: in the form of a child

notes.en: instrumental of manner — "in the guise of"
gerund (क्त्वा) — prior action: she nurses, then wishes to kill
patient in passive — what was suckled

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त; passive sense — कर्मणि क्त
भावकर्मणोः — passive ल-affixes become आत्मनेपद; क्त signals the same कर्मणि sense

notes.en: past passive participle (क्त) of √पा — neuter agreeing with विषम्
past passive participle (क्त) of √हन्, fem. agreeing with पूतना

readings.vyakhya: कर्मणिप्रयोगः — इह कर्ता तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्। कृष्णेन पूतना हता इति न कर्तरि, कर्मणि। दोषाः — आगत्य स्तनयित्वा इति पूर्वकालकृदन्ते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The grammar turn: for the first time the story is told in the **passive** (कर्मणि). In active voice Kṛṣṇa is the subject (कर्तृ) and takes the nominative; in passive he becomes the agent (still the doer, but now marked by तृतीया — instrumental — while the object rises to nominative). The past-passive participle क्त (निष्ठा, 3.2.102) carries this sense: पीतः (was drunk, masc.), पीतम् (neuter), हता (fem.). Two gerunds (क्त्वा / ल्यप्) chain the prior actions: Pūtanā "comes, then nurses, then wishes to kill" — each gerund hands off to the next.

source.ref: Bhāgavata 10.8 — the मृत्तिकाभक्षण and mouth-universe episode
source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

readings.sentence: एकदा कृष्णः मृत्तिकाम् अभक्षयत् इति बालाः यशोदां अवदन्। यशोदा पुत्रं पप्रच्छ — "किम् त्वं मृत्तिकाम् अखादः?" कृष्णः उवाच — "न अखादम्।" तदा यशोदा मुखं विवृणुष्व इति उक्त्वा दृष्टवती। तस्मिन् मुखे सा सर्वम् जगत् अपश्यत् — खम्, भूमिम्, देवान्, नक्षत्राणि च।
readings.translation: Once the children told Yaśodā that Kṛṣṇa had eaten mud. Yaśodā asked her son — "Did you eat mud?" Kṛṣṇa said — "I did not eat." Then Yaśodā said "open your mouth" and looked. In that mouth she saw all the world — sky, earth, gods, and stars.
readings.teaches: लिट् perfect (पप्रच्छ, उवाच), लङ् past (अभक्षयत्, अखादः, अखादम्, अपश्यत्), direct speech with इति, relative-demonstrative यस्मिन् / तस्मिन्, accusative-list object

notes.en: quotative — closes reported speech ("that he had eaten")
person told — indirect object of telling
interrogative pronoun — here a question marker
temporal adverb correlating with the question

notes.role: लोट् च — command takes लोट् → विवृणुष्व (2sg āt. लोट्)

notes.en: gerund (क्त्वा) — prior action of same agent

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — सर्व is a pronoun-class word
अनद्यतने लङ् → अपश्यत् (3sg लङ्, root √दृश् → √पश् in लङ्)

notes.en: item seen — in the list of what the cosmos contains

readings.vyakhya: इह कालभेदः स्पष्टः — बालाः अवदन्, यशोदा पप्रच्छ, कृष्णः उवाच इति लिट् परोक्षे; परन्तु स्मृत्या न परोक्षं — नाटकीयतया लिट् उचितः। लङ् तु अनद्यतने — अभक्षयत्, अखादः, अखादम्, अपश्यत् इति। लोट् विवृणुष्व इति विधौ।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two tenses meet in this reading. **लिट् perfect** (परोक्षे लिट्, 3.2.115) appears where the narrator stands at a remove — पप्रच्छ "she asked," उवाच "he said" — verbs of reported or narrated speech. **लङ्** (अनद्यतन, 3.2.111) marks the events directly recalled: the eating (अभक्षयत्), Kṛṣṇa's denial (न अखादम्), and Yaśodā's vision (अपश्यत्). One **लोट् imperative** (3.3.162) lives inside the quoted command — विवृणुष्व "open (your mouth)!" The vision that follows — sky, earth, gods, stars — is the whole universe listed in a single accusative string, with one past-active participle (दृष्टवती, क्तवतु fem.) as the main predicate: "she who saw."

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

readings.sentence: कालियो नाम महासर्पः कालिन्दीनद्यां वसति स्म। तस्य विषेण जलं दूषितम् आसीत्। गावः पिबन्त्यः तत् जलम् पीत्वा मूर्च्छिताः अभवन्। तदा कृष्णः तरुम् आरुह्य नद्यां अपतत्। सः सर्पस्य फणेषु नृत्यन् तम् अदमयत्। एवम् कालियः कृष्णेन पराजितः।
readings.translation: A great serpent named Kāliya lived in the Yamunā river. By his poison the water was polluted. The cows, while drinking, drank that water and fainted. Then Kṛṣṇa climbed a tree and fell into the river. He danced on the serpent's hoods and subdued it. Thus Kāliya was defeated by Kṛṣṇa.
readings.teaches: लिट्-style past (वसति स्म as past habitual); passive क्त with आसीत् (past passive predicate); gerund आरुह्य + अपतत्; present participle (शतृ) पिबन्त्यः, नृत्यन् (action simultaneous with main verb); passive अदमयत् → पराजितः

notes.en: particle — with लट् makes past habitual ("used to dwell")
instrument / cause — the poison is what polluted the water
present participle (शतृ, fem. pl.) — simultaneous action "while drinking"

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ suffix on a present root → पिबन्त् (masc.), पिबन्ती (fem.)

notes.en: pronoun (तद्, neut. acc.) — refers to जलम्
object of आरुह्य — what he climbed
gerund (ल्यप् — क्त्वा after prefix आ-) — prior action

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → ल्यप् (with prefix → आरुह्य)

notes.en: locative goal (direction into which he fell)
present participle (शतृ, masc. nom. sg.) — simultaneous with main verb
past passive participle (क्त) of परा-जि — "was defeated"

readings.vyakhya: द्वे नवीने — शतृप्रत्ययः (लटः शतृशानचौ) पिबन्त्यः नृत्यन् च; स्म-सहितः लट् भूतार्थे। कर्मणिप्रयोगः त्रिवारम् — दूषितम् आसीत्, मूर्च्छिताः अभवन्, पराजितः। जलचरे युद्धम् वर्णयितुम् क्त्वा-ल्यपौ बहुशः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two new tools. First, **शतृ** (the active present participle — लटः शतृशानचौ, 3.2.124): पिबन्त्यः "while drinking" (fem. pl., simultaneous with अभवन्) and नृत्यन् "while dancing" (masc. sg., simultaneous with अदमयत्). The participle says the background action runs alongside the main verb — not before it (that's क्त्वा) and not after it. Second, **वसति स्म** — a present-tense verb with the particle स्म shifts into past habitual: "used to dwell." Passive क्त appears three times (दूषितम्, मूर्च्छिताः, पराजितः), anchoring the pattern from ex098. The gerunds आरुह्य → अपतत् chain the action sequence into one breath.

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

readings.sentence: एकदा व्रजवासिनः इन्द्राय पूजाम् अकुर्वन्। कृष्णः अवदत् — "गोवर्धनाय पूजाम् कुरुत, न तु इन्द्राय।" जनाः तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तथा अकुर्वन्। तदा क्रुद्धः इन्द्रः मेघैः वर्षम् अप्रेरयत्। वर्षेण भयभीताः गावः च गोपाः च कृष्णम् अशरणम् अगच्छन्। कृष्णः तु गोवर्धनम् एव एकेन हस्तेन उद्धृत्य सप्त दिवसान् अधारयत्। एवम् गोवर्धनः कृष्णेन छत्रम् इव धृतः।
readings.translation: Once the inhabitants of Vraja were performing a puja for Indra. Kṛṣṇa said — "Offer puja to Govardhana, not to Indra." The people, having heard his words, did so. Then angry Indra sent rain-clouds. Frightened by the rain, the cows and cowherds went to Kṛṣṇa as their refuge. But Kṛṣṇa alone, lifting Govardhana with one hand, held it for seven days. Thus Govardhana was held by Kṛṣṇa like an umbrella.
readings.teaches: anīyar gerundive (implicitly: "the mountain is to-be-held"); upasarga + gerund उद्धृत्य; instrumental of cause (वर्षेण); accusative of duration (सप्त दिवसान्); simile (उपमा with इव); passive close (धृतः)

notes.role: लोट् च — command takes लोट् → कुरुत (2pl लोट्)

notes.en: object of श्रुत्वा — what they heard
past participle (क्त) of क्रुध् — attributive adjective
instrument — the clouds are the means of sending rain
cause of the fear — instrumental of cause
attribute of कृष्णम् — "(he who is) the refuge"
gerund (ल्यप् — क्त्वा after prefix उद्-) — prior action

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → ल्यप् (with prefix → उद्धृत्य)
अत्यन्तसंयोगे च — duration (unbroken extent) takes द्वितीया

readings.vyakhya: सर्वाधिकदीर्घा कथा — एका वाक्यपरम्परा। नवीनम् — उपमा (इव); अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया (सप्त दिवसान्); एकेन हस्तेन इति करणम्; क्रुद्धः इन्द्रः इति निष्ठाविशेषणम्। लोट् कुरुत इति विधौ; लङ् बहुशः कथावर्णने।
readings.vyakhya_en: The longest katha reading, and it earns its length: five separate clauses, each moving the story. New arrivals: **इव** (the simile particle — Govardhana held "like an umbrella," छत्रम् इव); **accusative of duration** — सप्त दिवसान् "for seven days" (अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया, 2.3.5); the **instrumental of instrument with body-part** — एकेन हस्तेन "with one hand" (2.3.18); and the **dual coordinator** गावः च गोपाः च "both cows and cowherds." The closing passive (धृतः, 3.2.102) rounds the arc: episodes ex098–ex101 all end with a कर्मणि क्त — "was killed," "she saw," "was defeated," "was held" — each one a summary judgment on what just happened.

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

readings.sentence: कंसः नाम क्रूरः राजा कृष्णस्य मातुलः आसीत्। सः अचिन्तयत् — "अयम् बालः मया हन्तव्यः, अन्यथा सः माम् हनिष्यति।" तस्मात् सः अक्रूरम् गोकुलम् प्रैषयत्। अक्रूरः रथेन गत्वा कृष्णम् अवदत् — "मथुराम् आगच्छ, यतः तव दर्शनम् सर्वे इच्छन्ति।"
readings.translation: A cruel king named Kaṃsa was Kṛṣṇa's maternal uncle. He thought — "This boy must be killed by me, otherwise he will kill me." Therefore he sent Akrūra to Gokula. Akrūra, having gone by chariot, said to Kṛṣṇa — "Come to Mathurā, for everyone desires the sight of you."
readings.teaches: gerundive (अनीयर्/तव्य — हन्तव्यः "to-be-killed," with instrumental agent मया); future लृट् (हनिष्यति, इच्छन्ति present); causative प्रैषयत्; relative यतः-clause (reason); सम्बन्ध-षष्ठी (कृष्णस्य मातुलः, तव दर्शनम्)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → कृष्णस्य (relation beyond the कारक roles)

notes.en: patient — "the boy is to be killed"
gerundive (कृत्य) — तव्य of √हन्; "(he) who must be killed"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सर्वे (pronominal nom. pl. ए)

readings.vyakhya: महत् नवीनम् — कृत्यप्रत्ययः। हन्तव्यः इति तव्य (तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः), अर्थे "अवश्यं हननीयः"। कृत्ये कर्ता तृतीयायाम् (मया), कर्म प्रथमायाम् (बालः) — कर्मणिवत्। लृट् हनिष्यति इति भविष्यति; यतः इति हेतौ।
readings.vyakhya_en: The big new arrival: the **gerundive** (कृत्य) — हन्तव्यः "(he) who must be killed," तव्य of √हन् (तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः, 3.1.96). It expresses necessity/obligation, and it governs case exactly like the passive: the agent goes to **instrumental** (मया "by me") and the patient to **nominative** (बालः). So "the boy is-to-be-killed by me" reads with मया … बालः … हन्तव्यः all in agreement. Against it stands the plain **future** हनिष्यति "he will kill" (लृट्, 3.3.13) — Kaṃsa weighs necessity against consequence. The reason-clause opens with यतः "because." This is the grammatical hinge from playful Gokula into the Mathurā confrontation.

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

readings.sentence: कृष्णे गच्छति सति गोप्यः अतीव अरुदन्। याः गोप्यः कृष्णम् प्रेम्णा अपश्यन्, ताः सर्वाः शोकेन मग्नाः अभवन्। रथे स्थितः कृष्णः ताः रुदतीः दृष्ट्वा अपि न न्यवर्तत। तस्य हृदये तु ताः एव सर्वदा अवसन्।
readings.translation: When Kṛṣṇa was leaving, the gopīs wept bitterly. Those gopīs who used to look upon Kṛṣṇa with love — all of them were sunk in grief. Kṛṣṇa, seated in the chariot, though he saw them weeping, did not turn back. Yet in his heart they alone dwelt always.
readings.teaches: locative absolute (सति-सप्तमी — कृष्णे गच्छति सति, 2.3.37); relative-correlative याः…ताः over a full clause; present participle as object (रुदतीः "weeping ones"); gerund दृष्ट्वा with concessive अपि

notes.role: यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम् → सति-सप्तमी — "when Kṛṣṇa…"

notes.en: present participle (शतृ, loc. sg.) in the absolute construction
present participle of √अस् (सत्), loc. — the marker of the सति-सप्तमी
correlative pronoun (तद्, fem. nom. pl.) — answers याः
past participle (क्त) of √स्था — "seated," attributive to कृष्णः
present participle (शतृ, fem. acc. pl.) — agreeing with ताः

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ → रुदत्; fem. रुदती, acc. pl. रुदतीः

readings.vyakhya: अधिकरणं त्रिविधम् इह — सति-सप्तमी (कृष्णे गच्छति सति) कालार्थे; रथे हृदये इति देशाधिकरणे। याः…ताः इति वाक्यद्वये सम्बन्धः। रुदतीः इति शतृ कर्मणि (ताः रुदतीः)। दृष्ट्वा अपि इति अनुमत्यर्थे — "दृष्ट्वापि न न्यवर्तत"।
readings.vyakhya_en: Three locatives, three jobs. The **locative absolute** (सति-सप्तमी, 2.3.37) sets the scene in time — कृष्णे गच्छति सति "Kṛṣṇa being-in-the-act-of-going," i.e. "as Kṛṣṇa was leaving": a whole subordinate clause folded into two locative words. Ordinary locatives of place follow — रथे "in the chariot," हृदये "in the heart" (2.3.36). The relative-correlative याः … ताः now spans a full clause ("those gopīs who used to look on him — they all sank in grief"). And the शतृ participle appears for the first time **as an accusative object** — ताः रुदतीः "them, the weeping ones." दृष्ट्वा अपि "even having seen" gives the concessive: he saw, yet did not turn.

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

readings.sentence: यः कंसः चिरम् कृष्णस्य वधम् इच्छति स्म, सः एव अधुना भयेन कम्पते। कृष्णः मथुराम् प्रविश्य रङ्गभूमौ मल्लान् अहन्। ततः सः उच्चासनात् कंसम् आकृष्य भूमौ अपातयत्। यम् राजानम् सर्वे जनाः अबिभयुः, सः कृष्णेन क्षणेन एव हतः। एवम् अधर्मस्य अन्तः, धर्मस्य च जयः अभवत्।
readings.translation: He who for long had wished for Kṛṣṇa's death — that very one now trembles with fear. Kṛṣṇa, having entered Mathurā, killed the wrestlers in the arena. Then he dragged Kaṃsa down from his high throne and threw him to the ground. The king whom all people had feared — he was killed by Kṛṣṇa in but a moment. Thus came the end of unrighteousness, and the victory of dharma.
readings.teaches: climax — two relative-correlatives (यः…सः on the subject, यम्…सः on the object); अपादान (भयस्य source → उच्चासनात् ablative, अबिभयुः with 5th); causative अपातयत्; षष्ठी of object with कृत् (कृष्णस्य वधम्, 2.3.65); passive close (हतः)

notes.en: object of the action-noun वधम् — "(the) killing OF Kṛṣṇa"

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति → object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → कृष्णस्य

notes.en: object of इच्छति — what Kaṃsa wished for
with लट् → past habitual — "had been wishing"
gerund (ल्यप् — क्त्वा after prefix प्र-) — prior action
causative of √पत् — "cause to fall, throw down"
object of अबिभयुः — whom they feared

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् → बिभयुः; with augment-like reduplication, 3pl perfect

readings.vyakhya: कथायाः शिखरम् — द्वौ सम्बन्धौ यद्-तद्। कर्तरि यः…सः (यः इच्छति स्म सः कम्पते); कर्मणि यम्…सः (यं अबिभयुः सः हतः)। अपादानम् द्विधा — उच्चासनात् (departure), भयस्य हेतुः भी-धातुना अबिभयुः। वधम् इति कृत्, तत्र कर्म षष्ठ्याम् (कृष्णस्य वधम्)। अन्ते कर्मणि हतः — कथार्धम् सर्वम् कर्मणि समाप्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The climax, and it gathers everything. Two relative-correlatives frame it, one on each axis: यः … सः on the **subject** ("he who long wished Kṛṣṇa's death — that one now trembles") and यम् … सः on the **object** ("the king whom all feared — he was killed"). Two ablatives of separation: उच्चासनात् "from the high throne" (2.3.28) and the fear-source folded into अबिभयुः. The action-noun वधम् "killing" takes its object in the **genitive** — कृष्णस्य वधम् "the killing OF Kṛṣṇa" (2.3.65, the कृत्-षष्ठी). The arc that began with butter and a rope ends as it must, in the passive: हतः "was killed" — and the whole Kṛṣṇa-childhood sequence closes on its grammatical signature, the कर्मणि क्त, now carrying the weight of a death rather than a game.

source.ref: Pañcatantra 1 — the lion and the clever rabbit (सिंहः शशकश्च)

readings.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् वने भासुरको नाम सिंहः वसति स्म। सः बलवान् आसीत्, किन्तु अतीव क्रूरः। प्रतिदिनम् सः बहून् पशून् अहन्। तेन सर्वे मृगाः भयेन कम्पन्ते स्म। ते मिलित्वा सिंहम् ऊचुः — "हे स्वामिन्, मा सर्वान् पशून् हन्। वयम् एव प्रतिदिनम् एकम् पशुम् तव आहाराय प्रेषयिष्यामः।"
readings.translation: In a certain forest there lived a lion named Bhāsuraka. He was strong, but exceedingly cruel. Every day he killed many animals. Because of this all the beasts trembled with fear. They, having gathered, said to the lion — "O master, do not kill all the animals. We ourselves will send one animal every day for your food."
readings.teaches: fable opening — कस्मिंश्चित् (indefinite locative), प्रोहिबिटिव mā + लङ् (मा हन्), future 1pl (प्रेषयिष्यामः), dative of purpose (आहाराय), लिट् ऊचुः; reuses gerund, instrumental of cause

notes.en: indefinite pronoun (किम् + चित्), locative — "in some / a certain"
with लट् → past — "used to dwell, lived"
pronoun (तद्, instr.) — "by that → because of this"
prohibitive particle — with लङ् (no augment) forbids the act

notes.role: लुङ् — after मा the prohibitive takes augmentless लुङ् (मा हिंसीः type)

notes.en: purpose — dative of purpose ("for the sake of food")

readings.vyakhya: नूतनकथारम्भः — पञ्चतन्त्रात्। कस्मिंश्चित् वने इति लोकप्रसिद्धम् आख्यानारम्भपदम्। मा हन् इति प्रतिषेधे लुङ् अनद्यतनः अनागमकः। आहाराय इति तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी; प्रेषयिष्यामः इति लृट् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचने।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new story begins — from the Pañcatantra, and it opens with the formula every Sanskrit tale is built on: कस्मिंश्चित् वने "in a certain forest" (कः + चित् = the indefinite "some"). One genuinely new construction: the **prohibitive** — मा with an augmentless past (मा … हन् "do not kill"), the standard way Sanskrit says "don't." Against it stands the animals' **future promise** — प्रेषयिष्यामः "we will send" (लृट्, 1st plural). The dative आहाराय "for food" is the dative of purpose (तादर्थ्य). All the rest — past tenses, gerund मिलित्वा, instrumental of cause भयेन — is grammar you already own, now carrying a fable instead of a god.

readings.sentence: एकदा शशकस्य वारः आगच्छत्। सः बुद्धिमान् शशकः चिरम् विचिन्त्य एकम् उपायम् अकरोत्। सः मन्दम् मन्दम् सिंहस्य समीपम् अगच्छत्। क्रुद्धः सिंहः अपृच्छत् — "किमर्थम् त्वम् विलम्बेन आगतः?" शशकः अवदत् — "मार्गे अन्यः बलवान् सिंहः माम् अरुणत्। सः त्वाम् एव स्वामिनम् न मन्यते।" तत् श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धः सिंहः तम् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति स्म।
readings.translation: One day the rabbit's turn came. That clever rabbit, after thinking for a long time, devised a plan. He went very slowly toward the lion. The angry lion asked — "Why have you come late?" The rabbit said — "On the road another strong lion stopped me. He does not regard you alone as master." Having heard that, the angry lion wished to see him.
readings.teaches: longer dialogue — किमर्थम् (why?), past participle as predicate (आगतः "have come"), gerund विचिन्त्य + श्रुत्वा, accusative of person stopped (माम् अरुणत्), infinitive of purpose (द्रष्टुम्), मन्यते आत्मनेपद

notes.en: gerund (ल्यप् — after prefix वि-) — prior action
past participle (क्त) of आ-गम् as predicate — "(you are) come"

readings.vyakhya: संवादः दीर्घतरः। किमर्थम् इति हेतुप्रश्ने; आगतः इति निष्ठा कर्तरि ("त्वम् आगतः")। माम् अरुणत् इति रुध्-धातोः सप्तमगणे लङ्। स्वामिनम् इति द्विकर्मके मन्यतेः अभिन्ननिर्देशे। द्रष्टुम् इच्छति इति तुमुन् इष्-धातुना।
readings.vyakhya_en: The dialogue lengthens — the trick is told, not just narrated. New touches: किमर्थम् "why? for what purpose?" (the interrogative of cause); the past participle as a finite-like **predicate** — त्वम् … आगतः "you have come" (क्त standing in for "you came/are come"); and a double-accusative with मन्यते — त्वाम् स्वामिनम् न मन्यते "does not regard you AS master," the object and its predicate-complement both accusative. The infinitive द्रष्टुम् इच्छति "wishes to see" closes on the hook that will spring the trap. Everything else is consolidation: four लङ् pasts, two gerunds (विचिन्त्य, श्रुत्वा), locatives, the मतुप् adjectives बलवान्/बुद्धिमान्.

chapters.title: कृत् — primary affixes: agent, action, and participle suffixes

readings.translation: The brahmin gives food; he is a giver.
readings.teaches: तृच् forms the agent-noun दातृ → दाता "giver" from दा.

notes.en: the root दा, as finite verb

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ → तृच् on दा → दातृ → दाता (agent-noun)

readings.vyakhya: दा-धातोः तृच्प्रत्यये दातृशब्दः सिध्यति, प्रथमैकवचने दाता इति रूपम्। यो ददाति स दाता।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.1.133 (ण्वुल्तृचौ) every root may take तृच् (the affix तृ) to name its agent. On दा "give" this yields the stem दातृ, whose nominative singular is दाता "giver". The agent-noun simply names the one who performs the verb's action — here, the one who gives.

readings.translation: Devadatta is a habitual doer.
readings.teaches: तृन् forms a habitual-agent noun कर्तृ → कर्ता from कृ.

notes.en: primary derivative naming the habitual agent

notes.role: तृन् on कृ → कर्तृ → कर्ता (habitual agent-noun)

readings.vyakhya: तृन्प्रत्यये कृ-धातोः कर्तृशब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने कर्ता। यः शीलेन करोति स कर्ता उच्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.135 (तृन्) the affix तृन् (तृ) comes after a root to name one who does the action habitually or by disposition (शील). On कृ "do" it gives the stem कर्तृ, nominative singular कर्ता. Unlike a plain agent, this names a characteristic doer — one whose nature it is to act.

readings.translation: The boy habitually goes to the village.
readings.teaches: णिनि with an उपपद forms the habit-agent गामिन् → गामी from गम्.

notes.en: the word-in-composition (द्वितीया) standing with the affix
primary derivative naming the habitual agent (ताच्छील्य)

notes.role: णिनि on गम् with उपपद ग्रामम् → गामिन् → गामी (habit agent-noun)

readings.vyakhya: ताच्छील्ये गम्यमाने उपपदे सति गम्-धातोः णिनिप्रत्यये गामिन्शब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने गामी। यः शीलेन ग्रामं गच्छति स ग्रामं गामी।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.78 (सुप्यजातौ णिनिस्ताच्छील्ये) the affix णिनि (इन्) attaches to a root when habit (ताच्छील्य) is meant and an उपपद — a noun in composition — stands with it. With उपपद ग्रामम् and root गम् "go", this yields the stem गामिन्, nominative singular गामी. The whole phrase ग्रामं गामी names one who customarily goes to the village.

readings.translation: The cooking (the act of cooking) is pleasing.
readings.teaches: घञ् makes a भाव action-noun from a root; पच् → पाकः.

notes.en: the bare action itself, named as a noun

readings.vyakhya: धातोः भावे घञ् प्रत्ययः। पच् इत्यस्मात् पाकः इति कृदन्तं नाम जायते। तत् प्रथमायां कर्तृ।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.18 the affix घञ् is added to a root to name the bare action (भाव). From पच् "to cook" we get पाकः, "the act of cooking", a कृदन्त noun. Here it stands in the nominative as the subject of रोचते.

readings.translation: He wishes for victory.
readings.teaches: अच् makes a भाव action-noun from an इ/ई-final root; जि → जयः.

notes.en: the bare action itself, named as a noun

readings.vyakhya: इवर्णान्तात् धातोः भावे अच् प्रत्ययः। जि इत्यस्मात् जयः इति कृदन्तम्। तत् द्वितीयायां कर्म।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.56 (एरच्) the affix अच् is added to a root ending in इ/ई to name the action (भाव). From जि "to conquer" we get जयः, "victory". Here it stands in the accusative as the object of इच्छति.

readings.translation: He begins the going (the departure).
readings.teaches: ल्युट् makes a neuter भाव action-noun in -अन; गम् → गमनम्.

notes.en: the bare action itself, named as a noun

notes.role: ल्युट् च → गम् → गमनम् (neuter action-noun in -अन)

readings.vyakhya: धातोः भावे ल्युट् प्रत्ययः, तस्य अन इति आदेशः। गम् इत्यस्मात् गमनम् इति नपुंसकं कृदन्तम्। तत् द्वितीयायां कर्म।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.115 the affix ल्युट् (realized as -अन) is added to a root to name the bare action (भाव), giving a neuter noun. From गम् "to go" we get गमनम्, "going". Here it stands in the accusative as the object of आरभते.

readings.translation: Wealth is to be given to the brahmin.
readings.teaches: यत् forms a कृत्य gerundive on vowel-final roots (दा → देयम्).

words.gloss: "to be given" — fit to be given

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

readings.vyakhya: अचो यत् इति वचनात् अजन्तात् धातोः दा इत्यस्मात् यत्प्रत्ययः। देयम् इति कृत्यम्। कर्म प्रथमायां, कर्ता तृतीयायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: By अचो यत् (3.1.97) a root ending in a vowel takes the कृत्य affix यत्; so दा becomes देयम्, "to be given." Like every gerundive it governs case exactly as the passive does: the patient (धनम्) stands in the nominative, and an agent, if expressed, would stand in the instrumental. Here the recipient ब्राह्मणाय is in the dative (सम्प्रदान).

readings.translation: The task is to be done by me.
readings.teaches: ण्यत् forms a कृत्य gerundive on ऋ-final / consonant-final roots (कृ → कार्यम्).

words.gloss: "the task / to be done" — fit to be done

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

readings.vyakhya: ऋहलोर्ण्यत् इति ऋवर्णान्तात् हलन्ताच्च धातोः ण्यत्प्रत्ययः। कृ इत्यस्मात् कार्यम्। कर्ता मया इति तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: By ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (3.1.124) a root ending in ऋ (short or long) or in a consonant takes the कृत्य affix ण्यत्; so कृ becomes कार्यम्, "to be done, a task." The construction mirrors the passive: the agent मया is in the instrumental (तृतीया, by 2.3.18) and the patient stands in the nominative.

readings.translation: The lesson is to be read by the student.
readings.teaches: अनीयर् (-अनीय) forms a कृत्य gerundive (पठ् → पठनीयः).

words.gloss: "to be read" — fit to be read

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

readings.vyakhya: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः इति धातोः अनीयर्प्रत्ययः। पठ् इत्यस्मात् पठनीयम्। कर्ता शिष्येण तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: By तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः (3.1.96) a root may take तव्यत्, तव्य, or अनीयर्; here the अनीयर् variant gives पठ् → पठनीयः, "to be read." As with all कृत्य gerundives the syntax is passive-like: the agent शिष्येण stands in the instrumental (तृतीया, 2.3.18) and the patient पाठः in the nominative.

readings.translation: The potter makes a pot.
readings.teaches: अण् (कर्मण्यण्) forms an agent-noun whose object stands as उपपद in one compound.

notes.en: the object कुम्भ stands in composition with the agent-noun

words.gloss: "pot" — a clay pot (object of the verb)

readings.vyakhya: कुम्भं करोतीति कुम्भकारः। कर्मणि उपपदे कृधातोः अण्प्रत्ययः। उपपदं कर्म च समस्यते एकपदे।
readings.vyakhya_en: When an object (कर्मन्) stands as उपपद beside a root, the root takes अण् to form an agent-noun. Here कुम्भ "pot" joins कृ "make" and the affix अण् gives कुम्भकारः "pot-maker." The object does not stay a separate accusative word; it merges into a single तत्पुरुष compound with the agent-noun.

readings.translation: The cow-giver gives a cow to the brahmin.
readings.teaches: क (आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः) suffixes an आ-final root with an object-उपपद and no उपसर्ग.

notes.en: the object गो stands in composition with the agent-noun

notes.role: आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः → गो + दा + क → गोदः (आ-final दा, no उपसर्ग)

notes.en: dative — the one to whom the gift is given

readings.vyakhya: गां ददातीति गोदः। आकारान्तात् दाधातोः अनुपसर्गात् कर्मण्युपपदे कप्रत्ययः। एवं धनदः जलदश्च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A root ending in long आ, with no उपसर्ग before it and an object standing as उपपद, takes क instead of अण्. Thus गो "cow" + दा "give" + क yields गोदः "cow-giver." The same pattern gives धनदः "wealth-giver" and जलदः "water-giver" (the cloud). The object गो merges with the agent-noun into one तत्पुरुष compound.

readings.translation: The delighting son gladdens his mother.
readings.teaches: ल्यु (→ अन) forms an agent-noun from नन्दि-group roots.

notes.en: agent-noun in अन from the नन्दि-group

readings.vyakhya: नन्दतीति नन्दनः। नन्दिग्रहिपचादिगणे नन्दिधातोः ल्युप्रत्ययः, यस्य अनादेशः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Roots of the नन्दि-group take ल्यु, and ल्यु is replaced by अन, giving agent-nouns like नन्दनः "the delighting one, the son." Unlike अण् and क above, this ल्यु-formation needs no उपपद object to attach; the affix alone names the doer. The same rule routes ग्रहि-roots to णिनि and पच्-group roots to अच्.

sequence.translation: The man goes.
sequence.teaches: bare कर्तृ + verb; the प्रथमा as the base case

notes.role: नर is the कर्तृ — the independent agent
प्रथमा for the bare prātipadika-sense → नरः

notes.text: नर + सु, then नरस् → नरः

sequence.vyakhya: नरः स्वतन्त्रः, अतः प्रथमा।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The agent acting on its own stands in the प्रथमा — the base case. This is the starting point every other case departs from.

sequence.translation: The man goes to the village.
sequence.teaches: adds कर्मन् → द्वितीया

notes.role: ग्राम is कर्मन् — what the agent reaches

sequence.vyakhya: यत् कर्तुः ईप्सिततमम् तत् कर्मन्, कर्मणि द्वितीया।
sequence.vyakhya_en: What the agent most wants to reach is the कर्मन्; the कर्मन् takes the द्वितीया. The goal of motion is reached, so it is कर्मन् — hence ग्रामम्.

sequence.translation: The man goes to the village on foot.
sequence.teaches: adds करण → तृतीया

notes.role: पाद is करण — the most effective means

notes.en: dual — a man has two feet

sequence.vyakhya: पादौ साधकतमम् करण, कर्तृकरणयोः तृतीया।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The feet are the most effective means by which the going is done — the करण — and the करण takes the तृतीया.

sequence.translation: The man comes from the village.
sequence.teaches: adds अपादान → पञ्चमी

notes.role: ग्राम is अपादान — the fixed point of departure

notes.text: आ +

notes.en: "come" — आ adds "toward," motion toward the speaker

sequence.vyakhya: ध्रुवम् अपाये अपादान, अपादाने पञ्चमी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The fixed point from which there is departure is the अपादान; it takes the पञ्चमी. Same word ग्राम — goal (द्वितीया) above, source (पञ्चमी) here. The case follows the role.

sequence.translation: The man gives fruit to the boy.
sequence.teaches: adds सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

notes.role: बाल is सम्प्रदान — the one aimed at, the recipient

sequence.vyakhya: कर्मणा यम् अभिप्रैति सः सम्प्रदान, चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The one the agent aims at through the object — here, through the fruit, the boy — is the सम्प्रदान; it takes the चतुर्थी.

sequence.translation: The man lives in the village.
sequence.teaches: adds अधिकरण → सप्तमी

notes.role: ग्राम is अधिकरण — the locus of the action

sequence.vyakhya: आधारः अधिकरण, सप्तमी अधिकरणे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The locus in which the action rests is the अधिकरण; it takes the सप्तमी. A third role for ग्राम: goal, source, and now locus — द्वितीया, पञ्चमी, सप्तमी.

sequence.translation: The man's son lives in the village.
sequence.teaches: adds षष्ठी (a relation, not a कारक)

words.gloss: of the man, the relation whose

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the remaining relation (genitive) → नरस्य

sequence.vyakhya: कारकभिन्नः सम्बन्धः शेष, तत्र षष्ठी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A relation that is not one of the कारकas — here mere belonging, "of the man" — is शेष, "the rest," and takes the षष्ठी. Note नर has stepped out of the agent-role; पुत्र is now the कर्तृ.

sequence.translation: The boy sees the fruit.
sequence.teaches: neuter stem फल: प्रथमा = द्वितीया (same frame, new declension)

notes.text: here प्रथमा and द्वितीया share one form, both फलम्

notes.role: अतोऽम् — neuter a-stem सु/अम् → अम्, so nom.sg फलम्
स्वमोर्नपुंसकात् — neuter सु and अम् behave alike: फलम् serves as both प्रथमा and द्वितीया

sequence.vyakhya: नपुंसके प्रथमा द्वितीया च समाने रूपे — फलम् इति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: In the neuter, प्रथमा and द्वितीया share one form. So फलम् is the कर्मन् here exactly as it would be the कर्तृ — the role still picks the case, but neuter collapses the two.

sequence.translation: The fruit falls from the tree.
sequence.teaches: neuter फलम् as कर्तृ (प्रथमा = द्वितीया form); reuses अपादान पञ्चमी

notes.role: फल is now कर्तृ — the same neuter form फलम् fills the agent role

notes.text: the neuter form is still फलम्

sequence.vyakhya: फलम् इह स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता, तथापि रूपम् तदेव।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same word फलम् that was the object above is the agent here — and looks identical, because the neuter does not distinguish them. The अपादान-पञ्चमी (वृक्षात्) is exactly as it was for ग्रामात्: the frame is unchanged.

sequence.translation: The man sees fruit in the river.
sequence.teaches: feminine ī-stem नदी: अधिकरण सप्तमी नद्याम्, with यण् sandhi

notes.role: स्त्रियाम् — the feminine, opening the stems नदी belongs to
ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् — नदी is a ङीप्-formed ī-stem feminine

notes.text: नदी + आम्

notes.role: ङेराम्नद्याम्नीभ्यः — ī-stem fem locative sg takes आम्: नदी+आम्

notes.text: → नद्याम्

notes.role: इको यणचि — ई before आम् becomes य्: नदी+आम् → नद्याम्

sequence.vyakhya: अधिकरणे सप्तमी — स्त्रीलिङ्गेऽपि सैव।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The locus takes the सप्तमी whatever the gender: ग्रामे (masc.) and नद्याम् (fem.) are the same case, differently declined. Role fixes the case; stem-class fixes the ending.

sequence.translation: The two men go to the village.
sequence.teaches: number: dual कर्तृ नरौ + dual verb

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने — two referents → द्विवचन (dual): नरौ, गच्छतः

notes.en: dual — the verb agrees with नरौ

sequence.vyakhya: द्वयोः द्विवचनम् — कर्तरि क्रियायाम् च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Two referents call for the द्विवचन — in the noun (नरौ) and, agreeing, in the verb (गच्छतः). The role is still कर्तृ-प्रथमा, exactly as नरः was; only the count has changed.

sequence.translation: The men go to the village.
sequence.teaches: number: plural कर्तृ नराः (नर+जस् → नराः) + plural verb

notes.text: नर + जस् → नराः

notes.role: प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — नर + जस् (अस्) → नराः, the nom.pl

sequence.vyakhya: बहूनाम् बहुवचनम्। एकः नरः, द्वौ नरौ, बहवः नराः — एकैव विभक्तिः, भिद्यते वचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Many referents call for the बहुवचन. नरः, नरौ, नराः — one प्रथमा case across three numbers: the विभक्ति is constant, the वचन varies.

sequence.translation: The fruits are eaten by the men.
sequence.teaches: plural instrumental नरैः (अ+भिस् → ऐस्) + neuter plural फलानि

notes.en: here the agent of a passive verb, in the instrumental

notes.text: नर + भिस् → नरैः

notes.role: अतो भिस ऐस् — a-stem instrumental plural भिस् → ऐस्: नर+ऐस् → नरैः

notes.text: फल → फलानि

notes.role: जश्शसोः शिः — neuter जस्/शस् → शि (इ): फल+शि
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् inserted before the शि-ending: फल+न्+इ
सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ — the stem vowel lengthens: फला-न्-इ → फलानि

sequence.vyakhya: बहुषु नरेषु करणभूतेषु तृतीया बहुवचनम्; फलानि नपुंसकबहुवचने।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The instrumental plural नरैः; the neuter plural फलानि. Same roles as ever — only the number is new, and each stem-class spells the plural its own way.

sequence.translation: I go to the village.
sequence.teaches: person (पुरुष): the उत्तमपुरुष — speaker — selects a different ending

notes.text: the pronoun for the speaker

notes.role: तिङस्त्रीणि त्रीणि प्रथममध्यमोत्तमाः — the तिङ् endings fall into three पुरुष: प्रथम, मध्यम, उत्तम
तिप्तस्झि… — the तिङ् ending मिप् for उत्तम·एक → गच्छामि

sequence.vyakhya: वक्ता उत्तमपुरुषः। एकस्मिन् कर्तरि एकवचनम् — गच्छामि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The speaker is the उत्तमपुरुष. The verb's ending names who acts, just as the noun's ending named its role: गच्छति (he goes) and गच्छामि (I go) share one root, one tense — only the पुरुष differs.

sequence.translation: You go to the village.
sequence.teaches: person: the मध्यमपुरुष — the one addressed

notes.text: the pronoun for the one addressed

notes.role: तिङ् ending सिप् for मध्यम·एक → गच्छसि

sequence.vyakhya: यम् प्रति उच्यते सः मध्यमपुरुषः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The one spoken to is the मध्यमपुरुष. Three persons now stand together: गच्छति (प्रथम, he), गच्छसि (मध्यम, you), गच्छामि (उत्तम, I) — one root, three endings.

sequence.translation: The boy went to the village.
sequence.teaches: tense (लकार): the past — लङ् replaces लट्, and an augment अ is prefixed

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् — for past (not of today) the लङ् replaces लट्

notes.text: अ-augment + गच्छ + त् → अगच्छत्

sequence.vyakhya: भूते अनद्यतने लङ्। धातुः स एव, कालः अन्यः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For the past, the लङ् stands where the present लट् stood. The root is the same √गम्; only the tense — the लकार — has changed. गच्छति (goes) → अगच्छत् (went): a new tense-slot, marked by the अ-augment in front.
sequence.note: // The full augment/ending derivation (3.4.100ff, 6.4.71) is later; here we state the siddha form अगच्छत् and cite the लकार choice 3.2.111. Stepwise derivation deferred to a Track-B path.

sequence.translation: The man is (becomes) in the village.
sequence.teaches: गुण of the root vowel — भू → भो → भव् before शप् gives भवति

notes.role: कर्तरि शप् — when an agent is denoted, शप् (अ) is added after the root (the गण-1 vikaraṇa)
सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः — before शप् the root vowel takes गुण → ऊ → ओ → (before अ) अव् → भव्
तिप्तस्झि… — the तिङ् ending तिप् for प्रथम·एक → भवति

sequence.vyakhya: भू इति धातुः। शपि परतः ऊकारस्य गुणः ओकारः, सोऽवादेशम् आपद्यते — भव्। तिपि भवति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The root भू "be." Before शप् (the अ-vikaraṇa of गण 1, by कर्तरि शप्), the root vowel ऊ takes गुण (7.3.84): ऊ → ओ, which before the following अ becomes अव् — भू → भव्. With the प्रथम·एक ending तिप्, the present is भवति. Compare गच्छति: same लट्, same तिप्, but भू shows its गुण where गम् does not.

sequence.translation: The two men go to the village.
sequence.teaches: number on the VERB — two agents take the तस् ending → गच्छतः

notes.role: तिङस्त्रीणि त्रीणि प्रथममध्यमोत्तमाः — each triad of तिङ् endings is प्रथम/मध्यम/उत्तम
तान्येकवचनद्विवचनबहुवचनान्येकशः — within a triad the three are एक/द्वि/बहुवचन

sequence.vyakhya: द्वयोः कर्त्रोः द्विवचनम्। प्रथमपुरुषस्य द्विवचनं तस् — गच्छतः। एको गच्छति, द्वौ गच्छतः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Number lives on the verb too. नरौ are two, so the verb takes the द्विवचन ending: of the प्रथम triad तिप्-तस्-झि (1.4.101/102), the middle one तस् gives गच्छतः. Side by side: गच्छति (one goes), गच्छतः (two go) — same root, tense, person; only वचन shifts.

sequence.translation: The boy fears the wolves.
sequence.teaches: special government: a verb of fearing makes the feared thing अपादान → पञ्चमी

words.gloss: of/from the wolves — the thing feared

notes.en: source — here, what one shrinks from

notes.role: भीत्रार्थानां भयहेतुः — with verbs of fearing, the cause of fear is अपादान

sequence.vyakhya: भयहेतुः अपादानम् — न तु कर्म। वृकेभ्यः बिभेति, न वृकान्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: One might expect the feared thing to be the कर्मन् (the object fearing "reaches"). But Pāṇini names it अपादान — what one shrinks away from — so it takes the पञ्चमी, not the द्वितीया: वृकेभ्यः, not वृकान्. Knowing the verb tells you the case.

sequence.translation: The man owes Devadatta a hundred.
sequence.teaches: special government: √धारि 'owe' makes the creditor सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

notes.role: धारेरुत्तमर्णः — with √धारि (owe), the creditor (उत्तमर्ण) is सम्प्रदान

sequence.vyakhya: उत्तमर्णः सम्प्रदानम्। यस्य ऋणं धार्यते सः सम्प्रदानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The creditor — the one to whom the debt is owed — is the सम्प्रदान, just as a gift's recipient is. So देवदत्ताय (चतुर्थी), the same case as the boy received the fruit in. A specific verb extends a familiar role.

sequence.translation: The man cooks rice.
sequence.teaches: the verb's ending is परस्मैपद — the active-voice set of तिङ् endings

notes.en: active voice — the तिप्-तस्-झि set of endings

notes.role: लः परस्मैपदम् — the तिङ् endings replacing a लकार are by default परस्मैपद

sequence.vyakhya: लादेशाः परस्मैपदम् — तिप्तस्झ्यादयः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The endings that replace a लकार are, in general, परस्मैपद — the active set (तिप्, तस्, झि …). पचति is one of them. A second set, the आत्मनेपद, stands beside it for the middle voice.

sequence.translation: The man cooks rice (for himself).
sequence.teaches: the आत्मनेपद — the middle-voice set, action for the agent's own sake

notes.en: middle voice — the त-आताम्-झ set of endings

notes.role: तङानावात्मनेपदम् — the तङ् (and शानच्/कानच्) replacements are आत्मनेपद
तान्येकवचन… — the nine endings distribute as 3 पुरुष × 3 वचन (एक/द्वि/बहु)

sequence.vyakhya: पचति परस्मैपदम्, पचते आत्मनेपदम् — स एव धातुः, फलम् अन्यत्र वा स्वे वा।
sequence.vyakhya_en: One root, two ending-sets. पचति (परस्मैपद) cooks for another; पचते (आत्मनेपद) cooks for oneself. The nine endings of each set fill the same grid — three पुरुष across three वचन — so a verb-form names person, number, and voice all at once.

sequence.translation: Homage to the gods.
sequence.teaches: नमः and its companions (स्वस्ति, स्वाहा …) govern the चतुर्थी

notes.text: the word of salutation

notes.role: नमःस्वस्ति… — with नमः (and स्वस्ति, स्वाहा, स्वधा, अलम्, वषट्) the word takes चतुर्थी

sequence.vyakhya: नमसा योगे चतुर्थी। नमो देवेभ्यः, न देवान्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A handful of fixed words — नमः foremost — govern the चतुर्थी by themselves, no verb needed. "नमो देवेभ्यः," homage to the gods (चतुर्थी), never देवान्. Learn the word, and its case comes with it.

sequence.translation: The man studies for a month.
sequence.teaches: duration and extent (काल, अध्वन्) in continuous connection take द्वितीया

notes.en: object — here, the span filled by the action

notes.role: कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे — a time-word (or distance) in unbroken connection takes द्वितीया

sequence.vyakhya: अत्यन्तसंयोगे कालाध्वनोः द्वितीया। मासम् अधीते — कृत्स्नं कालम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When an action fills a whole stretch of time or space without a break, that span stands in the द्वितीया: मासम् अधीते, "studies through a whole month." The accusative here measures extent, not an object reached.

sequence.translation: He goes to the village.
sequence.teaches: गत्यर्थ — with a verb of motion, the goal (कर्म) takes द्वितीया

notes.en: the goal of motion is treated as the object

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → the most-desired goal is कर्मन्
गत्यर्थकर्मणि द्वितीयाचतुर्थ्यौ — with a motion-verb the goal takes द्वितीया (or चतुर्थी)

notes.text: ग्रामम् → ग्रामं (final म् → anusvāra before ग)

sequence.vyakhya: गत्यर्थस्य धातोः कर्म गन्तव्यं द्वितीयायाम्। ग्रामो गन्तव्यः, अतः ग्रामम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A verb of motion (गम् "go") makes its destination the कर्मन् — the goal one most wants to reach (1.4.49) — and that takes the accusative (2.3.12). So "go TO the village" is simply ग्रामम् (acc.), no preposition needed. The same rule allows चतुर्थी (a dative of goal) in Vedic and poetry; classical prose prefers द्वितीया.

sequence.translation: He studies for a month.
sequence.teaches: अत्यन्तसंयोग — unbroken extent of time/space takes द्वितीया

notes.en: extent — the span over which the action runs without break

notes.role: कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे — a word of time or distance spanning an unbroken stretch takes द्वितीया

sequence.vyakhya: कालस्य अध्वनश्च अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया। मासम् इति कालपरिमाणम्।
