sequence.vyakhya_en: Duration and distance, when the action fills the whole stretch without a gap, stand in the accusative (2.3.5) — मासम् "(for) a month," क्रोशम् "(for) a krośa of road." Not "to a month" but "across the whole of it." This is why "he studies for a month" needs no "for": the bare accusative मासम् carries the span.

sequence.translation: "curds, Indra" → दधीन्द्रः (curds-Indra)
sequence.teaches: सवर्णदीर्घ — two like (सवर्ण) vowels merge into one long vowel

notes.text: दधि + इन्द्रः: इ meets इ

notes.en: homogeneous — vowels of the same place of articulation

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — a simple vowel before a like vowel; the two become one long vowel

notes.text: → ई → दधीन्द्रः

sequence.vyakhya: समाने सवर्णे अकः दीर्घ एकादेशः। इ + इ = ई।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When a simple vowel (अक्) meets a homogeneous vowel — इ with इ, उ with उ, अ with अ — the pair fuses into the single long vowel of that class. दधि + इन्द्रः gives दधीन्द्रः: two इ become one ई.

sequence.translation: "not here" → नेह
sequence.teaches: गुण — अ/आ before इ/उ/ऋ yields the गुण vowel (ए, ओ, अर्)

notes.text: न + इह: अ meets इ

notes.role: आद्गुणः — when अ/आ is followed by another vowel, the two become the single गुण vowel

notes.text: अ + इ → ए → नेह

sequence.vyakhya: अवर्णात् अचि गुण एकादेशः। अ + इ = ए।
sequence.vyakhya_en: An अ or आ followed by इ, उ, or ऋ does not merge to a long vowel but shifts to the गुण grade: अ + इ → ए, अ + उ → ओ, अ + ऋ → अर्. So न + इह → नेह. The same अ behaves differently depending on the vowel it meets.

sequence.translation: "yours indeed" → तवैव
sequence.teaches: वृद्धि — अ/आ before ए/ऐ/ओ/औ yields the वृद्धि vowel (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: तव + एव: अ meets ए

notes.role: वृद्धिरेचि — when अ/आ is followed by एच् (ए ऐ ओ औ), the two become the वृद्धि vowel

notes.text: अ + ए → ऐ → तवैव

sequence.vyakhya: अवर्णात् एचि वृद्धिः एकादेशः। अ + ए = ऐ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When अ or आ meets one of the diphthong-grade vowels (ए, ऐ, ओ, औ), the result climbs to the वृद्धि grade: अ + ए → ऐ, अ + ओ → औ. So तव + एव → तवैव. गुण and वृद्धि are the two upward grades इ/उ already met in the verb.

sequence.translation: "the wise one is to be served" → सुध्युपास्यः
sequence.teaches: यण् — इ/उ/ऋ before an unlike vowel become the glide य्/व्/र्

notes.text: सुधी + उपास्यः: ई meets उ (unlike)

notes.en: the glides य् व् र् ल्

notes.role: इको यणचि — an इक् vowel (इ उ ऋ ऌ) before any vowel becomes its corresponding यण् glide

notes.text: ई → य् → सुध्युपास्यः

sequence.vyakhya: इकः अचि यण् आदेशः। ई + उ → य् + उ = यु।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When इ, उ, or ऋ meets an unlike vowel, it does not merge but turns into its glide — य्, व्, र् — and the following vowel stands: सुधी + उपास्यः → सुध्युपास्यः. (Like meeting like gave the long vowel of ex023; unlike gives the glide here.)

sequence.translation: He did that (long ago / it is told).
sequence.teaches: लिट् — the perfect, for remote or reported past; the root reduplicates

notes.en: perfect — the remote or reported past (परोक्ष)

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — for a past beyond direct witness, लिट् replaces the लकार

notes.text: कृ reduplicates → च-कार → चकार

sequence.vyakhya: परोक्षे भूते लिट्। धातुः द्विरुक्तः — चकार।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For a past the speaker did not witness — the deep past of story and report — the लिट् is used, and the root doubles its first syllable: कृ → चकार, "he did" (out of sight, or long ago). Compare अकरोत् (लङ्, the past one saw): same act, different reach into time.

sequence.translation: He will do that tomorrow.
sequence.teaches: लृट् — the future; built on the root with a स्य-marker

notes.text: the adverb fixing the time as future

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — for what is yet to be, लृट् is used

notes.text: करि + ष्य + ति → करिष्यति

sequence.vyakhya: भविष्यति लृट्। करोति, अकरोत्, चकार, करिष्यति — एकः धातुः, चत्वारः कालाः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For what is still to come, the लृट् is used. Now the whole time-axis stands on one root √कृ: करोति (does), अकरोत् (did, witnessed), चकार (did, long ago), करिष्यति (will do). The लकार is the verb's clock — choose it, and the tense is set.

sequence.translation: He did that yesterday.
sequence.teaches: लङ् — the imperfect, for a NON-today (अनद्यतन) past

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् → the imperfect for a not-today past → अकरोत्
तिङ्: तिप् (3·sg) on the past base → अकरोत् (with अट्-augment)

sequence.vyakhya: अनद्यतने भूते लङ्। ह्यः इति अनद्यतनकालः, अतः अकरोत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit splits the past three ways by *remoteness*. लङ् (the imperfect, 3.2.111) is the past that does NOT fall on the current day — hence ह्यः "yesterday" → अकरोत् "he did." The अ- prefix (अट्-augment) is the past marker you also saw in अगच्छत्. Same root √कृ as करोति "does," now in the not-today past.

sequence.translation: He did that long ago.
sequence.teaches: लिट् — the perfect, for a remote (परोक्ष) past beyond witness

notes.en: indeclinable — "of old" (marks the परोक्ष, beyond-sight, past)
perfect — remote past, not directly witnessed

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् → the perfect for a past beyond the speaker's witness → चकार (reduplicated)

sequence.vyakhya: परोक्षे भूते लिट्। अदृष्टं चिरातीतं — चकार। तदेव कृ-धातुः, द्विरुक्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The perfect (लिट्, 3.2.115) is the *remote* past — परोक्ष, "beyond the eye," what the speaker did not himself witness (history, legend, "long ago"). √कृ reduplicates to चकार "he did (of old)." Contrast ex060: अकरोत् (लङ्) is yesterday's deed, चकार (लिट्) is the ancient deed. The tense itself tells you how far back, and whether anyone saw it.

sequence.translation: He did that today.
sequence.teaches: लुङ् — the aorist, the tense-neutral past (and today’s past)

notes.en: aorist — the general past (and the past of today)

notes.role: लुङ् → the aorist for past sense → अकार्षीत्
च्लेः सिच् — the aorist takes the सिच् (s-aorist) marker (derivation deferred)

sequence.vyakhya: भूते सामान्ये लुङ्। अद्यतनं भूतम् अपि लुङा — अकार्षीत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The aorist (लुङ्, 3.2.110) is the *unmarked* past — it states a past act without committing to remoteness, and it is the proper past for *today's* events (अद्य "today" → अकार्षीत् "he has done"). √कृ now spans all three pasts: अकरोत् (yesterday, लङ्) · चकार (long ago, लिट्) · अकार्षीत् (today, लुङ्). The full form-building (सिच्, वृद्धि) is a Track-B derivation.

sequence.translation: He will do that tomorrow.
sequence.teaches: लुट् — the periphrastic future, for a NON-today (अनद्यतन) future

notes.en: periphrastic future — a future not on the current day

notes.role: अनद्यतने लुट् → the लुट् future for a not-today future → कर्ता (= कर्तृ + an understood अस्ति)

sequence.vyakhya: अनद्यतने भविष्यति लुट्। श्वः इति अनद्यतनः, अतः कर्ता।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit splits the FUTURE too. लुट् (3.3.15) is the future that does NOT fall today — श्वः "tomorrow" → कर्ता "he will do." It is "periphrastic": the form कर्ता is literally an agent-noun ("(he is) a doer (tomorrow)"). Contrast करिष्यति (लृट्, the general future, ex028). Past and future each have a today/not-today split — the लकार is the verb's calendar.

sequence.translation: The fire blazes.
sequence.teaches: an इ-stem masculine: nominative अग्निः (नर-like सु, but on an इ-stem)

notes.text: अग्नि + सु → अग्निः

sequence.vyakhya: इकारान्तं पुंलिङ्गम् अग्निशब्दः। प्रथमायाम् अग्निः, यथा नरः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: अग्नि is a masculine stem ending in इ. In the प्रथमा it takes the same सु that नर did, giving अग्निः — outwardly like नरः. The stem-class shows itself not here but in the oblique cases, where the इ shifts.

sequence.translation: The man gives water to the fire.
sequence.teaches: the इ-stem dative अग्नये — the stem इ takes गुण (इ → ए) before the ending

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → the recipient अग्नि takes चतुर्थी
घेर्ङिति — before a ङित् ending (here ङे, the dative), the इ-stem takes गुण; अग्नि + ए → अग्नये

sequence.vyakhya: घेः ङिति गुणः। अग्नि + ए → अग्नये — इकारस्य गुणः एकारः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Where नर simply added its ending (नराय), the इ-stem first shifts its इ to the गुण grade ए before the dative: अग्नि → अग्नय् + ए → अग्नये. Same case, same role as बालाय — but the stem-vowel changes, which is what marks the इ-class.

sequence.translation: The fires blaze.
sequence.teaches: the इ-stem nominative plural अग्नयः — again गुण before the plural ending

notes.role: जसि च — before जस् (nom.pl), the short इ-stem takes गुण; अग्नि + अस् → अग्नय् + अस् → अग्नयः

sequence.vyakhya: जसि गुणः। अग्नि + अस् → अग्नयः, यथा चतुर्थ्याम् अग्नये।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same गुण appears in the nominative plural: अग्नि + जस् → अग्नयः ("the fires"), where नर gave नराः. The इ-stem reveals its character wherever an ending pulls the इ up to ए.

sequence.translation: The father comes with the son.
sequence.teaches: सह "with" → the accompanying (subordinate) person takes तृतीया

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — with सह, the accompanying (non-principal) thing takes तृतीया

notes.text: the particle governing पुत्रेण

sequence.vyakhya: सहयोगे अप्रधाने तृतीया। पिता प्रधानम्, पुत्रः अप्रधानम् — पुत्रेण सह।
sequence.vyakhya_en: With सह "together," the secondary companion — not the principal actor — stands in the तृतीया: पुत्रेण सह "with the son." The father is principal (प्रधान, प्रथमा); the son accompanies (अप्रधान, तृतीया). The same case that named the instrument also names the companion.

sequence.translation: A family [is sustained] by wealth.
sequence.teaches: हेतु "cause, reason" → the cause takes तृतीया

notes.role: हेतौ — the word naming a cause takes तृतीया

notes.en: instrumental — here the sense "by reason of"

sequence.vyakhya: हेतौ तृतीया। येन फलं साध्यते सः हेतुः — धनेन कुलम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: What brings a result about — the cause — takes the तृतीया: धनेन "by reason of wealth." This is the same case as the instrument करण, widened: the means by which, and the cause for which, share one form.

sequence.translation: He comes with his son.
sequence.teaches: सह — the accompanying (subordinate) word takes तृतीया

notes.en: here the तृतीया of accompaniment, not instrument

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — with सह, the accompanier (the non-principal) takes तृतीया

sequence.vyakhya: सहयोगे अप्रधानं तृतीयायाम्। पिता प्रधानम्, पुत्रः अप्रधानः — अतः पुत्रेण।
sequence.vyakhya_en: "With" (सह) puts the companion — the *subordinate* party, not the principal — in the instrumental (2.3.19). The father is the principal (he is the agent who comes); the son merely accompanies, so the son is पुत्रेण, तृतीया. One case (तृतीया) thus carries two senses you now hold: instrument (by) and accompaniment (with).

sequence.translation: A family (is honored) on account of wealth.
sequence.teaches: हेतु — the cause/motive takes तृतीया

words.gloss: on account of wealth, because of wealth

notes.en: cause — the reason for which something happens

notes.role: हेतौ — a word denoting the cause takes तृतीया (विद्यया यशः, धनेन कुलम्)

sequence.vyakhya: हेतौ तृतीया। धनं हेतुः, तेन कुलम् उन्नतम् — धनेन।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The cause or motive — "because of X" — takes the instrumental (2.3.23). विद्यया यशः "fame through learning," धनेन कुलम् "a family (raised) by wealth." It is the same तृतीया as instrument and accompaniment, now in a third sense: the reason. Note how much one case-ending does — the reader must read the *sense* from context, not the form alone.

sequence.translation: The fruit is seen by the man.
sequence.teaches: a-stem masc. नर तृतीया एकवचन = नरेण — टा→इन (7.1.12) + णत्व

notes.en: agent expressed by the instrumental (of the passive दृश्यते)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया — the agent of the passive दृश्यते takes तृतीया
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — after an a-stem, तृतीया टा → इन → नर + इन = नरेन
रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे — within one word the र turns the following न → ण → नरेण

notes.text: a passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग); its agent stands in तृतीया → नरेण

sequence.vyakhya: नरशब्दात् तृतीयैकवचने टा, सा अकारात् परा इनादेशम् (७.१.१२), ततो रेफात् नकारस्य णत्वम् (८.४.१), इति नरेण।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For नर in the instrumental singular the ending is टा; after an a-stem टा becomes इन (7.1.12), giving नरेन. The र then retroflexes the following न to ण (णत्व, 8.4.1) — नरेण. As the agent of the passive दृश्यते "is seen," it stands in the तृतीया (2.3.18).

sequence.translation: "speech here" → वाग् अत्र
sequence.teaches: जश्त्व — a word-final hard stop softens to its voiced counterpart

notes.en: the soft (voiced) stops ग् ज् ड् द् ब्

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — a stop at word's end becomes its जश् (voiced) counterpart; क् → ग्

notes.text: वाक् → वाग्

sequence.vyakhya: पदान्ते झलां जश्। क् → ग्, यथा वाक् → वाग्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A hard stop standing at the end of a word softens to its voiced partner: क्→ग्, त्→द्, प्→ब्. So वाक् "speech" appears as वाग् before अत्र. The word's lemma is वाक्; its sentence-form follows the join.

sequence.translation: "and that" → तच्च
sequence.teaches: श्चुत्व — a dental meeting a palatal becomes palatal

notes.text: तत् + च: dental त् meets palatal च

notes.en: the palatal series श् च् छ् ज् झ् ञ्

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — a dental (त-class/स) next to a palatal (च-class/श) turns palatal; त् → च्

notes.text: त् → च् → तच्च

sequence.vyakhya: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुत्वम्। त् + च → च् + च = च्च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A dental sound touching a palatal is pulled into the palatal series: तत् + च → तच्च. The त् becomes च् to match the following च. Assimilation — the first sound takes on the place of the second.

sequence.translation: "the forest laughs" → वनं हसति
sequence.teaches: a word-final म् becomes anusvāra (ं) before a consonant

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — a word-final म् before a consonant becomes anusvāra; म् → ं

notes.text: वनम् → वनं (before हसति)

sequence.vyakhya: पदान्ते मकारस्य हलि अनुस्वारः। वनम् → वनं हसति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A म् at the end of a word, when a consonant follows, contracts to the anusvāra ं: वनम् हसति → वनं हसति. (Before a vowel, or at a true pause, the म् stays — so it is the following consonant that triggers the change.)

sequence.translation: Without wealth, (there is) sorrow.
sequence.teaches: विना — "without" takes तृतीया (optionally पञ्चमी/द्वितीया)

notes.role: पृथग्विनानानाभिस्तृतीयान्यतरस्याम् — with पृथक्/विना/नाना the word takes तृतीया (also पञ्चमी, द्वितीया)

sequence.vyakhya: विना-योगे तृतीया अन्यतरस्याम्। धनेन विना, धनाद् विना, धनं विना — त्रयं साधु।
sequence.vyakhya_en: पृथक्, विना, and नाना — all meaning "apart / without" — govern the instrumental, *optionally* (अन्यतरस्याम्, 2.3.32); the genitive… no, the ablative (पञ्चमी) and accusative are also allowed. So धनेन विना = धनाद् विना = धनं विना, all correct. The optionality (विभाषा / अन्यतरस्याम्) is itself a feature to notice: Pāṇini often sanctions more than one form.

sequence.translation: The mountain is far from the village.
sequence.teaches: अपादान/पञ्चमी for separation-distance — "from"

notes.en: the fixed point from which distance is measured

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the fixed source-point is अपादान

notes.text: पर्वतः → पर्वतो before the voiced द (visarga सन्धि)

sequence.vyakhya: अपायस्य ध्रुवम् अपादानम्, तस्मिन् पञ्चमी। ग्रामो ध्रुवः, ततो दूरम् — ग्रामात्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The ablative (पञ्चमी) marks the fixed point one moves or measures *from* (1.4.24, 2.3.28). With words of distance — दूरे "far," अन्तिके "near" — the reference point stands in the ablative: ग्रामात् "from the village." You met पञ्चमी as "from" in विनयाद् याति; here it is spatial separation, the rule's core sense.

sequence.translation: "by Rāma": रामेन → रामेण (न becomes ण after र)
sequence.teaches: णत्व — न् becomes ण् after र्/ष् in the same word

notes.text: राम + इन (instr.sg ending ट्→इन): the न् stands after the र् of राम

notes.role: रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे → न् after र् or ष् in one word → ण् → रामेण
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि → the change still applies across an intervening vowel/guttural/labial (here the ए) → रामेण

sequence.vyakhya: रेफात् परः नकारः णकारः समानपदे, अट्-व्यवधानेऽपि। रामेन → रामेण।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Within one word, a न् turns cerebral (ण्) when an र् or ष् precedes it (8.4.1) — even when a vowel, guttural, or labial stands between them (8.4.2). So राम + the instrumental -इन gives रामेण, not *रामेन*: the र् of राम reaches across the ए to retroflex the न्. This णत्व is why we say रामायण, ब्राह्मणः, नारायण.

sequence.translation: "Rāma the sixth" → रामष्षष्ठः (स/त-series cerebralised by ष)
sequence.teaches: ष्टुत्व — स् and the dentals turn cerebral (ष्/ट-series) next to ष् or a cerebral

notes.text: रामस् + षष्ठः: a dental स् meets the cerebral ष्

notes.en: cerebralisation — स्/तवर्ग → ष्/टवर्ग in contact with ष् or a cerebral

notes.role: ष्टुना ष्टुः → स् and the dentals next to ष्/टवर्ग become ष्/टवर्ग → रामष्षष्ठः

sequence.vyakhya: षकारटवर्गसन्निधौ सकारतवर्गयोः ष्टुत्वम्। रामस् षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Mirror of श्चुत्व (which palatalised before श्/च-series): ष्टुत्व *cerebralises*. A dental स् or त-series sound, meeting a cerebral ष् or ट-series sound, itself becomes cerebral (8.4.41). रामस् + षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः; तत् + टीका → तट्टीका. The articulation simply assimilates to its neighbour's place — the same logic as जश्त्व and श्चुत्व, one row over.

sequence.sentence: सम् कृतम् → संस्कृतम् (सङ्… → the nasal homorganic).
sequence.translation: "well-made" सम्+कृत → the nasal matches the following stop
sequence.teaches: अनुस्वार → परसवर्ण — anusvāra becomes the nasal of the following class

notes.text: सम् + कृत: final म् → anusvāra (8.3.23), then the anusvāra may take the class-nasal

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः → word-final म् before a consonant → anusvāra (संकृत)

notes.en: the nasal homogeneous with the following sound

notes.role: अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः → the anusvāra becomes the class-nasal of the following यय् consonant

sequence.vyakhya: मकारः अनुस्वारः, सः ययि परसवर्णः। सम् + कृत → संकृत → सङ्… परसवर्णेन।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A final म् before a consonant first becomes anusvāra (8.3.23, the rule that gave वनं); then that anusvāra may take the *homorganic* nasal — the nasal belonging to the following sound's class (8.4.58). सम् + कृतम् → संस्कृतम्; सम् + गतः → सङ्गतः (the guttural ङ् before ग). The nasal quietly tunes itself to whatever stop follows.

sequence.translation: "homage to thee": the विसर्ग returns to स् before त
sequence.teaches: विसर्ग → स् — a visarga becomes स् before a hard dental (खर्)

notes.text: नमः + ते: the visarga of नमः meets the त् of ते

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः → a visarga → स् before a खर् consonant → नमस्ते

notes.text: नमस् here is a गति/preverb-like form; 8.3.40 also fixes its स् → नमस्ते, नमस्कारः

sequence.vyakhya: विसर्गस्य सकारः खरि। नमः + ते → नमस्ते। पुनः सकारः प्रत्येति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The visarga is not the end of the story — before a hard consonant (खर्) it can revert to स् (8.3.34): नमः + ते → नमस्ते, नमः + कारः → नमस्कारः. The final स् of नरः became visarga before pause (8.2.66 → 8.3.15); here the reverse environment pulls the visarga back to स्. Sandhi is contextual all the way down: the same sound shows different faces by what stands next.

sequence.translation: The man comes from the village.
sequence.teaches: अपादान/पञ्चमी singular — ङसि → आत् after the a-stem → ग्रामात्

notes.text: नरः → नरो before the voiced ग (visarga सन्धि)

notes.en: the fixed point from which departure happens

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the fixed point one moves away from is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी — the अपादान takes पञ्चमी
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — after an a-stem ङसि → आत् → ग्रामात्

sequence.vyakhya: ग्रामो ध्रुवम् अपायस्य, ततो नरस्य आगमनम्। अतो ग्रामात् इति अपादाने पञ्चमी; अकारान्तत्वात् ङसेः आत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The village is the fixed point the man moves away from, so it is अपादान (1.4.24), expressed by the पञ्चमी (2.3.28). Because the stem ends in अ, the ablative ending ङसि becomes आत् (7.1.12) → ग्रामात् "from the village."

sequence.translation: the king's man (विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः)
sequence.teaches: तत्पुरुष — the LATER member is primary; the earlier qualifies it

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the man of the king"

notes.role: प्राक् कडारात् समासः — from here the combinations are named समास

notes.en: determinative — the second member is the head

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

sequence.vyakhya: उत्तरपदार्थप्रधानः तत्पुरुषः। राजपुरुषः — पुरुषः प्रधानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: In a तत्पुरुष the second member is the head and the first qualifies it: राजपुरुषः is a kind of पुरुष (man) — the king's. Resolve it (विग्रह) as राज्ञः पुरुषः, "the man of the king." The compound is whatever its last member is.

sequence.translation: Rāma-and-Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च)
sequence.teaches: द्वन्द्व — members are coordinate ("and"); none subordinate

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: dual — two people, so the compound is dual

sequence.vyakhya: उभयपदार्थप्रधानः द्वन्द्वः। रामः च कृष्णः च = रामकृष्णौ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A द्वन्द्व joins members that would each stand with "and" — none is subordinate, both are heads: रामः च कृष्णः च collapses to रामकृष्णौ, "Rāma and Kṛṣṇa." Two people, so the compound itself is dual.

sequence.translation: the yellow-clothed one [Viṣṇu] (विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः)
sequence.teaches: बहुव्रीहि — neither member is the head; the compound points OUTSIDE itself

words.gloss: the one whose garment is yellow

notes.text: विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः

notes.en: possessive / exocentric — denotes someone characterised by the members

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

sequence.vyakhya: अन्यपदार्थप्रधानः बहुव्रीहिः। पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य — सः विष्णुः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A बहुव्रीहि names neither member: पीताम्बरः is not "yellow" and not "garment" but the one who has a yellow garment — Viṣṇu. The sense lies OUTSIDE the compound (अन्यपदार्थ). Resolve with यस्य: "he whose (यस्य) garment is yellow."

sequence.translation: near Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम्)
sequence.teaches: अव्ययीभाव — the FIRST member (an indeclinable) is primary; the whole is an अव्यय

notes.text: विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम् — उप = "near"

notes.en: adverbial — the compound behaves as an indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable (here उप) is अव्ययीभाव

sequence.vyakhya: पूर्वपदार्थप्रधानः अव्ययीभावः। उप कृष्णस्य समीपम् — सर्वम् अव्ययम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: In an अव्ययीभाव the first member — an indeclinable like उप ("near") — is primary, and the whole compound becomes an indeclinable itself: उपकृष्णम्, "near Kṛṣṇa," fixed in form. Four types, four answers to one question: which member carries the sense?

sequence.translation: When the sun has risen, the lotus opens.
sequence.teaches: सति सप्तमी — the locative absolute: one act marking the time of another

notes.en: the locative-absolute subject — its action marks the time

notes.role: यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम् — that whose action marks another's time takes सप्तमी

notes.en: a past participle (क्त), agreeing with सूर्ये in सप्तमी

notes.text: उद् + इ → उदित "risen"

sequence.vyakhya: यस्य भावेन अन्यस्य भावः लक्ष्यते, तत्र सप्तमी — सति सप्तमी। सूर्ये उदिते इति कालः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The "locative absolute" (सति सप्तमी): when one event fixes the *time* of another, the first stands — subject and participle together — in the locative (2.3.37). सूर्ये उदिते "the sun having risen" = "when the sun rose." It is Sanskrit's compact "when / while" clause: a noun + participle in सप्तमी, needing no conjunction.

sequence.translation: The man's doing / the deed of the man.
sequence.teaches: कृत्-योग — with a कृत् noun, agent & object take षष्ठी

notes.en: the agent, but expressed through षष्ठी before a कृत् noun

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — before a कृत्-formed word, agent and object take षष्ठी

notes.en: a कृत् noun (action-noun in क्तिन्) from कृ "do"

notes.role: स्त्रियां क्तिन् — the feminine action-noun in क्तिन् → कृति

sequence.vyakhya: कृति उपपदे कर्तृकर्मणोः षष्ठी। नरः कर्ता, कृतिः कृत्, अतः नरस्य कृतिः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When the head word is a कृत्-derivative (an action- or agent-noun built from a root), its agent and object are expressed by the genitive, not their usual cases (2.3.65). नरस्य कृतिः = "the man's deed" — नर is logically the doer, but before कृति (a कृत् noun) it takes षष्ठी. This is why "the seeing of the lotus" is कमलस्य दर्शनम्: the कृत् noun pulls everything into the genitive.

sequence.translation: The man is in the village.
sequence.teaches: सप्तमी (locative) singular — the अधिकरण as locus → ग्रामे

notes.en: locus — the substratum of the action

notes.role: आधारोऽधिकरणम् — the locus (आधार) is termed अधिकरण
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च — सप्तमी after the अधिकरण कारक

notes.text: ग्राम + ङि (loc.sg); the a-stem before ङि yields ग्रामे

sequence.vyakhya: ग्रामे इति अधिकरणे सप्तमी। आधारोऽधिकरणम् इति संज्ञा, सप्तम्यधिकरणे च इति विभक्तिः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: ग्रामे is the locus (अधिकरण) of the being: by आधारोऽधिकरणम् (1.4.45) the village as substratum gets the अधिकरण name, and सप्तम्यधिकरणे च (2.3.36) then assigns it the locative. The a-stem locative singular ending gives ग्रामे.

sequence.translation: The king of the gods shines.
sequence.teaches: a-stem masc. षष्ठी plural — आम् takes नुट् → नाम्, vowel lengthens, न → ण

notes.en: the genitive of relation/possession (the शेष relation)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the षष्ठी for the leftover relation, here "of the gods"
ह्रस्वनद्यापो नुट् — after a short-vowel/नदी/आप् stem, आम् takes the नुट् augment → नाम्
नामि — before नाम्, the stem-final vowel lengthens → देवा
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowels → देवानाम्

sequence.vyakhya: देवानाम् इति षष्ठीबहुवचनम् — आमि नुट् (नाम्), नामि पूर्वस्य दीर्घः, रेफात् परस्य नस्य णत्वम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: देवानाम् is the genitive plural. The ending आम् first takes the नुट् augment न (7.1.54) → नाम्; before नाम् the stem-vowel lengthens to देवा (6.4.3, नामि); finally the र retroflexes the न to ण across the intervening vowels (8.4.2) → देवानाम्. With राजा (nom. sg.) the phrase means "the king of the gods shines."

sequence.sentence: देवः देवौ देवाः। देवम् देवौ देवान्। देवेन देवाभ्याम् देवैः। देवाय देवाभ्याम् देवेभ्यः। देवात् देवाभ्याम् देवेभ्यः। देवस्य देवयोः देवानाम्। देवे देवयोः देवेषु। हे देव हे देवौ हे देवाः॥
sequence.translation: The complete declension of देव "god" (a-stem masculine) — eight cases × three numbers.
sequence.teaches: the FULL अकारान्त पुंलिङ्ग table — every cell of देव, with the सूत्र behind each ending (concepts already introduced; here gathered as a reference paradigm)

notes.role: स्वौजस्… — सु, the nom. sg. सुप् affix
ससजुषो रुः — final स् → रु → visarga → देवः
प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — अ + औ (the dual ending) → औ → देवौ
प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — अ + जस् (अस्) → आः → देवाः
अमि पूर्वः — अ + अम् → अम् → देवम्

words.gloss: द्वितीया द्वि — acc. dual (= nom. dual)

notes.text: acc. dual = nom. dual (औट् → औ), one form देवौ

notes.role: तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि — masc. शस् → आन् → देवान्

words.gloss: तृ/च/पं द्वि — instr/dat/abl dual (भ्याम्); ONE form for all three

notes.role: सुपि च — अ → आ before भ्याम् → देवाभ्याम् (covers तृतीया/चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी dual)
अतो भिस ऐस् — a-stem भिस् → ऐस् → देवैः
ङेर्यः — a-stem ङे → य; + सुपि च (अ→आ) → देवाय

words.gloss: च/पं बहु — dat/abl pl. (भ्यस्); ONE form for both

notes.role: बहुवचने झल्येत् — अ → ए before भ्यस् → देवेभ्यः (covers चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी pl.)

words.gloss: ष/स द्वि — gen/loc dual (ओस्); ONE form for both

notes.role: ओसि च — अ → ए before ओस् → देवयोः (covers षष्ठी/सप्तमी dual)
ह्रस्वनद्यापो नुट् — आम् takes नुट् → नाम्
नामि — vowel lengthens before नाम् → देवानाम्
बहुवचने झल्येत् (and the loc.sg ए-result) → देवे

words.gloss: सप्तमी बहु — loc. pl. (सुप् → सु; स → ष)

notes.role: बहुवचने झल्येत् — अ → ए before सु → देवे
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — स् → ष् after the इण् ए → देवेषु
सम्बोधने च — the vocative; sg. is the bare stem → हे देव

sequence.vyakhya: अकारान्तस्य पुंलिङ्गस्य (देव) सर्वाः विभक्तयः सर्वाणि वचनानि च — एकत्र दर्शिताः। एकैकं सूत्रं प्रत्येकं प्रत्ययम् आदेशं च साधयति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: You met प्रथमा through सप्तमी one cell at a time (ex001–ex013). Here is the WHOLE a-stem masculine paradigm of देव in one place — the reference table the readings were building toward. Read down each column for a number (sg · dual · pl), across each row for a case. Note the economies Pāṇini builds in: the dual collapses three oblique cases into देवाभ्याम् and two more into देवयोः; the plural shares देवेभ्यः for dative and ablative. Every other a-stem masculine — नर, राम, बाल, पुत्र, अश्व — declines exactly thus; learn देव and you hold them all. Each cell names the sūtra that shapes its ending, so the table doubles as an index into the अङ्ग-operations of adhyāyas 6–7.

sequence.translation: Let him go to the village. / He must go.
sequence.teaches: लोट् — the imperative, for a command

notes.role: लोट् च — for an injunction (विधि), the लोट् is used

sequence.vyakhya: विध्यादौ लोट्। गच्छति कथनम्, गच्छतु आज्ञा।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Where गच्छति merely reports "he goes," the लोट् commands: गच्छतु, "let him go / he must go." The verb stops describing and starts directing. The same root, a mood instead of a tense.

sequence.translation: He should go to the village. / He might go.
sequence.teaches: विधिलिङ् — the optative, for what ought to be or might be

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — for injunction, invitation, wish, request, the लिङ् is used

sequence.vyakhya: विधौ लिङ्। गच्छतु निश्चिता आज्ञा, गच्छेत् विधिः सम्भावना च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The विधिलिङ् softens command into propriety and possibility: गच्छेत्, "he should go," or "he might go." Beside the blunt लोट् (गच्छतु, "go!"), the लिङ् carries ought, may, would — the mood of advice and supposition. Tense says when; mood says how the speaker stands toward the act.

sequence.translation: He should do (it). / Let him do (it).
sequence.teaches: विधिलिङ् — the optative, for what ought or may happen

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रण… लिङ् → लिङ् in commanding/advising/permitting → कुर्यात्

sequence.vyakhya: विध्यादिषु लिङ्। कर्तव्यम् इति अर्थे — कुर्यात्। तदेव कृ-धातुः, विधिलिङि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The optative (विधिलिङ्, 3.3.161) is the mood of *should* — duty, advice, permission, rule (विधि, निमन्त्रण, आमन्त्रण…). सः कुर्यात् "he should do / let him do." It is the mood in which Pāṇini's own rules are framed ("X should happen"). √कृ: करोति "does" (fact), कुर्यात् "should do" (norm). Tense says when; mood says how the speaker stands toward the act.

sequence.sentence: सः कुर्यात् इति आशीः। क्रियात् सः।
sequence.translation: May he do (it) — the blessing form kriyāt.
sequence.teaches: आशीर्लिङ् — the benedictive, a distinct लिङ् for blessings

notes.en: benedictive — the लिङ् used specifically for a blessing (आशीस्)

notes.role: आशिषि लिङ्लोटौ → for a blessing, लिङ् (or लोट्) is used
लिङाशिषि → this लिङ् is the आशीर्लिङ् (distinct from the विधिलिङ्) → क्रियात्

sequence.vyakhya: आशिषि लिङ् — आशीर्लिङ्। "भूयात्", "क्रियात्" इति आशीर्वादरूपाणि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A blessing has its own mood. For an आशीस् (benediction, "may you…") the लिङ् is used (3.3.173), and this benedictive लिङ् is formally distinct from the optative (3.4.116) — क्रियात् "may he do," भूयात् "may (he) be / may it prosper." So √कृ has two लिङ् forms: कुर्यात् "should do" (विधिलिङ्, the norm) vs क्रियात् "may he do" (आशीर्लिङ्, the blessing). The same mood-letter ल् branches by intent.

sequence.translation: The father comes home.
sequence.teaches: an ऋ-stem nominative: पिता (the ऋ → आ in the nom.sg)

notes.role: ऋदुशनस्… — an ऋ-stem in the nom.sg lengthens to आ; पितृ + सु → पिता

sequence.vyakhya: ऋकारान्तस्य सौ आकारः। पितृ → पिता।
sequence.vyakhya_en: An ऋ-stem — the class of kinship words (पितृ, मातृ, भ्रातृ) and agent-nouns (कर्तृ "doer") — shows आ in the nominative singular: पितृ → पिता, "the father." Where नर gave नरः and अग्नि gave अग्निः, the ऋ-stem ends in a bare long आ.

sequence.translation: He sees the father.
sequence.teaches: the ऋ-stem strong stem पितर् — ऋ takes गुण (अर्) in the strong cases

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → the object पितृ takes द्वितीया
ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — the ऋ-stem takes गुण (अर्) in the strong cases; पितृ → पितर्

notes.text: पितर् + अम् → पितरम्

sequence.vyakhya: सर्वनामस्थाने ऋतः गुणः। पितृ → पितर् → पितरम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: In the strong cases the ऋ rises to its गुण grade अर्: पितृ → पितर्, giving पितरम् for the accusative. This is the same गुण principle as the इ-stem's अग्नये — इ→ए there, ऋ→अर् here. One rule of strengthening, each vowel-class to its own grade.

sequence.translation: The man (who has) gone to the village.
sequence.teaches: क्त — the past participle (निष्ठा); a root made into an adjective

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → ग्रामम् (→ ग्रामं before ग)

notes.en: a कृत्-formed word — a participle built from a root

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त (and क्तवतु) after a root for past sense → गम् + त → गतः

sequence.vyakhya: भूते निष्ठा — क्तप्रत्ययः। गम् + क्त → गतः। धातुः विशेषणं जातम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The first कृदन्त: the past participle. The निष्ठा affixes — क्त and क्तवतु (3.2.102) — attach to a root to give a past adjective. गम् + क्त → गतः "gone." It then declines like any अ-stem and agrees with its noun: ग्रामं गतः नरः "the man gone to the village." A root has become an adjective — this is what कृत् affixes do, and the whole chapter is their varieties.

sequence.translation: The rice was made by the man.
sequence.teaches: क्त as a PASSIVE past participle — agent in तृतीया (the कर्मणि construction)

notes.en: agent — but in the passive, expressed by तृतीया

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → the agent of a passive takes तृतीया → नरेण (with णत्व, 8.4.1)

notes.en: the object — but the grammatical subject of the passive participle
agrees with ओदनः (the patient), not the agent

sequence.vyakhya: क्तप्रत्ययः कर्मणि — कर्ता तृतीयायाम्, कर्म प्रथमायाम्। नरेण ओदनः कृतः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The क्त participle is usually PASSIVE: it agrees with the patient, and the agent stands in the instrumental (2.3.18) — exactly the कर्मणि (passive) construction. नरेण ओदनः कृतः = "by the man the rice (was) made." This is the everyday Sanskrit past: not a finite verb but a participle + agent-in-तृतीया. (Note रामेण-style णत्व in नरेण.)

source.curated: our simple Sanskrit telling the well-known episode; NOT the verbatim text

sequence.sentence: गोकुले कृष्णः नाम बालः वसति। यशोदा तस्य माता। सः गोपानां गृहेषु क्रीडति। सर्वे गोपाः तं बालं पश्यन्ति, सर्वाः गोप्यः च तं कामयन्ते।
sequence.translation: In Gokula lives a boy named Kṛṣṇa. Yaśodā is his mother. He plays in the houses of the cowherds. All the cowherds see the boy, and all the cowherd-women love him.
sequence.teaches: first STORY reading — connected prose reusing known grammar (loc., gen.pl, सः/तम्, present pl.); introduces the cast

notes.en: locus — where the story is set

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → सप्तमी for the locus → गोकुले

notes.en: agent — our hero (an a-stem masc., declined like देव)
"by name" — in apposition (कृष्णः नाम बालः = a boy named Kṛṣṇa)
locative plural (neuter a-stem → एषु, as देवेषु)
agent (ī-stem fem. nom. plural, as नद्यः)

sequence.vyakhya: कथायाः आरम्भः। गोकुलम् अधिकरणम्, कृष्णः कर्ता, यशोदा माता। ज्ञातमेव व्याकरणम् — केवलं कथा नूतना।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Your first connected story — and almost every form is grammar you already hold: a locative setting (गोकुले), genitive plurals (गोपानाम्), the सः/तस्य/तं pronoun, present verbs singular and plural. Nothing new to learn — that is the point. Meet the cast: कृष्णः the boy, यशोदा his mother, the गोपाः (cowherds) and गोप्यः (gopīs). They return in every episode, so their forms grow familiar. From here the sentences lengthen.

sequence.translation: He goes to the village.
sequence.teaches: the pronoun तद् — सर्वनाम class; nom.sg masc सः

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — सर्व, तद्, यद्… are the सर्वनाम (pronouns)
त्यदादीनामः — तद् takes अ before the ending (त् + अ + स् → सः, nom.sg masc)

sequence.vyakhya: तच्छब्दः सर्वनाम। पुंसि प्रथमैकवचने सः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: तद् is a सर्वनाम (pronoun) — its own declension-class. In the masculine nominative singular it is सः, "he / that one." You have met अहम् (I) and त्वम् (you); तद् supplies the third person, and stands in for any masculine noun.

sequence.translation: The man gives fruit to him.
sequence.teaches: the सर्वनाम special dative — स्मै, giving तस्मै (not the noun -आय)

notes.role: सर्वनाम्नः स्मै — an अ-stem pronoun's dative ending becomes स्मै; तद् + स्मै → तस्मै

sequence.vyakhya: सर्वनाम्नः ङेः स्मै। बालाय इति नाम, तस्मै इति सर्वनाम।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Where the noun बाल took -आय (बालाय, ex005), the pronoun takes a special dative -स्मै: तस्मै, "to him." This स्मै marks the सर्वनाम class — the pronouns decline by their own rules, and तस्मै/यस्मै/कस्मै all share it.

sequence.translation: Who studies, he knows. (He who studies, knows.)
sequence.teaches: relative–correlative यः … सः — the core Sanskrit clause-linker

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — यद् is a सर्वनाम; declines like तद् (यः, यस्मै…)

notes.text: the correlative answering यः

sequence.vyakhya: यः इति सम्बन्धः, सः इति प्रतिसम्बन्धः। यत्-तद्-नित्यसम्बन्धः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit links clauses with a relative–correlative pair: यः ("who") in the first clause is answered by सः ("he") in the second — "who studies, he knows." यद् and तद् decline alike and travel together; this यः … सः frame is how Sanskrit builds the relative clauses that pervade real prose.

sequence.translation: The man, (while) going, sees.
sequence.teaches: शतृ — the present active participle (replaces लट्)

notes.en: the शतृ affix — present active participle, replacing लट्

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ → शतृ/शानच् replace लट् for a participle → गच्छत् → गच्छन्
तौ सत् → these two are termed सत् (the "present-participle" साधन)
उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थाने → the त-stem inserts नुम् before strong endings → गच्छन्

sequence.vyakhya: लटः स्थाने शतृ — वर्तमाने कर्तरि। गच्छत् → गच्छन् नुमा। "गच्छन् पश्यति" = गच्छन् सन् पश्यति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The present participle: शतृ (active) replaces the present लट् (3.2.124) when the form is a participle agreeing with the agent — गम् → गच्छत्, which surfaces as गच्छन् (नुम्-insertion before strong endings, 7.1.70). "गच्छन् नरः पश्यति" = "the man, going, sees" = "while he goes, he sees." It is a त्-stem consonant participle, declining राजन्-style (strong/weak). The middle counterpart is शानच् (यजमानः "sacrificing").

sequence.translation: She goes to the river.
sequence.teaches: तद् in the feminine — nom.sg सा (contrast masc सः)

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — तद् is a सर्वनाम
त्यदादीनामः — तद् takes अ for its final (the base ता- in the feminine)
अजाद्यतष्टाप् — an a-stem feminine takes टाप् (आ); तद् → ता
हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्… — the nom.sg सु drops after the long आ-stem → सा

sequence.vyakhya: तच्छब्दः सर्वनाम। स्त्रियां टापा ता, सुलोपे सा।
sequence.vyakhya_en: You met सः, the masculine "he" (ex045). Its feminine is सा. तद् takes the अ-base (7.2.102), then the feminine टाप् (आ, 4.1.4) gives ता-; the nominative सु drops after this long आ-stem (6.1.68), leaving सा. One pronoun तद्, two genders — सः and सा.

sequence.translation: I go to the village.
sequence.teaches: अस्मद् "I" nom.sg = अहम् — the suppletive nominative

notes.en: pronoun — अस्मद् ("I/we") is of the सर्व-class

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — अस्मद् is a सर्वनाम
त्वाहौ सौ — before सु (nom.sg) अस्म् → अह; अस्मद् → अह + म् → अहम्

notes.text: so अहम् is suppletive — built on अह-, not the मद्/अस्म् stem of the oblique (मम, मया, मयि)

sequence.vyakhya: अस्मच्छब्दः सर्वनाम। सौ परे अस्म् इत्यस्य अह इत्यादेशः — अहम्। मम मया मयि इति तु मद्-रूपम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: अस्मद् ("I/we") has the irregular nominative singular अहम्. By त्वाहौ सौ (7.2.94), before the nom.sg ending सु the portion अस्म् is replaced by अह — अस्मद् → अहम्. This is suppletion: अहम् is built on a stem found nowhere else, while every oblique case of "I" uses the मद्/अस्म् material — मम, मया, मयि.

sequence.translation: The man wishes to go to the village.
sequence.teaches: तुमुन् — the infinitive ("to do"), for a purposed action

notes.en: the तुमुन् affix — "to ___", an indeclinable verbal goal

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् → तुमुन् for the purposed action → गम् + तुम् → गन्तुम्

sequence.vyakhya: क्रियार्थायां क्रियायां तुमुन् — गन्तुम्। अव्ययम्, इच्छाद्यपेक्षम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The infinitive is तुमुन् (3.3.10): "to go" = गन्तुम्, "to do" = कर्तुम्, "to see" = द्रष्टुम्. It names the action one *aims at* — so it pairs with verbs of wishing, being able, beginning: गन्तुम् इच्छति "wishes to go," गन्तुं शक्नोति "can go." Unlike क्त and शतृ, तुमुन् is indeclinable (an अव्यय) — it never changes form.

sequence.translation: Having gone to the village, the man eats rice.
sequence.teaches: क्त्वा — the gerund: the EARLIER of two acts by one agent

notes.en: the क्त्वा affix — the prior action, same agent

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले → क्त्वा after the verb of the EARLIER act, one shared agent → गत्वा
क्त्वातोसुन्कसुनः → a क्त्वा-form is an अव्यय (indeclinable)

sequence.vyakhya: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा — गत्वा खादति = गत्वा पश्चात् खादति। एकः कर्ता, द्वे क्रिये।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The gerund (क्त्वा, the "absolutive") chains two acts of ONE agent, marking the EARLIER (3.4.21): गत्वा … खादति = "having gone … (he) eats." First go, then eat — one man, two actions, the क्त्वा-form taking the first. It is indeclinable (1.1.40). When a prefix is present it becomes ल्यप् instead (आगत्य "having come"), but the meaning — "having ___, then ___" — is the same. This is how Sanskrit strings narrative: a row of gerunds ending in one finite verb.

source.curated: our graded prose telling the famous butter-theft; not the verbatim text

sequence.sentence: यशोदा गृहे नवनीतम् रक्षति। किन्तु कृष्णः नवनीतम् इच्छति। सः शनैः गृहम् प्रविशति, उच्चैः च नवनीतम् चोरयति। ततः सः मित्रेभ्यः तत् नवनीतम् यच्छति, स्वयम् च खादति। यशोदा तं पश्यति, क्रुध्यति च।
sequence.translation: Yaśodā keeps butter in the house. But Kṛṣṇa wants the butter. He quietly enters the house and steals the butter from up high. Then he gives that butter to his friends and eats it himself. Yaśodā sees him and grows angry.
sequence.teaches: a real SCENE — adversative किन्तु/ततः, adverbs (शनैः, उच्चैः, स्वयम्), सम्प्रदान (मित्रेभ्यः), clauses joined

notes.en: object — the prize of the whole episode (neuter a-stem)
adverb — "aloft" (the butter hung high; Kṛṣṇa reaches it)
recipients — to whom he gives the butter

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → मित्रेभ्यः (dat. pl., as देवेभ्यः)

sequence.vyakhya: दृश्यं विस्तृतम् — किन्तु, ततः, च इति योजकैः वाक्यानि सम्बद्धानि। नवनीतम् कर्म, मित्रेभ्यः सम्प्रदानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Now a whole scene, not a single fact. Sentences link by connectives — किन्तु ("but," turning Yaśodā's guarding into Kṛṣṇa's wanting), ततः ("then"), च ("and") — so the action flows. The new pieces are small and natural: adverbs (शनैः "quietly," उच्चैः "high up," स्वयम् "himself") and a chain of present verbs (इच्छति, प्रविशति, चोरयति, यच्छति, खादति). The case-roles are all known — नवनीतम् the object, मित्रेभ्यः the dative of recipient. You are reading a story now.

sequence.translation: The teacher tells the lesson.
sequence.teaches: a उ-stem masculine: nom गुरुः (parallel to अग्निः)

notes.text: गुरु + सु → गुरुः, just as अग्नि + सु → अग्निः

sequence.vyakhya: उकारान्तं पुंलिङ्गम् गुरुशब्दः। प्रथमायाम् गुरुः, यथा अग्निः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: गुरु ends in उ, as अग्नि ends in इ — and they decline alike. The nominative singular is गुरुः, formed exactly as अग्निः was. The उ-stem differs from the इ-stem only in which vowel it carries, not in how it behaves.

sequence.translation: He gives fruit to the teacher.
sequence.teaches: the उ-stem dative गुरवे — उ takes गुण (उ → ओ → अव्) by the SAME rule as अग्नये

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → the recipient गुरु takes चतुर्थी

notes.en: the grade ओ (उ → ओ, written अव् before the vowel)

notes.role: घेर्ङिति — the SAME rule that gave अग्नये; before a ङित् ending the उ-stem takes गुण; गुरु + ए → गुरवे

sequence.vyakhya: घेः ङिति गुणः — इकारे एकारः, उकारे ओकारः। अग्नये, गुरवे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The one rule घेर्ङिति strengthens both classes before the dative: इ → ए gave अग्नये; उ → ओ gives गुरवे (the ओ written as अव् before the following vowel). One principle of गुण, each vowel to its own grade — अग्नये and गुरवे are the same move on different vowels.

sequence.translation: The king goes.
sequence.teaches: न-stem राजन् — the bare पद loses its final न् → राजा

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → राजन् is the agent

notes.text: राजन् + सु; the सु drops, leaving the पद राजन्

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य → a पद-final न् drops → राजा (with lengthening, 6.4.8)
सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ → the penultimate आ-lengthening that gives राजा

sequence.vyakhya: प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य नकारस्य लोपः। राजन् → राजा। पदान्ते न् न तिष्ठति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Consonant stems behave differently from the vowel stems you have met. राजन् ("king") ends in न् — but a word-final (पद-final) न् DROPS (8.2.7), and the penultimate lengthens (6.4.8), so the nominative is राजा, not *राजन्*. The stem hides its न् whenever it stands bare at a word's end. This single न-loss shapes the whole paradigm.

sequence.translation: He sees the king.
sequence.teaches: राजन् accusative — a STRONG (सर्वनामस्थान) ending keeps न् and lengthens → राजानम्

notes.text: राजन् + अम्; अम् is a सर्वनामस्थान (strong) ending — the न् stays

notes.role: सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ → before a strong ending the penultimate lengthens → राजान् → राजानम्

sequence.vyakhya: सर्वनामस्थाने नकारः तिष्ठति, उपधा च दीर्घा। राजन् + अम् → राजानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Where the bare पद lost its न्, a *strong* ending (सर्वनामस्थान — the nom./acc. endings) keeps it and lengthens the vowel before it (6.4.8): राजन् + अम् → राजानम्. So the king is राजा when bare, राजानम् as object. The consonant stem is "strong" (full न्, long vowel) before some endings and "weak" before others — the split that defines this whole family.

sequence.translation: Going is better. / The going is preferable.
sequence.teaches: ल्युट् — the action-noun ("the ___ing"), a कृत् abstract

words.gloss: the going, the act of going

notes.en: the ल्युट् affix (→ अन) — names the action

notes.role: ल्युट् च → ल्युट् after a root for the action's name → गम् + अन → गमनम्

sequence.vyakhya: भावे ल्युट् — गमनम्। क्रियायाः नाम नपुंसकम्। घञापि भावः (यथा "यागः")।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Beyond participles, कृत् affixes also build action-NOUNS — "the going," "the doing." ल्युट् (→ अन, 3.3.115) gives गमनम् "going," दर्शनम् "seeing," a neuter अ-stem that declines like फल. The affix घञ् does the same with a different shape and grade (यज् → यागः "sacrifice," 3.3.18 भावे). So one root yields a whole family: गतः (gone), गच्छन् (going), गन्तुम् (to go), गत्वा (having gone), गमनम् (the going) — the कृदन्त system entire.

sequence.translation: a great man (विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः)
sequence.teaches: कर्मधारय — a तत्पुरुष whose members share one case (adjective + noun)

notes.text: विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः — "a man who is great"

notes.en: a तत्पुरुष of adjective + noun, both in the same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — a तत्पुरुष whose members are co-referential (same case) is कर्मधारय
विशेषणं विशेष्येण — a qualifier (महत्) combines with the qualified (पुरुष)

sequence.vyakhya: समानाधिकरणः तत्पुरुषः कर्मधारयः। महान् च असौ पुरुषः च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A कर्मधारय is a तत्पुरुष where the two members refer to the SAME thing — adjective and noun, both nominative: महान् पुरुषः → महापुरुषः, "great man." Unlike राजपुरुषः (the king's man — two different things, genitive relation), here महत् simply describes पुरुष. (महत् → महा in the compound.)

sequence.translation: the three worlds (विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः)
sequence.teaches: द्विगु — a numeral-first तत्पुरुष, denoting an aggregate

notes.text: विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः — "the aggregate of three worlds"

notes.en: a numeral-first compound, naming a counted aggregate

notes.role: संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः — a तत्पुरुष with a number (त्रि) as its first member is द्विगु

sequence.vyakhya: संख्यापूर्वः तत्पुरुषः द्विगुः। त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः त्रिलोकी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A द्विगु is a तत्पुरुष whose first member is a numeral: त्रि (three) + लोक (world) → त्रिलोकी, "the three worlds" taken as one set. It names a counted aggregate — द्वि-गु itself means "worth two cows." Same तत्पुरुष frame (second member heads), special first member: a number.

sequence.translation: The king's son.
sequence.teaches: राजन् weak/oblique — before a vowel ending the अ of अन् drops → राज्ञः

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → the relational genitive → राज्ञः

notes.text: राजन् + अस् (gen.sg); this is a भ weak base before a vowel ending

notes.role: अल्लोपोऽनः → in a भ stem the अ of अन् drops → राज्ञ् + अस् → राज्ञः

sequence.vyakhya: भसंज्ञके अनो अकारलोपः। राजन् + अस् → राज्ञः। दुर्बले अङ्गे न तिष्ठति अकारः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The third face of राजन्: before a vowel-initial weak ending (the भ base), the अ of -अन् itself drops (6.4.134), giving राज्ञ्- — so the genitive is राज्ञः "of the king." Now the full pattern stands: राजा (bare, न-loss), राजानम् (strong, full + long), राज्ञः (weak, अ-loss). One stem, three shapes, each triggered by the ending's strength — the heart of consonant declension.

sequence.translation: The mind is pure.
sequence.teaches: अस्-stem neuter मनस् — प्रथमा = द्वितीया, final स् → visarga

notes.en: neuter (an अस्-stem; nom. = acc., like फल)

notes.text: मनस् bare पद; final स् → रु → visarga before pause

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः → word-final स् → रु → मनः
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — context for neuter forms (नुम् where due); here शुद्धम् stands nom.=acc.

sequence.vyakhya: अकारान्तवत् नपुंसके प्रथमा द्वितीया च समे। मनस् → मनः, सान्तस्य रुत्वम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Another consonant family: the अस्-stems, here neuter मनस् ("mind"). Like every neuter, its nominative equals its accusative (मनः = मनः). The final स् of the bare word becomes रु → visarga (8.2.66, the same tail that gave नरः), so मनस् surfaces as मनः. The strengthening (अस् → आस् before strong endings, by 6.4.14) appears in the oblique — मनांसि "minds" — the next cell to add.

sequence.translation: The descendant of Daśaratha is "Dāśarathi" (= Rāma).
sequence.teaches: अपत्य — the patronymic; इञ् after an अ-stem, with आदिवृद्धि

notes.en: genitive — the विग्रह "of ___" that the affix replaces

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → दशरथस्य (the analysis; the तद्धित condenses it)

notes.en: the SENSE the affix carries — "descendant of"
a secondary derivative — noun made from a noun

notes.role: तस्यापत्यम् → in the sense "descendant of ___", a तद्धित affix
अत इञ् → after an अ-stem the affix is इञ् → दशरथ + इ → दाशरथि (आदिवृद्धि अ→आ)

sequence.vyakhya: तस्य अपत्यम् इति अर्थे इञ्; आदेर्वृद्धिः। दशरथ → दाशरथिः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A तद्धित attaches to a *finished* word and makes a new one. The patronymic: "descendant of X" (4.1.92) becomes a single word by adding इञ् after an अ-stem (4.1.95), with vṛddhi of the first vowel — दशरथ → दाशरथिः "son of Daśaratha." The genitive phrase दशरथस्य अपत्यम् collapses into one derived noun. (Other bases take अण् → गार्ग्यः, यञ् → for गोत्र lines.)

sequence.translation: One born/found in Mathurā is "Māthura."
sequence.teaches: तत्र भवः — "born in / belonging to a place", with आदिवृद्धि

notes.en: locus — the सप्तमी base of the derivation

notes.role: तत्र भवः → "being in (that place)" → an affix after the locative base → माथुरः (आदिवृद्धि)

sequence.vyakhya: तत्र भवः इति अर्थे अण्; मथुरा → माथुरः। देशकालादेः भवार्थः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: "Born in / found in / belonging to a place" — तत्र भवः (4.3.53) — turns a locative phrase into one adjective: मथुरायां भवः → माथुरः "of Mathurā," with vṛddhi (मथुरा → माथुर). The same family gives "relating to X" (तस्येदम्, 4.3.120) and "good for X" (तस्मै हितम्, 5.1.5). These locative/genitive/dative taddhitas are how Sanskrit forms its everyday relational adjectives.

sequence.translation: He who has wealth is "wealthy" (dhanavān).
sequence.teaches: मतुप् — the possessive "having ___"

notes.en: "be" — the विग्रह "X is his / in him"

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् → मतुप् "it is his / in him" → धन + मतुप् → धनवत् → धनवान्
उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थाने → the मतुप् (वत्) stem inserts नुम् before strong endings → धनवान्

sequence.vyakhya: तत् अस्य अस्ति इति मतुप् — मत्वर्थः। धन + मतुप् → धनवान् (बुद्धिमान् वत्)।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The possessive: "having X / in whom X is" — मतुप् (5.2.94). धन + मतुप् → धनवान् "wealthy," बुद्धि + मतुप् → बुद्धिमान् "wise" (the affix shows as -वत्/-मत्, declining राजन्-style with नुम्). You met गुणवान् and वीरवत्तमं in real text; this is the rule behind them — the workhorse that turns any noun into "the one who has it."

sequence.translation: This one is cleverer than that.
sequence.teaches: तरप् — the comparative ("more ___ than")

notes.role: पञ्चमी विभक्ते → the term compared-from takes पञ्चमी → ततः
द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ → तरप् (तर)/ईयसुन् for comparison of two → पटु + तर → पटुतरः

sequence.vyakhya: द्वयोः विभजने तरप्; पञ्चमी विभक्ते। पटु → पटुतरः, अन्यस्मात्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Comparing TWO: तरप् → -तर (5.3.57), "more X (than the other)" — पटु → पटुतरः "cleverer." The thing surpassed stands in the ablative (पञ्चमी, 2.3.42): ततः पटुतरः "cleverer than that." The matching ईयस् (-ीयस्) is the irregular comparative (श्रेयस्, the श्रेयः you met). For surpassing ALL — the superlative — it is तमप्/इष्ठन् (5.3.55): पटुतमः "cleverest" (you saw रत्नधातमम्, वीरवत्तमम्).

sequence.translation: The state of being heavy/a-teacher is "gurutva" (heaviness / gravity).
sequence.teaches: त्व/तल् — the abstract noun ("-ness, the state of")

words.gloss: of the heavy one / of the teacher

notes.en: genitive — the base whose "-ness" is named

words.gloss: heaviness, gravity; the state of being a guru

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ → त्व (and तल् → ता) for "the state of ___" → गुरु + त्व → गुरुत्वम्

sequence.vyakhya: तस्य भावः इति त्व-तलौ। गुरुत्वम् (नपुंसकम्), गुरुता (स्त्री)। भाववाचकम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The abstract: "the state of being X" — त्व and तल् (5.1.119). गुरु → गुरुत्वम् "heaviness/gurutva" (neuter, with -त्व) or गुरुता "guru-hood" (feminine, with -ता). देव → देवत्वम्/देवता. This is Sanskrit's "-ness / -hood": take any noun or adjective, add त्व or ता, and you have named its quality as a thing. Patronymic, place-adjective, possessive, comparative, abstract — the तद्धित system's productive core.

sequence.translation: Among all the clever, this one is the cleverest.
sequence.teaches: तमप् — the superlative ("most ___ of all"); निर्धारण in सप्तमी

notes.role: यतश्च निर्धारणम् → the group one is singled out from → सप्तमी (or षष्ठी) → सर्वेषु

notes.en: the class — locative plural, parallel to सर्वेषु

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ → तमप् (तम)/इष्ठन् for surpassing all → पटु + तम → पटुतमः

sequence.vyakhya: अतिशायने तमप्; निर्धारणे सप्तमी। सर्वेषु पटुषु पटुतमः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The superlative completes the pair: तमप् → -तम (5.3.55), "most X of all" — पटु → पटुतमः "the cleverest." The group one is singled out FROM takes निर्धारण-सप्तमी (2.3.41): सर्वेषु पटुषु "among all the clever." So तर/तम are the degree-affixes — पटुतरः "cleverer (of two)," पटुतमः "cleverest (of all)" — closing the productive तद्धित set the reader needs.

source.curated: our graded prose telling the दामोदर binding; not the verbatim text

sequence.sentence: क्रुद्धा यशोदा रज्ज्वा कृष्णम् बध्नाति। किन्तु रज्जुः सर्वदा ह्रस्वा भवति। सा पुनः पुनः यतते, तथापि बालम् बन्धितुम् न शक्नोति। अन्ते कृष्णः स्वयम् एव मातुः प्रेम्णा बद्धः। तेन सः दामोदरः इति प्रसिद्धः।
sequence.translation: Angry Yaśodā binds Kṛṣṇa with a rope. But the rope is always too short. She tries again and again, yet cannot bind the boy. In the end Kṛṣṇa is bound only by his mother's love, of his own accord. By this he became famous as "Dāmodara" (bound-at-the-belly).
sequence.teaches: longest yet — past participles (क्रुद्धा, बद्धः), an infinitive (बन्धितुम्) with शक्, तृतीया of means (रज्ज्वा, प्रेम्णा), closing name-etymology

notes.en: past participle (क्त) of क्रुध्, feminine, agreeing with यशोदा
instrument — that with which she binds
means — that by which he is bound (न-stem प्रेमन् instr.)
past participle (क्त) of बन्ध् — the predicate "is bound"

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त → बद्ध; passive past participle as predicate

notes.en: possessive compound — दाम (rope) + उदर (belly) → "(he) at whose belly is the rope"

sequence.vyakhya: कथा दीर्घतरा। क्रुद्धा बद्धः इति निष्ठे, बन्धितुम् इति तुमुन्, रज्ज्वा प्रेम्णा इति करणे। अन्ते नामनिर्वचनम् — दाम उदरे यस्य सः दामोदरः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The longest reading yet, weaving together what you met as isolated cells: past participles as adjective and predicate (क्रुद्धा "angry," बद्धः "bound"), an infinitive with "can" (बन्धितुम् न शक्नोति "cannot bind"), and the instrumental of means twice (रज्ज्वा "with a rope," प्रेम्णा "by love"). It closes the way Sanskrit tales love to — a name-etymology: दाम (rope) + उदर (belly) makes the बहुव्रीहि दामोदर, "the one with a rope at his belly." The grammar is familiar; the story now carries it.

sequence.translation: The brahmin gives food; he is a giver.
sequence.teaches: तृच् forms the agent-noun दातृ → दाता "giver" from दा.

notes.en: the root दा, as finite verb

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ → तृच् on दा → दातृ → दाता (agent-noun)

sequence.vyakhya: दा-धातोः तृच्प्रत्यये दातृशब्दः सिध्यति, प्रथमैकवचने दाता इति रूपम्। यो ददाति स दाता।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.1.133 (ण्वुल्तृचौ) every root may take तृच् (the affix तृ) to name its agent. On दा "give" this yields the stem दातृ, whose nominative singular is दाता "giver". The agent-noun simply names the one who performs the verb's action — here, the one who gives.

sequence.translation: Devadatta is a habitual doer.
sequence.teaches: तृन् forms a habitual-agent noun कर्तृ → कर्ता from कृ.

notes.en: primary derivative naming the habitual agent

notes.role: तृन् on कृ → कर्तृ → कर्ता (habitual agent-noun)

sequence.vyakhya: तृन्प्रत्यये कृ-धातोः कर्तृशब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने कर्ता। यः शीलेन करोति स कर्ता उच्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.135 (तृन्) the affix तृन् (तृ) comes after a root to name one who does the action habitually or by disposition (शील). On कृ "do" it gives the stem कर्तृ, nominative singular कर्ता. Unlike a plain agent, this names a characteristic doer — one whose nature it is to act.

sequence.translation: The boy habitually goes to the village.
sequence.teaches: णिनि with an उपपद forms the habit-agent गामिन् → गामी from गम्.

notes.en: the word-in-composition (द्वितीया) standing with the affix
primary derivative naming the habitual agent (ताच्छील्य)

notes.role: णिनि on गम् with उपपद ग्रामम् → गामिन् → गामी (habit agent-noun)

sequence.vyakhya: ताच्छील्ये गम्यमाने उपपदे सति गम्-धातोः णिनिप्रत्यये गामिन्शब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने गामी। यः शीलेन ग्रामं गच्छति स ग्रामं गामी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.78 (सुप्यजातौ णिनिस्ताच्छील्ये) the affix णिनि (इन्) attaches to a root when habit (ताच्छील्य) is meant and an उपपद — a noun in composition — stands with it. With उपपद ग्रामम् and root गम् "go", this yields the stem गामिन्, nominative singular गामी. The whole phrase ग्रामं गामी names one who customarily goes to the village.

sequence.translation: The cooking (the act of cooking) is pleasing.
sequence.teaches: घञ् makes a भाव action-noun from a root; पच् → पाकः.

notes.en: the bare action itself, named as a noun

sequence.vyakhya: धातोः भावे घञ् प्रत्ययः। पच् इत्यस्मात् पाकः इति कृदन्तं नाम जायते। तत् प्रथमायां कर्तृ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.18 the affix घञ् is added to a root to name the bare action (भाव). From पच् "to cook" we get पाकः, "the act of cooking", a कृदन्त noun. Here it stands in the nominative as the subject of रोचते.

sequence.translation: He wishes for victory.
sequence.teaches: अच् makes a भाव action-noun from an इ/ई-final root; जि → जयः.

notes.en: the bare action itself, named as a noun

sequence.vyakhya: इवर्णान्तात् धातोः भावे अच् प्रत्ययः। जि इत्यस्मात् जयः इति कृदन्तम्। तत् द्वितीयायां कर्म।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.56 (एरच्) the affix अच् is added to a root ending in इ/ई to name the action (भाव). From जि "to conquer" we get जयः, "victory". Here it stands in the accusative as the object of इच्छति.

sequence.translation: He begins the going (the departure).
sequence.teaches: ल्युट् makes a neuter भाव action-noun in -अन; गम् → गमनम्.

notes.en: the bare action itself, named as a noun

notes.role: ल्युट् च → गम् → गमनम् (neuter action-noun in -अन)

sequence.vyakhya: धातोः भावे ल्युट् प्रत्ययः, तस्य अन इति आदेशः। गम् इत्यस्मात् गमनम् इति नपुंसकं कृदन्तम्। तत् द्वितीयायां कर्म।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.115 the affix ल्युट् (realized as -अन) is added to a root to name the bare action (भाव), giving a neuter noun. From गम् "to go" we get गमनम्, "going". Here it stands in the accusative as the object of आरभते.

source.curated: first quarter (पाद a) of the verse, taken whole; rest of the śloka omitted

sequence.translation: Knowledge gives humility.
sequence.teaches: first REAL sentence — uses only grammar already met (आ-stem fem, कर्मन्, present verb)

notes.text: an आ-stem feminine (formed with टाप्)

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् — feminines like विद्या take टाप् (the आ-ending); विद्या stands in प्रथमा
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → विनय is the कर्मन्

sequence.vyakhya: विद्या कर्त्री, विनयः कर्म, ददाति क्रिया — सर्वं पूर्वोक्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Your first real sentence, from the Hitopadeśa — and you can already read it. विद्या (knowledge) is the कर्तृ in प्रथमा; विनयम् (humility) is the कर्मन् in द्वितीया; ददाति (gives) is a present-tense verb. Every piece is grammar you have met on toy sentences; here it stands in real Sanskrit, unchanged.

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

sequence.sentence: पूतना राक्षसी गोकुलं आगत्य शिशुरूपेण तिष्ठति। सा कृष्णं स्तनयित्वा विषेण हन्तुम् इच्छति। किन्तु कृष्णेन सः स्तनः पीतः, विषं च पीतम्। एवम् पूतना कृष्णेन हता।
sequence.translation: The demoness Pūtanā comes to Gokula and stands there in the form of a child (i.e. a woman). She wishes to kill Kṛṣṇa by nursing him with poison. But by Kṛṣṇa the breast was suckled, and the poison too was drunk. Thus Pūtanā was slain by Kṛṣṇa.
sequence.teaches: passive construction (कर्मणि क्त — पीतः, हता, with instrumental of agent); gerund आगत्य (prior action); accusative object (कृष्णम्, विषम्)

notes.en: goal of motion — where she comes to
gerund (क्त्वा after prefix → ल्यप्) — prior action of same agent

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → ल्यप् (prefix + root → आगत्य)

words.gloss: in the form of a child

notes.en: instrumental of manner — "in the guise of"
gerund (क्त्वा) — prior action: she nurses, then wishes to kill
patient in passive — what was suckled

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त; passive sense — कर्मणि क्त
भावकर्मणोः — passive ल-affixes become आत्मनेपद; क्त signals the same कर्मणि sense

notes.en: past passive participle (क्त) of √पा — neuter agreeing with विषम्
past passive participle (क्त) of √हन्, fem. agreeing with पूतना

sequence.vyakhya: कर्मणिप्रयोगः — इह कर्ता तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्। कृष्णेन पूतना हता इति न कर्तरि, कर्मणि। दोषाः — आगत्य स्तनयित्वा इति पूर्वकालकृदन्ते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The grammar turn: for the first time the story is told in the **passive** (कर्मणि). In active voice Kṛṣṇa is the subject (कर्तृ) and takes the nominative; in passive he becomes the agent (still the doer, but now marked by तृतीया — instrumental — while the object rises to nominative). The past-passive participle क्त (निष्ठा, 3.2.102) carries this sense: पीतः (was drunk, masc.), पीतम् (neuter), हता (fem.). Two gerunds (क्त्वा / ल्यप्) chain the prior actions: Pūtanā "comes, then nurses, then wishes to kill" — each gerund hands off to the next.

source.curated: second quarter of the same verse as rd001; taken whole

sequence.translation: From humility one attains worthiness.
sequence.teaches: more of the SAME verse — adds the अपादान (पञ्चमी "from") in real text

notes.en: source — that from which one proceeds

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the starting point (humility, whence worthiness comes) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → विनयात् (→ विनयाद् before the voiced य, by जश्त्व)
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पात्रता is the कर्मन्

sequence.vyakhya: विनयात् इति अपादानम्, पात्रताम् इति कर्म। एकस्माद् गुणाद् अन्यः फलति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The verse continues: from humility (विनयाद्, अपादान/पञ्चमी) one attains worthiness (पात्रताम्, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). Note विनयात् → विनयाद् — the final त् softens to द् before the voiced य (जश्त्व, the consonant-sandhi you met). Real text, real sandhi, all grammar you hold. The chain so far: knowledge → humility → worthiness.

source.curated: third quarter; taken whole

sequence.translation: From worthiness one obtains wealth.
sequence.teaches: third link of the same chain — the अपादान→कर्मन् pattern is now a rhythm

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी → पात्रत्वात् (→ पात्रत्वाद् before the voiced ध, जश्त्व)

sequence.vyakhya: पात्रत्वाद् इति अपादानम्, धनम् इति कर्म — स एव विधिः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same shape a third time: from worthiness (पात्रत्वाद्, पञ्चमी) one obtains wealth (धनम्, द्वितीया). Once you see the अपादान→कर्मन् rhythm — "from X, attain Y" — the verse reads itself. पात्रत्वात् → पात्रत्वाद् again by जश्त्व before ध.

source.ref: Bhāgavata 10.8 — the मृत्तिकाभक्षण and mouth-universe episode
source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

sequence.sentence: एकदा कृष्णः मृत्तिकाम् अभक्षयत् इति बालाः यशोदां अवदन्। यशोदा पुत्रं पप्रच्छ — "किम् त्वं मृत्तिकाम् अखादः?" कृष्णः उवाच — "न अखादम्।" तदा यशोदा मुखं विवृणुष्व इति उक्त्वा दृष्टवती। तस्मिन् मुखे सा सर्वम् जगत् अपश्यत् — खम्, भूमिम्, देवान्, नक्षत्राणि च।
sequence.translation: Once the children told Yaśodā that Kṛṣṇa had eaten mud. Yaśodā asked her son — "Did you eat mud?" Kṛṣṇa said — "I did not eat." Then Yaśodā said "open your mouth" and looked. In that mouth she saw all the world — sky, earth, gods, and stars.
sequence.teaches: लिट् perfect (पप्रच्छ, उवाच), लङ् past (अभक्षयत्, अखादः, अखादम्, अपश्यत्), direct speech with इति, relative-demonstrative यस्मिन् / तस्मिन्, accusative-list object

notes.en: quotative — closes reported speech ("that he had eaten")
person told — indirect object of telling
interrogative pronoun — here a question marker
temporal adverb correlating with the question

notes.role: लोट् च — command takes लोट् → विवृणुष्व (2sg āt. लोट्)

notes.en: gerund (क्त्वा) — prior action of same agent

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — सर्व is a pronoun-class word
अनद्यतने लङ् → अपश्यत् (3sg लङ्, root √दृश् → √पश् in लङ्)

notes.en: item seen — in the list of what the cosmos contains

sequence.vyakhya: इह कालभेदः स्पष्टः — बालाः अवदन्, यशोदा पप्रच्छ, कृष्णः उवाच इति लिट् परोक्षे; परन्तु स्मृत्या न परोक्षं — नाटकीयतया लिट् उचितः। लङ् तु अनद्यतने — अभक्षयत्, अखादः, अखादम्, अपश्यत् इति। लोट् विवृणुष्व इति विधौ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Two tenses meet in this reading. **लिट् perfect** (परोक्षे लिट्, 3.2.115) appears where the narrator stands at a remove — पप्रच्छ "she asked," उवाच "he said" — verbs of reported or narrated speech. **लङ्** (अनद्यतन, 3.2.111) marks the events directly recalled: the eating (अभक्षयत्), Kṛṣṇa's denial (न अखादम्), and Yaśodā's vision (अपश्यत्). One **लोट् imperative** (3.3.162) lives inside the quoted command — विवृणुष्व "open (your mouth)!" The vision that follows — sky, earth, gods, stars — is the whole universe listed in a single accusative string, with one past-active participle (दृष्टवती, क्तवतु fem.) as the main predicate: "she who saw."

source.curated: fourth quarter, completing the verse; taken whole

sequence.translation: From wealth, righteousness; from that, happiness.
sequence.teaches: the closing link + elision of the repeated verb (understood आप्नोति)

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी → धनात् (→ धनाद् before voiced ध, जश्त्व)

notes.text: धर्मम् → धर्मं (final म् → anusvāra before त, the sandhi you met)

notes.en: indeclinable adverb (= "from that", standing for तस्मात्)

sequence.vyakhya: धनाद् धर्मः, धर्मात् सुखम् — क्रिया अनुवर्तते। विद्यायाः सुखपर्यन्तः क्रमः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The verse closes: from wealth, righteousness (धर्मं); from that (ततः), happiness (सुखम्). The verb आप्नोति is not repeated — it is understood, carried over (अनुवृत्ति) from the previous line, exactly as a sūtra carries words forward. You have now read a whole verse: विद्या → विनय → पात्रत्व → धन → धर्म → सुख, knowledge leading step by step to happiness.

sequence.translation: The potter makes a pot.
sequence.teaches: अण् (कर्मण्यण्) forms an agent-noun whose object stands as उपपद in one compound.

notes.en: the object कुम्भ stands in composition with the agent-noun

words.gloss: "pot" — a clay pot (object of the verb)

sequence.vyakhya: कुम्भं करोतीति कुम्भकारः। कर्मणि उपपदे कृधातोः अण्प्रत्ययः। उपपदं कर्म च समस्यते एकपदे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When an object (कर्मन्) stands as उपपद beside a root, the root takes अण् to form an agent-noun. Here कुम्भ "pot" joins कृ "make" and the affix अण् gives कुम्भकारः "pot-maker." The object does not stay a separate accusative word; it merges into a single तत्पुरुष compound with the agent-noun.

sequence.translation: The cow-giver gives a cow to the brahmin.
sequence.teaches: क (आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः) suffixes an आ-final root with an object-उपपद and no उपसर्ग.

notes.en: the object गो stands in composition with the agent-noun

notes.role: आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः → गो + दा + क → गोदः (आ-final दा, no उपसर्ग)

notes.en: dative — the one to whom the gift is given

sequence.vyakhya: गां ददातीति गोदः। आकारान्तात् दाधातोः अनुपसर्गात् कर्मण्युपपदे कप्रत्ययः। एवं धनदः जलदश्च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A root ending in long आ, with no उपसर्ग before it and an object standing as उपपद, takes क instead of अण्. Thus गो "cow" + दा "give" + क yields गोदः "cow-giver." The same pattern gives धनदः "wealth-giver" and जलदः "water-giver" (the cloud). The object गो merges with the agent-noun into one तत्पुरुष compound.

sequence.translation: The delighting son gladdens his mother.
sequence.teaches: ल्यु (→ अन) forms an agent-noun from नन्दि-group roots.

notes.en: agent-noun in अन from the नन्दि-group

sequence.vyakhya: नन्दतीति नन्दनः। नन्दिग्रहिपचादिगणे नन्दिधातोः ल्युप्रत्ययः, यस्य अनादेशः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Roots of the नन्दि-group take ल्यु, and ल्यु is replaced by अन, giving agent-nouns like नन्दनः "the delighting one, the son." Unlike अण् and क above, this ल्यु-formation needs no उपपद object to attach; the affix alone names the doer. The same rule routes ग्रहि-roots to णिनि and पच्-group roots to अच्.

source.curated: second hemistich only; the first (śatruṇā na hi sandadhyāt…, optative) omitted as harder

sequence.sentence: सुतप्तम् अपि पानीयं शमयत्य् एव पावकम्।
sequence.translation: Even well-heated water puts out fire.
sequence.teaches: first Pañcatantra line; a complete vivid maxim, all known grammar + the particle अपि

notes.en: adjective qualifying पानीयम् (agrees with it — neuter, प्रथमा)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → पानीय (water) is the agent
अतोऽम् — neuter a-stem प्रथमा → पानीयम् (→ पानीयं, anusvāra before श)
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पावक (fire) is the कर्मन्

sequence.vyakhya: पानीयं कर्तृ, पावकम् कर्म, शमयति क्रिया। अपि-शब्देन विरोधः सूच्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A complete Pañcatantra maxim, and it parses cleanly: पानीयं (water, कर्तृ/प्रथमा) शमयति (extinguishes) पावकम् (fire, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). The particle अपि ("even") + सुतप्तम् ("well-heated") carry the twist — even water that has itself been heated still quells fire. Real text, real rhetoric, grammar you hold.

sequence.sentence: कालियो नाम महासर्पः कालिन्दीनद्यां वसति स्म। तस्य विषेण जलं दूषितम् आसीत्। गावः पिबन्त्यः तत् जलम् पीत्वा मूर्च्छिताः अभवन्। तदा कृष्णः तरुम् आरुह्य नद्यां अपतत्। सः सर्पस्य फणेषु नृत्यन् तम् अदमयत्। एवम् कालियः कृष्णेन पराजितः।
sequence.translation: A great serpent named Kāliya lived in the Yamunā river. By his poison the water was polluted. The cows, while drinking, drank that water and fainted. Then Kṛṣṇa climbed a tree and fell into the river. He danced on the serpent's hoods and subdued it. Thus Kāliya was defeated by Kṛṣṇa.
sequence.teaches: लिट्-style past (वसति स्म as past habitual); passive क्त with आसीत् (past passive predicate); gerund आरुह्य + अपतत्; present participle (शतृ) पिबन्त्यः, नृत्यन् (action simultaneous with main verb); passive अदमयत् → पराजितः

notes.en: particle — with लट् makes past habitual ("used to dwell")
instrument / cause — the poison is what polluted the water
present participle (शतृ, fem. pl.) — simultaneous action "while drinking"

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ suffix on a present root → पिबन्त् (masc.), पिबन्ती (fem.)

notes.en: pronoun (तद्, neut. acc.) — refers to जलम्
object of आरुह्य — what he climbed
gerund (ल्यप् — क्त्वा after prefix आ-) — prior action

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → ल्यप् (with prefix → आरुह्य)

notes.en: locative goal (direction into which he fell)
present participle (शतृ, masc. nom. sg.) — simultaneous with main verb
past passive participle (क्त) of परा-जि — "was defeated"

sequence.vyakhya: द्वे नवीने — शतृप्रत्ययः (लटः शतृशानचौ) पिबन्त्यः नृत्यन् च; स्म-सहितः लट् भूतार्थे। कर्मणिप्रयोगः त्रिवारम् — दूषितम् आसीत्, मूर्च्छिताः अभवन्, पराजितः। जलचरे युद्धम् वर्णयितुम् क्त्वा-ल्यपौ बहुशः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Two new tools. First, **शतृ** (the active present participle — लटः शतृशानचौ, 3.2.124): पिबन्त्यः "while drinking" (fem. pl., simultaneous with अभवन्) and नृत्यन् "while dancing" (masc. sg., simultaneous with अदमयत्). The participle says the background action runs alongside the main verb — not before it (that's क्त्वा) and not after it. Second, **वसति स्म** — a present-tense verb with the particle स्म shifts into past habitual: "used to dwell." Passive क्त appears three times (दूषितम्, मूर्च्छिताः, पराजितः), anchoring the pattern from ex098. The gerunds आरुह्य → अपतत् chain the action sequence into one breath.

source.curated: first hemistich only; second (dhanur vaṃśa-viśuddho…) omitted

sequence.sentence: यस्य कस्य प्रसूतोऽपि गुणवान् पूज्यते नरः।
sequence.translation: A virtuous man, though born of whomever, is honored.
sequence.teaches: genitive relative (यस्य कस्य) + a passive verb (पूज्यते) in real text

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — यद् is a सर्वनाम (pronoun)
षष्ठी शेषे — the relational genitive → यस्य

notes.text: यस्य कस्य together = "of no matter whom"

notes.en: agent (a past participle agreeing with नरः)

notes.text: प्रसूतः → प्रसूतो before अपि (visarga sandhi)
passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग) — "is honored", as भुज्यन्ते earlier

notes.en: agent (here the grammatical subject of the passive)

sequence.vyakhya: यस्य कस्य प्रसूतः अपि — सम्बन्धः अनिश्चितः; गुणवान् नरः पूज्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The genitive pair यस्य कस्य ("of whomsoever") waives the question of birth; अपि ("even/though") concedes it; and the verse turns on पूज्यते — "is honored," a passive, the same कर्मणि form you met in नरैः फलानि भुज्यन्ते. The sense: a man of merit (गुणवान्) is honored whatever his lineage. A relative clause and a passive, working together in real Sanskrit.

sequence.translation: Wealth is to be given to the brahmin.
sequence.teaches: यत् forms a कृत्य gerundive on vowel-final roots (दा → देयम्).

words.gloss: "to be given" — fit to be given

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

sequence.vyakhya: अचो यत् इति वचनात् अजन्तात् धातोः दा इत्यस्मात् यत्प्रत्ययः। देयम् इति कृत्यम्। कर्म प्रथमायां, कर्ता तृतीयायाम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By अचो यत् (3.1.97) a root ending in a vowel takes the कृत्य affix यत्; so दा becomes देयम्, "to be given." Like every gerundive it governs case exactly as the passive does: the patient (धनम्) stands in the nominative, and an agent, if expressed, would stand in the instrumental. Here the recipient ब्राह्मणाय is in the dative (सम्प्रदान).

sequence.translation: The task is to be done by me.
sequence.teaches: ण्यत् forms a कृत्य gerundive on ऋ-final / consonant-final roots (कृ → कार्यम्).

words.gloss: "the task / to be done" — fit to be done

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

sequence.vyakhya: ऋहलोर्ण्यत् इति ऋवर्णान्तात् हलन्ताच्च धातोः ण्यत्प्रत्ययः। कृ इत्यस्मात् कार्यम्। कर्ता मया इति तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (3.1.124) a root ending in ऋ (short or long) or in a consonant takes the कृत्य affix ण्यत्; so कृ becomes कार्यम्, "to be done, a task." The construction mirrors the passive: the agent मया is in the instrumental (तृतीया, by 2.3.18) and the patient stands in the nominative.

sequence.translation: The lesson is to be read by the student.
sequence.teaches: अनीयर् (-अनीय) forms a कृत्य gerundive (पठ् → पठनीयः).

words.gloss: "to be read" — fit to be read

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

sequence.vyakhya: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः इति धातोः अनीयर्प्रत्ययः। पठ् इत्यस्मात् पठनीयम्। कर्ता शिष्येण तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः (3.1.96) a root may take तव्यत्, तव्य, or अनीयर्; here the अनीयर् variant gives पठ् → पठनीयः, "to be read." As with all कृत्य gerundives the syntax is passive-like: the agent शिष्येण stands in the instrumental (तृतीया, 2.3.18) and the patient पाठः in the nominative.

source.curated: first hemistich; the connective 'tathā ca-' tag and the rest of the verse omitted

sequence.sentence: न अग्निस् तृप्यति काष्ठानां न अपगानां महोदधिः।
sequence.translation: Fire is not sated with logs, nor the great ocean with rivers.
sequence.teaches: genitive plural (of-what one is sated) + a कर्मधारय compound (महा+उदधि) in real text

notes.text: the इ-stem अग्नि you declined (अग्निः); न+अग्निः → नाग्निः

notes.en: genitive — the thing one is sated OF

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the relational genitive; "sated of logs" takes षष्ठी

notes.en: compound — महा (great) + उदधि (ocean), adjective+noun same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — महा+उदधि is a कर्मधारय (महा+उदधि → महोदधि by सन्धि)

sequence.vyakhya: अग्निः काष्ठानां न तृप्यति, महोदधिः अपगानां न — षष्ठी तृप्तेः विषये।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Two parallel clauses: fire (अग्निः) is not sated of logs (काष्ठानां, genitive plural), the great ocean (महोदधिः, a कर्मधारय compound = महा "great" + उदधि "ocean") not of rivers. The genitive marks what one is sated *of*; the verb तृप्यति is shared across both halves. You now meet your own grammar — इ-stem, षष्ठी, कर्मधारय — in a real Pañcatantra verse.
