sequence.sentence: एकदा व्रजवासिनः इन्द्राय पूजाम् अकुर्वन्। कृष्णः अवदत् — "गोवर्धनाय पूजाम् कुरुत, न तु इन्द्राय।" जनाः तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तथा अकुर्वन्। तदा क्रुद्धः इन्द्रः मेघैः वर्षम् अप्रेरयत्। वर्षेण भयभीताः गावः च गोपाः च कृष्णम् अशरणम् अगच्छन्। कृष्णः तु गोवर्धनम् एव एकेन हस्तेन उद्धृत्य सप्त दिवसान् अधारयत्। एवम् गोवर्धनः कृष्णेन छत्रम् इव धृतः।
sequence.translation: Once the inhabitants of Vraja were performing a puja for Indra. Kṛṣṇa said — "Offer puja to Govardhana, not to Indra." The people, having heard his words, did so. Then angry Indra sent rain-clouds. Frightened by the rain, the cows and cowherds went to Kṛṣṇa as their refuge. But Kṛṣṇa alone, lifting Govardhana with one hand, held it for seven days. Thus Govardhana was held by Kṛṣṇa like an umbrella.
sequence.teaches: anīyar gerundive (implicitly: "the mountain is to-be-held"); upasarga + gerund उद्धृत्य; instrumental of cause (वर्षेण); accusative of duration (सप्त दिवसान्); simile (उपमा with इव); passive close (धृतः)

notes.role: लोट् च — command takes लोट् → कुरुत (2pl लोट्)

notes.en: object of श्रुत्वा — what they heard
past participle (क्त) of क्रुध् — attributive adjective
instrument — the clouds are the means of sending rain
cause of the fear — instrumental of cause
attribute of कृष्णम् — "(he who is) the refuge"
gerund (ल्यप् — क्त्वा after prefix उद्-) — prior action

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → ल्यप् (with prefix → उद्धृत्य)
अत्यन्तसंयोगे च — duration (unbroken extent) takes द्वितीया

sequence.vyakhya: सर्वाधिकदीर्घा कथा — एका वाक्यपरम्परा। नवीनम् — उपमा (इव); अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया (सप्त दिवसान्); एकेन हस्तेन इति करणम्; क्रुद्धः इन्द्रः इति निष्ठाविशेषणम्। लोट् कुरुत इति विधौ; लङ् बहुशः कथावर्णने।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The longest katha reading, and it earns its length: five separate clauses, each moving the story. New arrivals: **इव** (the simile particle — Govardhana held "like an umbrella," छत्रम् इव); **accusative of duration** — सप्त दिवसान् "for seven days" (अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया, 2.3.5); the **instrumental of instrument with body-part** — एकेन हस्तेन "with one hand" (2.3.18); and the **dual coordinator** गावः च गोपाः च "both cows and cowherds." The closing passive (धृतः, 3.2.102) rounds the arc: episodes ex098–ex101 all end with a कर्मणि क्त — "was killed," "she saw," "was defeated," "was held" — each one a summary judgment on what just happened.

sequence.sentence: अ॒ग्निमी॑ळे पु॒रोहि॑तं य॒ज्ञस्य॑ दे॒वमृ॒त्विजं॑। होता॑रं रत्न॒धात॑मं॥
sequence.translation: I praise Agni, the chosen priest, god, minister of the sacrifice, the invoker, lavisher of treasure.
sequence.teaches: ACCENT debuts — the svara marks (॒ anudātta, ॑ udātta-context); grammar is known (accusatives in apposition + present verb)

notes.en: accent — the marks ॒ (anudātta, low) and ॑ (udātta/svarita); the underline on अ॒ is anudātta

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → अग्निम् (the इ-stem अग्नि you declined, here accusative)
तङानावात्मनेपदम् — ईळे is आत्मनेपद (the middle voice you met in पचते)

words.gloss: the one placed in front — the chosen priest

notes.text: padapāṭha shows the compound split: पुरः-हित (saṃhitā पुरोहितम्)

words.gloss: the sacrificing priest, minister of the rite
the invoker (the priest who calls the gods)

notes.en: an ऋ-stem (होतृ, like कर्तृ) in the accusative → होतारम्

notes.text: padapāṭha split रत्न-धातम (saṃhitā रत्नधातमम्)

sequence.vyakhya: सर्वाणि कर्माणि अग्निविशेषणानि — द्वितीयायाम्। स्वराः उपरि अधश्च चिह्निताः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Your first Vedic verse, and the grammar is already yours: ईळे "I praise" governs a string of accusatives all in apposition to अग्निम् — पुरोहितम्, देवम्, ऋत्विजम्, होतारम्, रत्नधातमम् — "I praise Agni: priest, god, minister, invoker, treasure-giver." The ONE new thing is accent: the underline ॒ marks anudātta (low pitch), the stroke ॑ marks the raised/svarita pitch. Each word's accent is shown in its padapāṭha (isolated) form — पुरोहितं appears word-alone as पुरः-हितम्. Read it aloud with the pitches: this is how the Veda is chanted.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: अ॒ग्निः पूर्वे॑भि॒र्ऋषि॑भि॒रीड्यो॒ नूत॑नैरु॒त। स दे॒वाँ एह व॑क्षति॥
sequence.translation: Agni, worthy to be praised by ancient seers and by new ones too — may he bring the gods here.
sequence.teaches: second verse of the SAME hymn — अग्नि now नॉम (कर्तृ), instrumental-plural agents (the तृतीया, "by"), accent reinforced

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → Agni is now the agent (नॉम, vs अग्निम् acc in verse 1)
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → "by the ancient seers" takes तृतीया (the -भिः ending you met in नरैः)

notes.text: a gerundive (कृत्य) of ईड् "praise" — "fit to be praised"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः (he), the तद् pronoun

notes.text: a future/subjunctive sense — "he will/may bring"

sequence.vyakhya: अग्निः पूर्वैः नूतनैश्च ऋषिभिः ईड्यः; स देवान् इह आ वक्षति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same hymn's second verse, and the frame holds: अग्निः is now the कर्तृ (nominative — last verse he was अग्निम्, the object). The seers who praise him stand in the तृतीया (पूर्वेभिः, ऋषिभिः, नूतनैः — "by the ancient, by the seers, by the new"), the same instrumental "by" you met in नरैः. ईड्यः is a gerundive — "to-be-praised." Then सः (he) देवान् (the gods, acc.) आ … वक्षति — "may bring here." One word, अग्नि, you now know in two cases and with its accent.

sequence.sentence: कंसः नाम क्रूरः राजा कृष्णस्य मातुलः आसीत्। सः अचिन्तयत् — "अयम् बालः मया हन्तव्यः, अन्यथा सः माम् हनिष्यति।" तस्मात् सः अक्रूरम् गोकुलम् प्रैषयत्। अक्रूरः रथेन गत्वा कृष्णम् अवदत् — "मथुराम् आगच्छ, यतः तव दर्शनम् सर्वे इच्छन्ति।"
sequence.translation: A cruel king named Kaṃsa was Kṛṣṇa's maternal uncle. He thought — "This boy must be killed by me, otherwise he will kill me." Therefore he sent Akrūra to Gokula. Akrūra, having gone by chariot, said to Kṛṣṇa — "Come to Mathurā, for everyone desires the sight of you."
sequence.teaches: gerundive (अनीयर्/तव्य — हन्तव्यः "to-be-killed," with instrumental agent मया); future लृट् (हनिष्यति, इच्छन्ति present); causative प्रैषयत्; relative यतः-clause (reason); सम्बन्ध-षष्ठी (कृष्णस्य मातुलः, तव दर्शनम्)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → कृष्णस्य (relation beyond the कारक roles)

notes.en: patient — "the boy is to be killed"
gerundive (कृत्य) — तव्य of √हन्; "(he) who must be killed"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सर्वे (pronominal nom. pl. ए)

sequence.vyakhya: महत् नवीनम् — कृत्यप्रत्ययः। हन्तव्यः इति तव्य (तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः), अर्थे "अवश्यं हननीयः"। कृत्ये कर्ता तृतीयायाम् (मया), कर्म प्रथमायाम् (बालः) — कर्मणिवत्। लृट् हनिष्यति इति भविष्यति; यतः इति हेतौ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The big new arrival: the **gerundive** (कृत्य) — हन्तव्यः "(he) who must be killed," तव्य of √हन् (तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः, 3.1.96). It expresses necessity/obligation, and it governs case exactly like the passive: the agent goes to **instrumental** (मया "by me") and the patient to **nominative** (बालः). So "the boy is-to-be-killed by me" reads with मया … बालः … हन्तव्यः all in agreement. Against it stands the plain **future** हनिष्यति "he will kill" (लृट्, 3.3.13) — Kaṃsa weighs necessity against consequence. The reason-clause opens with यतः "because." This is the grammatical hinge from playful Gokula into the Mathurā confrontation.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.translation: Through Agni one may win wealth and growth day by day — glorious, most rich in heroes.
sequence.teaches: अग्नि now in the instrumental (अग्निना, "through/by"); the करण sense + an आम्रेडित (दिवेदिवे "day after day")

words.gloss: through Agni, by means of Agni

notes.en: instrument — that by which the gain is won

notes.role: साधकतमं करणम् — Agni is the करण (the most effective means)
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → अग्निना (the इ-stem, now तृतीया — a third case for अग्नि)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → रयिम् (an इ-stem accusative, like अग्निम्)

notes.text: a subjunctive (लेट्) sense — "may/shall win"

notes.en: object (a second thing won, alongside रयिम्)

notes.text: an आम्रेडित — the word दिवे doubled (दिवे-दिवे) to mean "day after day"

notes.en: adjective qualifying रयिम् (an अस्-stem in द्वितीया)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वीरवत्-तम (saṃhitā वीरवत्तमम्)

notes.en: superlative adjective qualifying रयिम् (a वत्-stem + तम superlative)

sequence.vyakhya: अग्निना इति करणम्, रयिं पोषं च कर्म। दिवेदिवे इति आम्रेडितम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Now अग्नि steps into a third case: अग्निना, the तृतीया — "through Agni." You have met this stem as object (अग्निम्), as agent (अग्निः), and here as instrument (अग्निना): one इ-stem across three कारकas. Through Agni one wins रयिम् (wealth) and पोषम् (growth), both accusatives, qualified by यशसं वीरवत्तमं ("glorious, hero-rich"). दिवेदिवे — दिवे doubled — is an आम्रेडित, "day after day."

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: अग्ने॒ यं य॒ज्ञम॑ध्व॒रं वि॒श्वतः॑ परि॒भूरसि॑। स इद्दे॒वेषु॑ गच्छति॥
sequence.translation: O Agni, the sacrifice, the rite which you encompass on every side — that alone goes to the gods.
sequence.teaches: a Vedic relative-correlative (यं … सः) + सम्बोधन (अग्ने, "O Agni") + a 2sg verb असि ("you are")

notes.role: सम्बोधने च — the vocative; अग्ने (a fourth use of अग्नि, now address)
सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → यद् is a सर्वनाम

notes.text: padapāṭha splits परि-भू (saṃhitā परिभूः); परि "around" + भू "be"

notes.en: 2nd person — "you are" (the मध्यम you met in गच्छसि)

sequence.vyakhya: अग्ने इति सम्बोधनम्; यं यज्ञं परिभूः असि, स इत् देवेषु गच्छति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A relative-correlative, Vedic style: यं … (यज्ञम् अध्वरं) … सः — "which sacrifice … that one." अग्ने is the सम्बोधन (vocative, "O Agni") — your fourth case-use of this one stem. असि is "you are," 2nd person (मध्यमपुरुष), matching the सम्बोधन. The sense: the rite that Agni encloses on every side (विश्वतः परिभूः) — *that one alone* (स इत्) reaches the gods (देवेषु, locative).

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

sequence.sentence: कृष्णे गच्छति सति गोप्यः अतीव अरुदन्। याः गोप्यः कृष्णम् प्रेम्णा अपश्यन्, ताः सर्वाः शोकेन मग्नाः अभवन्। रथे स्थितः कृष्णः ताः रुदतीः दृष्ट्वा अपि न न्यवर्तत। तस्य हृदये तु ताः एव सर्वदा अवसन्।
sequence.translation: When Kṛṣṇa was leaving, the gopīs wept bitterly. Those gopīs who used to look upon Kṛṣṇa with love — all of them were sunk in grief. Kṛṣṇa, seated in the chariot, though he saw them weeping, did not turn back. Yet in his heart they alone dwelt always.
sequence.teaches: locative absolute (सति-सप्तमी — कृष्णे गच्छति सति, 2.3.37); relative-correlative याः…ताः over a full clause; present participle as object (रुदतीः "weeping ones"); gerund दृष्ट्वा with concessive अपि

notes.role: यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम् → सति-सप्तमी — "when Kṛṣṇa…"

notes.en: present participle (शतृ, loc. sg.) in the absolute construction
present participle of √अस् (सत्), loc. — the marker of the सति-सप्तमी
correlative pronoun (तद्, fem. nom. pl.) — answers याः
past participle (क्त) of √स्था — "seated," attributive to कृष्णः
present participle (शतृ, fem. acc. pl.) — agreeing with ताः

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ → रुदत्; fem. रुदती, acc. pl. रुदतीः

sequence.vyakhya: अधिकरणं त्रिविधम् इह — सति-सप्तमी (कृष्णे गच्छति सति) कालार्थे; रथे हृदये इति देशाधिकरणे। याः…ताः इति वाक्यद्वये सम्बन्धः। रुदतीः इति शतृ कर्मणि (ताः रुदतीः)। दृष्ट्वा अपि इति अनुमत्यर्थे — "दृष्ट्वापि न न्यवर्तत"।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Three locatives, three jobs. The **locative absolute** (सति-सप्तमी, 2.3.37) sets the scene in time — कृष्णे गच्छति सति "Kṛṣṇa being-in-the-act-of-going," i.e. "as Kṛṣṇa was leaving": a whole subordinate clause folded into two locative words. Ordinary locatives of place follow — रथे "in the chariot," हृदये "in the heart" (2.3.36). The relative-correlative याः … ताः now spans a full clause ("those gopīs who used to look on him — they all sank in grief"). And the शतृ participle appears for the first time **as an accusative object** — ताः रुदतीः "them, the weeping ones." दृष्ट्वा अपि "even having seen" gives the concessive: he saw, yet did not turn.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: अ॒ग्निर्होता॑ क॒विक्र॑तुः स॒त्यश्चि॒त्रश्र॑वस्तमः। दे॒वो दे॒वेभि॒रा ग॑मत्॥
sequence.translation: Agni the invoker, wise in will, true, most brilliant in fame — a god, may he come with the gods.
sequence.teaches: a chain of NOMINATIVE epithets (predication, no verb) + a बहुव्रीहि-type compound + तृतीया-of-accompaniment

notes.en: epithet (in apposition to अग्निः) — an ऋ-stem nominative होता

notes.text: padapāṭha splits कवि-क्रतु (saṃhitā कविक्रतुः); कवि "sage" + क्रतु "will"

notes.en: possessive compound — "(one) whose क्रतु is that of a कवि"

notes.role: अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — a बहुव्रीहि naming an external possessor

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चित्रश्रवः-तम; चित्र "bright" + श्रवस् "fame" + तम superlative

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने → the accompanier takes तृतीया → देवेभिः ("with the gods")

notes.text: an aorist-subjunctive (लुङ्/लेट्) sense — "may he come"

sequence.vyakhya: होता कविक्रतुः सत्यः चित्रश्रवस्तमः देवः — सर्वाणि अग्निविशेषणानि प्रथमायाम्। देवेभिः इति सहार्थे तृतीया।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Verse 1 strung accusatives; this one strings NOMINATIVES. होता, कविक्रतुः, सत्यः, चित्रश्रवस्तमः, देवः — all प्रथमा, all naming अग्निः (predication, no copula needed). कविक्रतुः is a बहुव्रीहि: "(one) whose क्रतु is a sage's." Then देवेभिः is the तृतीया of accompaniment — "with the gods" — the सह-sense you met in पुत्रेण सह. आ गमत्: "may he come hither."

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: यदं॒ग दा॒शुषे॒ त्वमग्ने॑ भ॒द्रं क॑रि॒ष्यसि॑। तवेत्तत्स॒त्यमं॑गिरः॥
sequence.translation: Whatever good you will do for the worshipper, O Agni — that, indeed, is your truth, O Aṅgiras.
sequence.teaches: the सम्प्रदान (दाशुषे "for the giver", चतुर्थी) + a future verb (करिष्यसि, लृट्) in real Vedic

notes.en: relative — here introducing the whole clause

words.gloss: for the worshipper, for the giver (of offerings)

notes.en: recipient — the one for whom the good is done

notes.role: कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स सम्प्रदानम् → the worshipper is सम्प्रदान
लृट् शेषे च → future → करिष्यसि (√कृ; 2sg, "you will do")

notes.en: vocative — a second address to Agni

sequence.vyakhya: यत् भद्रं दाशुषे करिष्यसि, तत् तव सत्यम्। दाशुषे इति सम्प्रदाने चतुर्थी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A यत्…तत् sentence with two new turns. दाशुषे is the सम्प्रदान — the dative (चतुर्थी), "for the worshipper," the same "for whom" case you met in नमो देवेभ्यः. करिष्यसि is a FUTURE (लृट्), "you will do" — √कृ now in the future, 2nd person. Two vocatives frame it: अग्ने and अङ्गिरः (a name of Agni). The sense: whatever blessing you will do for the giver — *that* is your truth.

source.curated: our graded prose; the story is canonical, the sentences are ours

sequence.sentence: यः कंसः चिरम् कृष्णस्य वधम् इच्छति स्म, सः एव अधुना भयेन कम्पते। कृष्णः मथुराम् प्रविश्य रङ्गभूमौ मल्लान् अहन्। ततः सः उच्चासनात् कंसम् आकृष्य भूमौ अपातयत्। यम् राजानम् सर्वे जनाः अबिभयुः, सः कृष्णेन क्षणेन एव हतः। एवम् अधर्मस्य अन्तः, धर्मस्य च जयः अभवत्।
sequence.translation: He who for long had wished for Kṛṣṇa's death — that very one now trembles with fear. Kṛṣṇa, having entered Mathurā, killed the wrestlers in the arena. Then he dragged Kaṃsa down from his high throne and threw him to the ground. The king whom all people had feared — he was killed by Kṛṣṇa in but a moment. Thus came the end of unrighteousness, and the victory of dharma.
sequence.teaches: climax — two relative-correlatives (यः…सः on the subject, यम्…सः on the object); अपादान (भयस्य source → उच्चासनात् ablative, अबिभयुः with 5th); causative अपातयत्; षष्ठी of object with कृत् (कृष्णस्य वधम्, 2.3.65); passive close (हतः)

notes.en: object of the action-noun वधम् — "(the) killing OF Kṛṣṇa"

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति → object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → कृष्णस्य

notes.en: object of इच्छति — what Kaṃsa wished for
with लट् → past habitual — "had been wishing"
gerund (ल्यप् — क्त्वा after prefix प्र-) — prior action
causative of √पत् — "cause to fall, throw down"
object of अबिभयुः — whom they feared

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् → बिभयुः; with augment-like reduplication, 3pl perfect

sequence.vyakhya: कथायाः शिखरम् — द्वौ सम्बन्धौ यद्-तद्। कर्तरि यः…सः (यः इच्छति स्म सः कम्पते); कर्मणि यम्…सः (यं अबिभयुः सः हतः)। अपादानम् द्विधा — उच्चासनात् (departure), भयस्य हेतुः भी-धातुना अबिभयुः। वधम् इति कृत्, तत्र कर्म षष्ठ्याम् (कृष्णस्य वधम्)। अन्ते कर्मणि हतः — कथार्धम् सर्वम् कर्मणि समाप्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The climax, and it gathers everything. Two relative-correlatives frame it, one on each axis: यः … सः on the **subject** ("he who long wished Kṛṣṇa's death — that one now trembles") and यम् … सः on the **object** ("the king whom all feared — he was killed"). Two ablatives of separation: उच्चासनात् "from the high throne" (2.3.28) and the fear-source folded into अबिभयुः. The action-noun वधम् "killing" takes its object in the **genitive** — कृष्णस्य वधम् "the killing OF Kṛṣṇa" (2.3.65, the कृत्-षष्ठी). The arc that began with butter and a rope ends as it must, in the passive: हतः "was killed" — and the whole Kṛṣṇa-childhood sequence closes on its grammatical signature, the कर्मणि क्त, now carrying the weight of a death rather than a game.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: उप॑ त्वाग्ने दि॒वेदि॑वे॒ दोषा॑वस्तर्धि॒या व॒यं। नमो॒ भरं॑त॒ एम॑सि॥
sequence.translation: To you, O Agni, day by day, by night and dawn, we come in thought, bearing homage.
sequence.teaches: first-person PLURAL verb (एमसि "we come") + वयम् "we" + तृतीया-of-means (धिया "by thought")

notes.text: the आम्रेडित दिवे-दिवे (met in rd010) — "every day"
padapāṭha splits दोषा-वस्तः; दोषा "at night" + वस्तर् "at dawn"

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → धिया (तृतीया of the ई-stem धी)

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) agreeing with वयम् — "(we) bearing"

sequence.vyakhya: वयं धिया नमो भरन्तः दिवेदिवे त्वा उप आ इमसि। एमसि इति उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The worshippers speak now in their own voice: वयम् "we," and एमसि (उप…आ…इमसि) "we come" — a 1st-person PLURAL verb (उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचन), the same person you met as -मि in गच्छामि, now plural. To you (त्वा, accusative) we come, day by day (दिवेदिवे), at night and dawn (दोषावस्तः), in thought (धिया, तृतीया of means), bearing homage (नमः भरन्तः). A whole sentence of grammar you already hold.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole — the object-string of verse 7 continued. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: राजं॑तमध्व॒राणां॑ गो॒पामृ॒तस्य॒ दीदि॑विं। वर्ध॑मानं॒ स्वे दमे॑॥
sequence.translation: (To you,) ruling over the rites, the guardian of truth, the shining one, growing in your own home.
sequence.teaches: a string of accusative epithets (continuing rd014) + षष्ठी-plural (अध्वराणां "of the rites") + सप्तमी (स्वे दमे "in one’s own home")

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) in the accusative — "(you who are) ruling"

notes.en: accusative (apposed to the त्वा of verse 7)
genitive plural — that over which one rules

notes.text: a middle present participle (शानच्) in the accusative — "(you) growing"

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → स्वे (सप्तमी, agreeing with दमे)

words.gloss: in the home, in the abode

sequence.vyakhya: राजन्तं गोपां दीदिविं वर्धमानं — सर्वाणि कर्माणि (पूर्वस्या ऋचः त्वा-शब्दस्य विशेषणानि)। अध्वराणाम् ऋतस्य च षष्ठी; स्वे दमे इति सप्तमी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: This verse has no new finite verb — it continues verse 7's "to you we come," piling accusative epithets onto that त्वा: राजन्तम् (ruling), गोपाम् (guardian), दीदिविम् (shining), वर्धमानम् (growing). Two participles (राजन्तम् active, वर्धमानम् middle) decline like nouns in the accusative. The genitives अध्वराणाम् (over the rites) and ऋतस्य (of truth) mark domain; स्वे दमे — सप्तमी — locates it: "in his own home." Cases you hold, stacked into Vedic praise.

source.ref: Pañcatantra 1 — the lion and the clever rabbit (सिंहः शशकश्च)
source.curated: our graded prose; the fable is canonical, the sentences are ours

sequence.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् वने भासुरको नाम सिंहः वसति स्म। सः बलवान् आसीत्, किन्तु अतीव क्रूरः। प्रतिदिनम् सः बहून् पशून् अहन्। तेन सर्वे मृगाः भयेन कम्पन्ते स्म। ते मिलित्वा सिंहम् ऊचुः — "हे स्वामिन्, मा सर्वान् पशून् हन्। वयम् एव प्रतिदिनम् एकम् पशुम् तव आहाराय प्रेषयिष्यामः।"
sequence.translation: In a certain forest there lived a lion named Bhāsuraka. He was strong, but exceedingly cruel. Every day he killed many animals. Because of this all the beasts trembled with fear. They, having gathered, said to the lion — "O master, do not kill all the animals. We ourselves will send one animal every day for your food."
sequence.teaches: fable opening — कस्मिंश्चित् (indefinite locative), प्रोहिबिटिव mā + लङ् (मा हन्), future 1pl (प्रेषयिष्यामः), dative of purpose (आहाराय), लिट् ऊचुः; reuses gerund, instrumental of cause

notes.en: indefinite pronoun (किम् + चित्), locative — "in some / a certain"
with लट् → past — "used to dwell, lived"
pronoun (तद्, instr.) — "by that → because of this"
prohibitive particle — with लङ् (no augment) forbids the act

notes.role: लुङ् — after मा the prohibitive takes augmentless लुङ् (मा हिंसीः type)

notes.en: purpose — dative of purpose ("for the sake of food")

sequence.vyakhya: नूतनकथारम्भः — पञ्चतन्त्रात्। कस्मिंश्चित् वने इति लोकप्रसिद्धम् आख्यानारम्भपदम्। मा हन् इति प्रतिषेधे लुङ् अनद्यतनः अनागमकः। आहाराय इति तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी; प्रेषयिष्यामः इति लृट् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचने।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A new story begins — from the Pañcatantra, and it opens with the formula every Sanskrit tale is built on: कस्मिंश्चित् वने "in a certain forest" (कः + चित् = the indefinite "some"). One genuinely new construction: the **prohibitive** — मा with an augmentless past (मा … हन् "do not kill"), the standard way Sanskrit says "don't." Against it stands the animals' **future promise** — प्रेषयिष्यामः "we will send" (लृट्, 1st plural). The dative आहाराय "for food" is the dative of purpose (तादर्थ्य). All the rest — past tenses, gerund मिलित्वा, instrumental of cause भयेन — is grammar you already own, now carrying a fable instead of a god.

sequence.sentence: स नः॑ पि॒तेव॑ सू॒नवेऽग्ने॑ सूपाय॒नो भ॑व। सच॑स्वा नः स्व॒स्तये॑॥
sequence.translation: Be to us, O Agni, easy of approach, as a father to his son; abide with us for our well-being.
sequence.teaches: a simile (पिता+इव "like a father") + सम्प्रदान dative (सूनवे, नः, स्वस्तये) + imperatives (भव, सचस्व, लोट्)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पिता-इव; पिता (nom, the ऋ-stem you met) + इव "like"

notes.en: recipient — "(as a father) to a son"

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → सूनवे (an उ-stem dative, गुण → सूनवे, like अग्नये)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सु-उपायन; सु "well, easy" + उपायन "approach"

notes.en: predicate adjective of भव — "be (one) easy to approach"
imperative — "be!" (the command mood you met in गच्छतु)

notes.text: नः again — here "with us" (object/goal of सचस्व)

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → स्वस्तये (an इ-stem dative, like अग्नये)

sequence.vyakhya: पिता सूनवे इव, अग्ने नः सूपायनः भव; नः स्वस्तये सचस्व। चतुर्थ्यः बह्व्यः — सूनवे नः स्वस्तये।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with a prayer, dense with the चतुर्थी (dative): नः "for us," सूनवे "to a son," स्वस्तये "for well-being" — three datives, all the "for whom" case (सम्प्रदान). The heart is a simile: पिता इव सूनवे — "as a father (is) to a son." Two imperatives (लोट्) carry the request: भव "be!" and सचस्व "abide!" — the command mood you met in गच्छतु, here in real Vedic. With this you have read the whole first hymn of the Ṛgveda, end to end, with its accent.

sequence.sentence: वाय॒वा या॑हि दर्शते॒मे सोमा॒ अरं॑कृताः। तेषां॑ पाहि श्रु॒धी हवं॑॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu, come, beautiful one; these Soma-draughts are made ready — drink of them, hear our call.
sequence.teaches: a new hymn (वायु); the invocation pattern — सम्बोधन (वायो) answered by imperatives (आ याहि, पाहि, श्रुधि)

notes.en: vocative — direct address (उ-stem वायु → वायो, गुण, like गुरो)

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → the vocative; वायो addresses the god

words.gloss: O beautiful one, O visible one

notes.en: vocative epithet — addressing Vāyu as "fair to see"
demonstrative pronoun "this" (इदम्), nom. plural agreeing with सोमाः

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → इदम् is a सर्वनाम

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अरम्-कृत; अरम् "enough, fitly" + कृत "made"

sequence.vyakhya: वायो इति सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि पाहि श्रुधि इति लोडर्थाः। सोमाः कर्तारः, तेषां पाहि — षष्ठ्यर्थे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new god — but the grammar is the invocation pattern you just met closing hymn 1. वायो is the सम्बोधन (vocative of the उ-stem वायु, गुण → वायो like गुरो), and it is answered by a volley of imperatives (लोट्): आ याहि "come!", पाहि "drink!", श्रुधि "hear!". The Somas (सोमाः, nominative plural) stand ready (अरंकृताः); drink *of them* — तेषाम्, a genitive (षष्ठी) in the partitive sense — and hear the call (हवम्, accusative). The whole verse is address + command, the heartbeat of Vedic prayer.

source.curated: our graded prose; the fable is canonical, the sentences are ours

sequence.sentence: एकदा शशकस्य वारः आगच्छत्। सः बुद्धिमान् शशकः चिरम् विचिन्त्य एकम् उपायम् अकरोत्। सः मन्दम् मन्दम् सिंहस्य समीपम् अगच्छत्। क्रुद्धः सिंहः अपृच्छत् — "किमर्थम् त्वम् विलम्बेन आगतः?" शशकः अवदत् — "मार्गे अन्यः बलवान् सिंहः माम् अरुणत्। सः त्वाम् एव स्वामिनम् न मन्यते।" तत् श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धः सिंहः तम् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति स्म।
sequence.translation: One day the rabbit's turn came. That clever rabbit, after thinking for a long time, devised a plan. He went very slowly toward the lion. The angry lion asked — "Why have you come late?" The rabbit said — "On the road another strong lion stopped me. He does not regard you alone as master." Having heard that, the angry lion wished to see him.
sequence.teaches: longer dialogue — किमर्थम् (why?), past participle as predicate (आगतः "have come"), gerund विचिन्त्य + श्रुत्वा, accusative of person stopped (माम् अरुणत्), infinitive of purpose (द्रष्टुम्), मन्यते आत्मनेपद

notes.en: gerund (ल्यप् — after prefix वि-) — prior action
past participle (क्त) of आ-गम् as predicate — "(you are) come"

sequence.vyakhya: संवादः दीर्घतरः। किमर्थम् इति हेतुप्रश्ने; आगतः इति निष्ठा कर्तरि ("त्वम् आगतः")। माम् अरुणत् इति रुध्-धातोः सप्तमगणे लङ्। स्वामिनम् इति द्विकर्मके मन्यतेः अभिन्ननिर्देशे। द्रष्टुम् इच्छति इति तुमुन् इष्-धातुना।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The dialogue lengthens — the trick is told, not just narrated. New touches: किमर्थम् "why? for what purpose?" (the interrogative of cause); the past participle as a finite-like **predicate** — त्वम् … आगतः "you have come" (क्त standing in for "you came/are come"); and a double-accusative with मन्यते — त्वाम् स्वामिनम् न मन्यते "does not regard you AS master," the object and its predicate-complement both accusative. The infinitive द्रष्टुम् इच्छति "wishes to see" closes on the hook that will spring the trap. Everything else is consolidation: four लङ् pasts, two gerunds (विचिन्त्य, श्रुत्वा), locatives, the मतुप् adjectives बलवान्/बुद्धिमान्.

sequence.sentence: वाय॑ उ॒क्थेभि॑र्जरंते॒ त्वामच्छा॑ जरि॒तारः॑। सु॒तसो॑मा अह॒र्विदः॑॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu, the singers praise you with hymns — Soma-pressers who know the days.
sequence.teaches: the worshippers now NAMED as agents (जरितारः, ऋ-stem nom.pl) + तृतीया-of-means (उक्थेभिः "with hymns") + 3pl verb

notes.en: means — that with which they praise
indeclinable — "toward" (governs the praising directed AT Vāyu)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → जरितारः (the agents; an ऋ-stem nom. plural, like कर्तारः)

words.gloss: those who have pressed the Soma

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सुत-सोम; सुत "pressed" + सोम

notes.en: possessive compound — "(those) by whom Soma is pressed"

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अहः-विद्; अहर् "day" + विद् "knowing"

sequence.vyakhya: जरितारः कर्तारः, त्वां कर्म, उक्थेभिः इति करणम्। सुतसोमाः अहर्विदः च तेषां विशेषणे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Hymn 1 ended with "we come"; here the worshippers are NAMED — जरितारः, "the singers," the agents (कर्तृ, an ऋ-stem nominative plural like कर्तारः). They praise (जरन्ते, 3rd-person plural) you (त्वाम्, accusative) with hymns (उक्थेभिः) — the तृतीया of means, the same "with/by" you met in नरैः and धिया. Two epithets describe them: सुतसोमाः ("Soma-pressed," a बहुव्रीहि) and अहर्विदः ("day-knowers"). All grammar you hold.

sequence.sentence: वायो॒ तव॑ प्रपृंच॒ती धेना॑ जिगाति दा॒शुषे॑। उ॒रू॒ची सोम॑पीतये॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu, your nourishing stream goes to the worshipper, broad, for the Soma-drinking.
sequence.teaches: a feminine subject (धेना "stream") + षष्ठी of possession (तव "your") + दाशुषे dative + a purpose-dative (सोमपीतये)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits प्र-पृञ्चती; प्र + पृच् "fill, mingle"

notes.en: present participle (feminine, शतृ + ई) qualifying धेना
recipient — to whom the stream goes

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → दाशुषे (the dative you met in hymn 1)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सोम-पीतये; सोम + पीति "drinking"

notes.en: purpose — "for the sake of" (the dative of purpose)

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → सोमपीतये (इ-stem dative, like स्वस्तये)

sequence.vyakhya: तव धेना दाशुषे जिगाति। दाशुषे सोमपीतये च चतुर्थ्यौ — सम्प्रदाने तादर्थ्ये च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A feminine subject leads: धेना ("stream," an आ-stem feminine like विद्या), with two feminine adjectives agreeing — प्रपृञ्चती ("nourishing") and उरूची ("broad"). It is तव ("yours," genitive) and it जिगाति ("goes") दाशुषे ("to the worshipper," dative). The last word shows a second flavour of the dative: सोमपीतये — *for the purpose of* Soma-drinking. One case (चतुर्थी), two senses: "to whom" (दाशुषे) and "for what" (सोमपीतये).

sequence.sentence: इंद्र॑वायू इ॒मे सु॒ता उप॒ प्रयो॑भि॒रा ग॑तं। इंद॑वो वामु॒शंति॒ हि॥
sequence.translation: O Indra and Vāyu, these pressed (Somas) are here — come with delights; the drops long for you both.
sequence.teaches: the DUAL debuts — a dual deity (इन्द्रवायू), a dual imperative (आ गतम् "come, you two"), and वाम् "you two" (1.4.22)

notes.en: a dual द्वन्द्व compound — इन्द्र + वायु, two deities as one pair

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → the DUAL number (two → द्विवचन) → इन्द्रवायू

notes.en: demonstrative (इदम्), nom. plural agreeing with सुताः
subject — the offerings (past participle of सु "press", used as noun)

words.gloss: with delights, with offerings of joy

notes.text: padapāṭha splits प्रयः-भिः; प्रयस् "delight, dainty" (अस्-stem)

notes.en: imperative — but DUAL: "come, you two" (मध्यम द्विवचन)

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → dual ending → गतम् (addressed to the two gods)

notes.en: subject (second clause) — the bright drops (उ-stem nom. plural)
object — whom the drops long for

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → वाम् ("you two", the dual enclitic of युष्मद्)

sequence.vyakhya: इन्द्रवायू इति द्वन्द्वः द्विवचने; आ गतम् इति द्विवचनलोट्; वाम् इति द्विवचनम्। द्वौ देवौ, द्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The DUAL arrives — Sanskrit's third number, for exactly two. The pair इन्द्रवायू is a द्वन्द्व compound ("Indra and Vāyu") in the dual (द्विवचन, 1.4.22), and everything addressed to them is dual too: आ गतम् "come, *you two*" (a dual imperative), and वाम् "you two" (the dual of युष्मद्). Between, सुताः ("the pressed Somas") and इन्दवः ("the drops") are plural subjects. Singular, plural, and now dual — the वचन triad is complete, here in real Vedic.

sequence.sentence: वाय॒विंद्र॑श्च चेतथः सु॒तानां॑ वाजिनीवसू। तावा या॑त॒मुप॑ द्र॒वत्॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu and Indra, you two take note of the pressed (Somas), O rich in plenty — come, you both, swiftly.
sequence.teaches: a DUAL finite verb (चेतथः "you two perceive") + a dual epithet (वाजिनीवसू) + तौ "you two" — the dual reinforced

notes.en: vocative (here नॉम-form joined to वायो by च — "Vāyu and Indra")
genitive plural — that of which they take note

words.gloss: O you two rich in plenty

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वाजिनी-वसु; वाजिनी "abundance" + वसु "wealth"

notes.en: vocative DUAL epithet — addressing the pair
pronoun — the DUAL of तद् ("those two / you two")
imperative DUAL — "come, you two" (as आ गतम् in rd020)

sequence.vyakhya: वायुः इन्द्रश्च — द्वौ; चेतथः यातम् इति द्विवचने तिङन्ते। सर्वं द्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The dual you just met now drives the VERB. वायो and इन्द्रः, joined by च, are two — so चेतथः ("you two perceive") is a dual finite verb, तौ ("you two") is the dual pronoun, यातम् ("come, you two") the dual imperative, and वाजिनीवसू a dual vocative epithet. Everything addressed to the pair is dual. They take note सुतानाम् — "of the pressed Somas," a partitive genitive (षष्ठी). The whole verse is a drill in द्विवचन.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: वाय॒विंद्र॑श्च सुन्व॒त आ या॑त॒मुप॑ निष्कृ॒तं। म॒क्ष्वि१॒॑त्था धि॒या न॑रा॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu and Indra, come to the presser's prepared (offering), swiftly, even so, through thought, O strong ones.
sequence.teaches: a goal-of-motion (निष्कृतं, what they come UP-to) + a genitive of the presser (सुन्वतः) + dual vocative नरा

notes.text: a present participle of सु "press", used as a noun

notes.en: genitive — "of the presser" (whose offering they approach)

words.gloss: the prepared place / the readied offering

notes.text: padapāṭha splits निः-कृत; निस् + कृत "made ready"

notes.en: goal of motion — "up to the readied (offering)"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → निष्कृतम् (the goal of गति takes द्वितीया)

notes.en: means — "by thought" (the धिया you met in rd014)

words.gloss: O you two men / strong ones

notes.text: नरा = नरौ — the dual of नर, your very first noun, now in the vocative dual

sequence.vyakhya: सुन्वतः निष्कृतम् उप आ यातम् — गत्यर्थे द्वितीया। नरा इति द्विवचनसम्बोधनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The pair is called again — यातम्, "come, you two" — but now with a goal: उप … निष्कृतम्, "up to the prepared offering," where the goal of motion takes the accusative (द्वितीया, just as a destination does). सुन्वतः ("of the presser") is a genitive: whose offering it is. धिया ("by thought") is the instrumental of means you already hold. And the address नरा is नरौ — the DUAL of नर, the very first noun you ever declined, now standing in the vocative dual.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: मि॒त्रं हु॑वे पू॒तद॑क्षं॒ वरु॑णं च रि॒शाद॑सं। धियं॑ घृ॒ताचीं॒ साधं॑ता॥
sequence.translation: I call Mitra of pure discernment and Varuṇa the foe-destroyer, who make perfect the lucid thought.
sequence.teaches: a new deity-pair (Mitra & Varuṇa) as accusative objects + 1sg हुवे "I call" + a dual participle साधन्ता

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पूत-दक्ष; पूत "purified" + दक्ष "skill, discernment"

notes.en: possessive compound qualifying मित्रम् — "(he) whose दक्ष is pure"
object of साधन्ता — "(who perfect) the thought"

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) in the DUAL — "the two perfecting"

notes.en: apposed to मित्रम् + वरुणम् (the pair) — accusative dual

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → dual → साधन्ता (the two of them)

sequence.vyakhya: मित्रं वरुणं च हुवे — द्वितीयायाम्। साधन्ता इति द्विवचनं कृदन्तम्, तयोः विशेषणम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A new divine pair enters — Mitra and Varuṇa. Here they are OBJECTS: मित्रम् … वरुणम् च, accusatives, "I call (हुवे, 1st-person singular) Mitra and Varuṇa," each with its epithet (पूतदक्षम् "pure-skilled," रिशादसम् "foe-destroying"). They jointly perfect धियं घृताचीम् ("the luminous thought," accusative) — and साधन्ता, "the two who perfect," is a participle in the DUAL, agreeing with the pair. The dual now appears even on a participle.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.translation: By the Truth, O Mitra-Varuṇa, increasers of Truth, touchers of Truth — you two have won a vast will.
sequence.teaches: a dual द्वन्द्व vocative (मित्रावरुणौ) + तृतीया-of-means (ऋतेन) + a PERFECT dual verb (आशाथे)

words.gloss: by the Truth, through cosmic order

notes.en: dual द्वन्द्व compound — Mitra + Varuṇa as one pair

words.gloss: O you two who increase the Truth

notes.text: padapāṭha splits ऋत-वृध्; ऋत "Truth" + वृध् "increasing"

words.gloss: you two who touch the Truth

notes.text: padapāṭha splits ऋत-स्पृश्; ऋत + स्पृश् "touching"

words.gloss: you two have attained, have won

notes.en: perfect — "have won" (the लिट् you met in चकार)

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → DUAL perfect → आशाथे ("you two have")

sequence.vyakhya: ऋतेन इति करणम्; मित्रावरुणौ ऋतावृधौ ऋतस्पृशा — द्विवचनसम्बोधनानि; बृहन्तं क्रतुम् आशाथे — लिटि द्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Now Mitra-Varuṇa are ADDRESSED, as a single dual द्वन्द्व: मित्रावरुणौ (vocative dual), with two dual epithets, ऋतावृधौ ("Truth-increasers") and ऋतस्पृशा ("Truth-touchers"). The line opens with ऋतेन — "by the Truth," the instrumental of means. And the verb is new: आशाथे, "you two have attained" — a PERFECT (लिट्, the tense of चकार) in the DUAL. Tense, number, and compound all converge on the pair.

source.ref: RV 1.2.9 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — closes the hymn
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; final verse of the Vāyu/Mitra-Varuṇa hymn. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: क॒वी नो॑ मि॒त्रावरु॑णा तुविजा॒ता उ॑रु॒क्षया॑। दक्षं॑ दधाते अ॒पसं॑॥
sequence.translation: Two seers, Mitra and Varuṇa, of mighty birth, wide-dwelling — they hold for us a working skill.
sequence.teaches: dual NOMINATIVE epithets (कवी, तुविजाता, उरुक्षया) + a present DUAL verb दधाते + the dative नः

notes.text: कवी = the DUAL of कवि — "two seers"

notes.en: dual द्वन्द्व — here NOMINATIVE (the agents), vs vocative in rd024

notes.text: padapāṭha splits तुवि-जात; तुवि "much, mighty" + जात "born"
padapāṭha splits उरु-क्षय; उरु "wide" + क्षय "dwelling"

words.gloss: the two hold, the two establish

notes.en: "hold, place" (the दा/धा you met in ददाति)

sequence.vyakhya: कवी मित्रावरुणा तुविजाता उरुक्षया — द्विवचनप्रथमायाम्; नः दक्षम् अपसं दधाते — द्विवचनतिङन्तम्। हिमवत् सूक्तं समाप्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with the pair as SUBJECTS, all in the nominative dual: कवी ("two seers"), मित्रावरुणा (now agents, not addressed), तुविजाता ("mightily born"), उरुक्षया ("wide-dwelling"). They दधाते — "the two hold" — a present DUAL verb of √धा, the same root as ददाति "gives." For us (नः, dative) they hold दक्षम् अपसम् ("a working skill," accusative). You have now read the whole second hymn, and through it drilled the entire dual — noun, pronoun, adjective, participle, and verb across three tenses.

source.ref: RV 1.3.1 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — opens the Aśvin hymn
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; first ṛc of the Aśvins triplet. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: अश्वि॑ना॒ यज्व॑री॒रिषो॒ द्रव॑त्पाणी॒ शुभ॑स्पती। पुरु॑भुजा चन॒स्यतं॑॥
sequence.translation: O Aśvins, swift-handed lords of bliss, take pleasure in the worshipper's offerings, you of many bounties.
sequence.teaches: a NEW dual pair (the Aśvins) in the vocative + an accusative-plural object इषः + the present dual imperative चनस्यतम् ("take pleasure, you two")

notes.text: अश्विना = the dual of अश्विन् — the two horsemen-gods, addressed as a pair

notes.en: object — what they are to enjoy

notes.text: padapāṭha splits द्रवत्-पाणी; द्रवत् "rushing" + पाणि "hand"
शुभः (gen.) + पती (dual of पति) — "lords of welfare/bliss"

words.gloss: O you of many enjoyments, much-bestowing

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पुरु-भुजा; पुरु "much" + भुज "enjoying, bestowing"

notes.en: "take delight in" (denominative) — here addressed to the pair
2nd person — DUAL imperative ("you two, take pleasure")

sequence.vyakhya: अश्विना — सम्बोधने द्विवचनम्; यज्वरीः इषः — द्वितीयाबहुवचनं कर्मणि; द्रवत्पाणी शुभस्पती पुरुभुजा — सम्बोधनद्विवचनविशेषणानि; चनस्यतम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new dual pair: the अश्विन्s, the twin horsemen, addressed throughout in the dual vocative — अश्विना, द्रवत्पाणी ("swift-handed"), शुभस्पती ("lords of bliss"), पुरुभुजा ("of many bounties"). They are asked to चनस्यतम् — "take pleasure, you two" — a DUAL imperative (लोट्), the same dual-of-command you met as आ गतम् in rd020. What they enjoy is यज्वरीः इषः, "the worshipper's offerings," an accusative PLURAL object (कर्मन्). The dual you drilled across RV 1.2 now carries to a fresh pair.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; second ṛc of the Aśvins triplet. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: अश्वि॑ना॒ पुरु॑दंससा॒ नरा॒ शवी॑रया धि॒या। धिष्ण्या॒ वन॑तं॒ गिरः॑॥
sequence.translation: O Aśvins of many deeds, O heroes, with your forceful thought, attentive ones, win our songs of praise.
sequence.teaches: the instrumental धिया ("by thought," the करण met in rd014) + an accusative-plural object गिरः + नरा (= नरौ, the very first noun ever declined, now in a hymn)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पुरु-दंससा; पुरु "much" + दंसस् "deed, wondrous act"
नरा = नरौ, the DUAL of नर — the very first noun you declined, now vocative in the hymn

notes.en: instrument — "by means of thought" (the धिया you met in rd014)
object — what they are to win

sequence.vyakhya: अश्विना नरा धिष्ण्या — सम्बोधनद्विवचनम्; शवीरया धिया — तृतीयैकवचनं करणे; गिरः — द्वितीयाबहुवचनं कर्मणि; वनतम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The Aśvins again, addressed as नरा — which is नरौ, the dual of नर, the first noun this whole reader ever declined, now standing in a Vedic hymn. They are to वनतम् ("win, you two," dual imperative) the गिरः, "songs of praise" (accusative plural object). The means is शवीरया धिया, "with forceful thought" — an INSTRUMENTAL (करण, तृतीया), the same धी "thought" you met as धिया in rd014. One verse braids three threads you already hold: the dual address, the accusative object, and the instrument of means.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; third and last ṛc to the Aśvins. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: दस्रा॑ यु॒वाक॑वः सु॒ता नास॑त्या वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः। आ या॑तं रुद्रवर्तनी॥
sequence.translation: O wondrous Nāsatyas, the pressed soma-draughts are yours, the sacred grass is strewn — come, O you whose path is Rudra's.
sequence.teaches: a string of dual-nominative predicate words (युवाकवः, सुता, वृक्तबर्हिषः) + the familiar आ यातम् ("come, you two," dual imperative met in rd020)

notes.en: vocative dual — the Aśvins as "wondrous ones"

notes.text: युवाकु "directed toward you two" — derived from युवाम् (you two)

notes.en: predicate adjective of the soma — "yearning for you"

notes.text: सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press" — the pressed soma

notes.en: vocative dual — a name of the Aśvins

words.gloss: for whom the sacred grass is strewn

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वृक्त-बर्हिस्; वृक्त "twisted, strewn" + बर्हिस् "sacred grass"

notes.en: "go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — the same आ यातम् of rd020

words.gloss: O you whose path is Rudra's

notes.text: padapāṭha splits रुद्र-वर्तनी; रुद्र + वर्तनि "track, path"

sequence.vyakhya: दस्रा नासत्या रुद्रवर्तनी — सम्बोधनद्विवचनम्; युवाकवः सुताः वृक्तबर्हिषः — प्रथमायां प्रत्ययनामानि; आ यातम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्। अश्विसूक्तं समाप्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The triplet to the Aśvins closes with a NOMINATIVE string describing the offering: युवाकवः सुताः वृक्तबर्हिषः — "the pressed (soma), yearning for you, with sacred grass strewn." These are predicates: the rite is ready. The pair, addressed as दस्रा ("wondrous"), नासत्या ("truthful"), रुद्रवर्तनी ("of Rudra's path"), are bidden आ यातम् — "come, you two" — the very dual imperative you first met as आ गतम् in rd020. The Aśvin hymn is complete.

sequence.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि चित्रभानो सु॒ता इ॒मे त्वा॒यवः॑। अण्वी॑भि॒स्तना॑ पू॒तासः॑॥
sequence.translation: Come, O Indra of bright splendour — these pressed (soma-draughts) are longing for you, purified through the fine (filter), in continuous flow.
sequence.teaches: the SINGULAR turn — after the dual Aśvins, Indra is addressed one-on-one: vocative इन्द्र + the 2nd-person SINGULAR imperative आ याहि ("come!") vs the dual आ यातम् of rd028

notes.en: vocative SINGULAR — one god now addressed, not a pair
singular (contrast the dual अश्विना of rd026)
"go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — same root as the dual आ यातम्
2nd person — SINGULAR imperative ("you, come"), vs dual यातम्

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चित्र-भानो; चित्र "bright" + भानु "radiance"
सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press"
त्वायु "yearning toward you" — built on त्वा (you, acc.)

notes.en: predicate adjective of सुताः — "(the draughts) longing for you"

notes.text: पूत = क्त-participle of पू "purify"; -आसः = Vedic nom. pl.

sequence.vyakhya: इन्द्र चित्रभानो — सम्बोधने एकवचनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम् (द्विवचनयातमः प्रतियोगि); सुताः इमे त्वायवः पूतासः — प्रथमाबहुवचने कर्तृविशेषणानि; अण्वीभिः तना — तृतीया करणे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The hymn turns from the pair to a single god, and the grammar turns with it: इन्द्र is a SINGULAR vocative, and he is bidden आ याहि — "come!" — a 2nd-person SINGULAR imperative, exactly the dual आ यातम् of rd028 with one fewer. Hold the two side by side: यातम् = "come, you two," याहि = "come, you one." The soma is described in a nominative string (सुताः … त्वायवः … पूतासः, "pressed … longing for you … purified"), strained अण्वीभिः, "through the fine filter" (instrumental of means). The dual you drilled all through RV 1.2 now has its singular foil.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; fifth ṛc of RV 1.3. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि धि॒येषि॒तो विप्र॑जूतः सु॒ताव॑तः। उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि वा॒घतः॑॥
sequence.translation: Come, O Indra, urged on by the thought, hastened by the seers — up to the prayers of the soma-pressing worshipper.
sequence.teaches: the same singular आ याहि again + the preverb उप governing an accusative goal (ब्रह्माणि "the prayers") + the instrumental of agent (धिया "by the thought")

notes.en: instrument — "urged BY the thought" (the धी met in rd027)

notes.text: इषित = क्त-participle of इष् "impel" — "(you,) urged on"
padapāṭha splits विप्र-जूतः; विप्र "inspired seer" + जूत "sped, urged"

words.gloss: of the soma-presser, of him who has pressed (soma)

notes.text: सुतावत् = सुत "pressed soma" + मतुप् (वत्) "possessing"

notes.en: preverb — "toward," directing the motion to ब्रह्माणि
goal of motion — "(come) up to the prayers"

words.gloss: of the worshipper, of the reciter

sequence.vyakhya: इन्द्र — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; धिया — तृतीया करणे; इषितः विप्रजूतः — क्तान्तविशेषणे; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया कर्मणि गत्यर्थे; सुतावतः वाघतः — षष्ठी सम्बन्धे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same call — आ याहि, "come" — but now Indra is moved BY something and moves TO something. He is धिया इषितः, "urged on by the thought" (instrumental of means, the धी you met as धिया in rd027), and विप्रजूतः, "hastened by the seers." Where to? उप ब्रह्माणि वाघतः — "up to the prayers of the worshipper," where उप is a preverb steering the verb of motion onto an accusative goal (ब्रह्माणि), and वाघतः is a genitive ("of the worshipper"). Means in the instrumental, goal in the accusative, possession in the genitive — three cases you hold, in one line of the Veda.

sequence.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि॒ तूतु॑जान॒ उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि हरिवः। सु॒ते द॑धिष्व न॒श्चनः॑॥
sequence.translation: Come, O Indra, hastening, up to the prayers, O lord of the bay steeds; at the pressing take delight in us.
sequence.teaches: a LOCATIVE of occasion (सुते "at the pressing," when the soma is pressed) + a middle imperative दधिष्व ("take, for yourself") + the dative नः

notes.en: 2nd person — singular imperative (third time in the triplet)

notes.text: तूतुजान = perfect middle participle of तुज् "speed" — "(you,) hastening"

notes.en: preverb directing motion to ब्रह्माणि (as in rd030)
goal of motion — "(come) up to the prayers"

words.gloss: O lord of the bay steeds

notes.text: हरिवत् = हरि "bay horse" + मतुप् (वत्) "possessing"; here vocative हरिवः

words.gloss: at the pressing, when (the soma) is pressed

notes.text: सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press," here LOCATIVE — "at the pressed (soma)"

notes.en: "hold, place, take" — the same √धा of दधाते (rd025), here MIDDLE imperative
2nd person — singular MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative "take for yourself"
for us / in us — the enclitic नः
object — "take delight" (the चन- of चनस्यतम्, rd026, now as a noun)

sequence.vyakhya: इन्द्र हरिवः — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया गत्यर्थे; सुते — सप्तमी अधिकरणे; दधिष्व — लोटि आत्मनेपदम्; नः चनः — आत्मने ग्रहणम्। इन्द्रसूक्तत्रयं समाप्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The third and last call to Indra adds one new case: सुते, a LOCATIVE — "at the pressing," the occasion when the soma is pressed (अधिकरण, सप्तमी, by 2.3.36). The verb दधिष्व is √धा again — the root of दधाते "the two hold" in rd025 — but here a MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative, "take FOR YOURSELF," carrying delight (चनः, the noun of the very चनस्यतम् "take pleasure" that opened the hymn in rd026). The triplet to Indra is complete: three times "come," each adding a case — instrument, goal, and now occasion.
